title: Immigrant Nation: Three from Mahdi Fleifel
description: In Elefsina Notre Amour, Mahdi Fleifel films the deserted ruins of abandoned shipwrecks—and a history of exiled and abandoned refugees—in Elefsina’s Mediterranean waters. A Drowning Man follows a struggling refugee in Athens who faces impossible decisions to survive far from home. The latter short film foreshadows Fleifel’s moving feature To a Land Unknown, in which the Palestinian director pays tribute to the aesthetic heritage of New Hollywood (namely Midnight Cowboy) and to millions of refugees from his homeland who deal with the soul-crushing weight of displacement. Elefsina Notre Amour. 2023. Greece. Written and directed by Mahdi Fleifel. DCP. 9 min. A Drowning Man. 2017. Denmark/UK/Greece. Written and directed by Mahdi Fleifel. With Atef Alshafei, Jalal Qaniry, Thymios Koukios. DCP. In Arabic, Greek; English subtitles. 16 min. To a Land Unknown. 2024. UK/France/Germany/Netherlands/Greece/Qatar/Saudi Arabia/Palestine. Directed by Mahdi Fleifel. Screenplay by Fleifel, Fyzal Boulifa, Jason McColgan. With Mahmood Bakri, Aram Sabbagh, Angeliki Papoulia, Mohammad Alsurafa, Mouataz Alshaltouh, Mohammad Ghassan, Mondher Rayahneh. DCP. In Arabic, English, Greek; English subtitles. 105 min. Program approx. 130 min.

title: Off-Circuit: The Visitor
description: 30-year-old Danielius returns to his hometown to sell his parents’ flat, but the visit lasts longer than expected. With nowhere to rush, he tries to reconnect with the people and the town that no longer feels like his. Vytautas Katkus' debut feature is a delicate study of homecoming, fatherhood, and belated farewells.

title: Leviticus
description: Two teenage boys must escape a violent entity that takes the form of the person they desire most - each other.…

title: A Free Woman
description: On the cusp of marriage, Liana becomes convinced she shouldn't live a life in service of a man. Instead, she leaves for Amalfi, where she embarks on an affair. From there she makes for Paris, but each new adventure is compromised by some kind of emotional constraint, culminating in a final act of tragedy. Vittorio Cottafavi's remarkably modern exploration of female autonomy exhibits the melodramatic finesse of Douglas Sirk with a style reminiscent of Max Ophuls. A Free Woman has been newly restored by Radiance.

title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
description: A forgotten Peter Parker lives alone as a full-time Spider-Man until mounting pressure triggers a dangerous change and a powerful new enemy emerges.

title: The Incomer
description: On an Orkney isle, siblings Isla and Sandy hunt birds and talk to mythical beings while fighting off outsiders. Their lives change when Daniel, an awkward official, arrives to relocate them.

title: The Death of Robin Hood
description: THE DEATH OF ROBIN HOOD is a darker reimagining of the classic Robin Hood tale. Set of its time, the film sees the title character grappling with his past after a life of crime and murder; a battleworn loner who finds himself gravely injured after a battle he thought would be his last. In the hands of a mysterious woman, he is offered a chance at salvation.

title: Angel's Egg
description: In an underwater city, a young girl takes care of a large egg she holds carefully in her arms. A boy with a gun arrives in search of a bird he saw in his dream. At first, it seems as if feelings of sympathy are developing between the two. Forty years after the film’s original release, Anime Limited is proud to present an all-new 4K restoration of the film, supervised by director Mamoru Oshii, in cinemas nationwide for the very first time. The film is a creative collaboration between acclaimed director Mamoru Oshii (Ghost in the Shell), who wrote and directed the feature, and revered artist Yoshitaka Amano (Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D). The film beautifully intertwines Oshii’s thematic reflections on philosophy and theology with Amano’s distinctive ink painting style, culminating in an arrestingly beautiful hand-drawn allegorical fantasy.

title: Marketa Lazarova
description: Frequently hailed as the greatest Czech film ever made, František Vláčil’s staggering medieval epic, shot in stark widescreen black and white, plunges into the blood-soaked borderlands of 13th-century Bohemia amid the uneasy transition from paganism to Christianity.

title: Donkey Skin (1970)
description: In this lovingly crafted, wildly eccentric adaptation of a classic French fairy tale, Jacques Demy casts Catherine Deneuve as a princess who must go into hiding as a scullery maid in order to fend off an unwanted marriage proposal—from her own father, the king (Jean Marais). A topsy-turvy riches-to-rags fable with songs by Michel Legrand, Donkey Skin creates a tactile fantasy world that's perched on the border between the earnest and the satiric, and features Delphine Seyrig in a delicious supporting role as a fashionable fairy godmother.

title: Closely Observed Trains
description: Our screening on Wednesday 9 September will be introduced by the close friend of Jiří Menzel: film critic, broadcaster, and lecturer…

title: Tony
description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

title: BITTER CHRISTMAS
description: Raúl is a cult filmmaker in the midst of a creative crisis. When tragedy strikes one of his closest collaborators, he draws inspiration from it to write his next film. Little by little, he imagines Elsa, a filmmaker in the midst of writing a script, whose journey begins to mirror his own. The two fi...

title: Falling Leaves
description: Iosseliani’s debut feature—winner of the FIPRESCI Award at Cannes—follows newly minted oenologists Nico and Otar, just out of winemaking school, as they head to work at an agricultural cooperative in Tbilisi, there to have their first intimate experiences of the opposite sex… as well as their introduction to the corruption bred by stifling bureaucracy and arbitrarily imposed production quotas. A stinging satire of Soviet-style economic planning and its unintended consequences smuggled within a pseudo-documentary depiction of the Georgian wine industry, and a deeply personal film about youth for the first time facing up to the full measure of adult negligence and corruption. New 4K restoration commissioned by Pastorale Productions. Part of Otar Iosseliani: Fables of Modern Life

title: Tony (15) (AD)

title: The Invite
description: A couple invites the neighbours over for cocktails, igniting an evening full of unexpected twists and turns, revealing deeply repressed emotions and unexplored sexuality.

title: Late Fame (15)
description: A forgotten postman’s poetry collection finds new admirers in a story about how the mystique of the past filters into the present.

title: SUPER NATURE
description: Filmed exclusively on the original home movie format, Super 8, SUPER NATURE  proposes a new way of seeing. A celebration of all we have and reflecting on all we have to lose, audiences are invited on a journey across 25 different countries, with people embracing both abundance and loss, to feel a se...

title: Late Fame
description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

title: Screening + Talk: Paradise (2022) / Calla Henkel and Max Pitegoff
Site&Sound 11: Service Please!
description: Site&Sound is an event series that explores the relationship between architecture and film. Each session will feature curated clips and short…

title: Leviticus
description: Teenage boys Naim and Ryan strike up an unexpected connection. But when their bond draws the attention of their community, a ritual is performed on them, releasing a violent entity. An entity that takes the form of its victim's truest desire.

title: TEACH OUR CHILDREN + INSIDE WOMEN INSIDE
description: Christine Choy & Susan Robeson TEACH OUR CHILDREN 1972, 35 min, 16mm-to-DCP This film focuses on the historic 1971 Attica prison rebellion in upstate New York. It targets the conditions that caused prisoners to take drastic steps toward securing their basic rights. The film questions the reactions of prison warden Oswald, New York governor Nelson Rockefeller, and President Nixon, as well as the death of 31 inmates and prison guards from bullets fired by the National Guard. Through on-site footage taken during and following the rebellion, and follow-up interviews with inmates, TEACH OUR CHILDREN relates a powerful message concerning prisoner’s rights and represents an important historical document. Christine Choy & Cynthia Maurizio INSIDE WOMEN INSIDE 1978, 21 min, 16mm-to-DCP This film exposes the daily humiliation regularly faced by women in U.S. prisons using firsthand accounts of inmates at the North Carolina Correctional Center for Women and the Correctional Institute for Women at Riker’s Island, New York. Provocative interviews with these women reveal the anger and frustrations of life behind bars. In spite of the realities of their oppression, their optimism and strength are insurmountable. Total running time: ca. 60 min.

title: Leviticus
description: Two teenage boys must escape a violent entity that takes the form of the person they desire most - each other.…

title: MEET THE BARBARIANS
description: The town council of Paimpont — a small village in Brittany — has unanimously voted in favor of welcoming a family of Ukrainian refugees. However, the refugees who turn up aren’t Ukrainian but Syrian, and some of the locals are not very pleased with their new neighbors. Yet the Fayad family avoids all the clichés the French villagers may have expected. So much so that, they leave one wondering: who in this little village are the true ‘barbarians’?

title: Minari
description: Minari. 2020. USA. Written and directed by Lee Isaac Chung. With Steven Yuen, Yeri Han, Yuh-Jung Youn. DCP. In English, Korean; English subtitles. 115 min. Jacob (Steven Yeun) dreams of having his own farm to introduce a prosperous bounty of Korean vegetables to American kitchens. When a plot of land and a mobile home in the Ozarks become available, Jacob promises his wife, Monica (Yeri Han) and their two children (Alan Kim, Noel Cho) that a move from San Francisco is worth it. The family’s adjustment to their new life is upended by the sudden arrival of Monica’s mother, the eccentric grandma Soonja (Yuh-Jung Youn). Anchored by stellar performances and Lee Isaac Chung’s soulful direction, Minari is a rare gem, a cinematic ode to family, faith, and the American dream.

title: EC: EARTH / ZEMLYA
description: A poetic expression of love for both nature and Ukrainian culture by the man who was alternatively branded a deserter by Ukrainians and a Ukrainian nationalist by Russian Soviets. Dovzhenko champions the progression of life, class struggle, and new attitudes for a town changed by a tractor and a fallen hero.

title: Onslaught
description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

title: The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert
description: Two drag queens and a transgender woman drive across the Australian outback in a tour bus named Priscilla, in this wild road comedy that earned Lizzy Gardiner and Tim Chappell Oscars for their imaginative costume designs. Terence Stamp gives an impressive change-of-pace performance as the world-weary Bernadette, and he’s matched by Hugo Weaving as the trio’s conflicted leader. Guy Pearce delivers a breakout performance as the youngest of the group. Deftly mixing campy humor and genuine emotion amidst stunning locations, Priscilla was an international success and spawned a hit stage musical.

title: THE ELEPHANT MAN
description: In one of his most legendary films, director David Lynch chronicles the intense emotional journey of a complex, lonely man and the dedicated surgeon who changed his life. John Merrick (John Hurt) was born with a horribly disfiguring congenital disease, and suffered the humiliation of being a sideshow freak. Only when London doctor Frederick Treves (Anthony Hopkins) rescues him does Merrick begin to regain the life of dignity and respect that everyone deserves. Based on a true story, the critically acclaimed, Oscar-nominated film has earned its place in cinematic history. Visually fascinating and historically relevant, Lynch has created a haunting masterpiece of compassion, beauty and ultimately, humanity.

title: Barry Lyndon
description: Stanley Kubrick bent the conventions of the historical drama to his own will in this dazzling vision of a pitiless aristocracy, adapted from a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray. In picaresque detail, Barry Lyndon chronicles the adventures of an incorrigible trickster (Ryan O’Neal) whose opportunism takes him from an Irish farm to the battlefields of the Seven Years’ War and the parlours of high society. For the most sumptuously crafted film of his career, Kubrick recreated the decadent surfaces and intricate social codes of the period, evoking the light and texture of eighteenth-century painting with the help of pioneering cinematographic techniques and lavish costume and production design, all of which earned Academy Awards. The result is a masterpiece—a sardonic, devastating portrait of a vanishing world whose opulence conceals the moral vacancy at its heart. Please Note: The film will be presented with a brief 5-10min intermission.

title: In the Mood for Love
description: Hong Kong, 1962: neighbors Chow Mo-Wan (Tony Leung Chiu-wai) and Su Li-Zhen (Maggie Cheung) suspect their spouses business trips to Japan are cover for an affair; as the truth becomes clearer, so do the feelings of Mr. Chow and Mrs. Chan. Cinematographers Christopher Doyle and Mark Lee Ping Bing bring to life — in vivid detail — an elegant pile-up of affections, memories, and illusions. A slow seduction of stolen glances; the “Quizás, Quizás, Quizás” of restrained passions prove, once again, Wong Kar Wai can wring more emotions out of a silk dress than stains at a laundromat.

title: The Night is Short, Walk on Girl
description: A surreal nocturnal animated odyssey from Yuasa, the mad genius behind Mind Game, rendered in a frenetic, galaxy-brained, endlessly morphing style. The Night is Short, Walk on Girl follows a mysterious high schooler known only as The Girl with Black Hair through the streets of Kyoto’s famed Ponto-Cho party district, drinking middle-aged salarymen under the table when she’s not mixing with barflies, obsessive collectors, and guerilla theater performers, all the while oblivious to the efforts of a fellow student who has been creating increasingly fantastic and contrived reasons to run into her in a gambit to win her love. A comic fable of fleeting youthful passions, as lived out through one mad, unforgettable night. Part of This Night Has Opened My Eyes

title: The Odyssey
description: The Odyssey (2026), Christopher Nolan’s epic adaptation of Homer’s classic, follows Greek hero Odysseus on a perilous journey home after the Trojan War, encountering gods, monsters, and treacherous seas while his family faces turmoil in Ithaca Photo Id may required for 15 certificate films

title: Reclaim The Frame Presents: Beautiful Thing
description: Join Fruits on Film and Reclaim The Frame for a special 30th anniversary screening of Beautiful Thing. This screening will have Descriptive subtitles…

title: Don't Look Back In Anger
description: “Don’t Look Back In Anger” charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s triumphant reunion tour, Oasis Live ‘25, one of the most anticipated rock ‘n’ roll comebacks of our time. The film is an unapologetically uplifting account of the biggest musical event of 2025, capturing the experience and emotions of the band and their fans across the world. The unique perspective includes rehearsal, backstage, and onstage access as well as the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in over 20 years. Alongside the band’s sold-out world tour, the film also explores the profound emotional impact of this phenomenal global cultural moment and what their music means to audiences and generations worldwide. Steven Knight says, “The Oasis world tour united generations, cultures and countries and spoke to a broken world about reconciliation. ‘Don’t Look Back In Anger’ is not only your ticket to the show – it’s a backstage pass and a seat at the table when Liam and Noel sit down together for the first time in 15 years and tell it how it is and how it was.” Featuring unprecedented access and never-before-seen footage, the film is a Magna Studios production, presented by Sony Music Vision in association with Sony Music Entertainment UK. The producers are Sam Bridger (“Lewis Capaldi: How I’m Feeling Now,” “Meet Me in the Bathroom”) and Guy Heeley (“Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man”). The executive producers include Kate Shepherd, Marisa Clifford, Davud Karbassioun, Tom Mackay, Krista Wegener, Isabel Davis, and Tim O’Shea, with Oscar®-winning sound mixers James Mather (“Top Gun: Maverick,” “Belfast”) and Tarn Willers (“The Zone of Interest”), cinematographer Haris Zambarloukos (“Belfast,” “Beetlejuice Beetlejuice”), and editors George Cragg and Martina Zamolo leading the creative technical team.

title: FROM SPIKES TO SPINDLES + FEI TIEN, GODDESS IN FLIGHT
description: Christine Choy FROM SPIKES TO SPINDLES 1976, 46 min, 16mm-to-DCP This raw, gutsy portrait of New York’s Chinatown captures the early days of an emerging consciousness in the community. We see a Chinatown rarely depicted, a vibrant community whose young and old join forces to protest police brutality and hostile real estate developers. With bold strokes, it paints an overview of the community and its history, from the early laborers driving spikes into the transcontinental railroad to the garment workers of today. Christine Choy FEI TIEN, GODDESS IN FLIGHT 1983, 26 min, 16mm-to-DCP Based on the play, “Pigeons”, by Ginny Lim, this film focuses on the meeting between an older immigrant and a younger American-born woman living in NYC’s Chinatown. The linkages in their pasts and possible futures unfold as their friendship grows. Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: Off-Circuit: UK PREMIERE Pin de Fartie + Q&A
description: The latest production from boundlessly imaginative Argentine collective El Pampero Cine sees successive pairs of characters bid farewell: a mother and her son, a caretaker and her charge, two actors endlessly rehearsing a scene that will never be performed. A playful spin on theatrical adaptation, Alejo Moguillansky's new film is a delightfully imaginative take on Samuel Beckett's Fin de Partie , punctuated by music, tennis, and another exceptional turn by Laura Paredes. The UK Premiere screening on the 4 September will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Alejo Moguillansky.

title: Sherman's March
description: Sherman’s March , winner of the Grand Jury Prize for Best Documentary at Sundance in 1987, is Ross McElwee’s monumental documentary which has been officially listed by the International Documentary Association as one of the top 20 documentary films of all time. Intending to make a film about General Sherman’s 1864 March to the Sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. Affected by a recent breakup, he slows his progress through the American South to spend time with a succession of women and explore the possibility of romantic fulfilment in the nuclear age.

title: Mystery Movie
description: Don't miss our fan favourite MYSTERY MOVIE screenings! On a near weekly basis we will serve up a random mystery movie, with No Clues and No Hints as to what they will be. In 2026, we'll be presenting these as STAFF CURATED selections each and every week by our lovely Front of House, Duty Manager, and Projection Team! You can find the schedule below: --- Wed 29th July - Aya's Pick (120 minutes) Wed 5th Aug - Chloe's Pick (91 minutes) Wed 12th Aug - Liv's Pick (92 minutes) Wed 19th Aug - Julia's Pick (82 minutes) Wed 26th Aug - Chevy's Pick (112 minutes) --- You can find a list of every MYSTERY MOVIE we have ever screened HERE ; if a film is on this list, it is not eligible for future Mystery Movie screenings! --- Content Advice : As these films are a mystery, we aren't able to provide specific ratings / guidance on the film's content. We strongly advise that you take this into consideration before purchasing a ticket.

title: Margeaux Labat presents THE WATERMELON WOMAN
description: Humorous, heartfelt and angry in equal measure, The Watermelon Woman was the first narrative feature film to be directed by an openly gay Black woman, and one of the foundational works of the New Queer Cinema. As part of our ongoing Rio Forever celebrations, we’re proud to screen it with an in-perso...

title: Pressure
description: In the tense 72 hours before D-Day, and the fate of the free world hanging in the balance, PRESSURE follows General Dwight D. Eisenhower and Captain James Stagg as they face an impossible choice—launch the largest and most dangerous invasion in history or risk losing the war altogether.

title: Bitter Christmas (15) (AD)
description: Pedro Almodóvar is back with his unique brand of storytelling, setting the stage for the tale of a filmmaker who is a little too heavily inspired by the real lives of those around him.

title: Leviticus (15) (AD)
description: Two teenage boys living in an ultraconservative community in rural Australia are threatened by a violent entity seeking to destroy them in this breath-taking queer horror.

Set of its time, the film sees the title character grappling with his past after a life of crime and murder; a battleworn loner who finds himself gravely injured after a battle he thought would be his last. In the hands of a mysterious woman, he is offered a chance at salvation.

title: TEENAGE SEX AND DEATH AT CAMP MIASMA
description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director for resurrection. But when she visits the original's star, a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, ...

title: The Dog Stars
description: Set in a post-apocalyptic world in which a virus has wiped out most of humanity, with survivors being terrorized by roaming scavengers called "Reapers." The protagonist is Hig, a pilot who survived the flu that killed everyone he knew, his wife included. He lives in the hangar of a small abandoned airport with his dog, his only neighbor a gun-toting ex-Marine. Hig sometimes heads off in his 1956 Cessna, where he can fish and pretend things are how they used to be. When a random transmission somehow beams through his radio, the voice ignites a hope deep inside him that a better life might exist if he flies a bit further. He risks it all. to chase a possible haven in Grand Junction.

title: Late Fame
description: In Kent Jones’s marvelously witty second feature, a once-upon-a-time New York poet (Willem Dafoe) gets an ego boost when he is welcomed into the world of an emerging literary salon, but must reckon with the authenticity of his newfound circle of twentysomething admirers.

title: Member Screening: El Último Sueño de Frida y Diego
description: Enjoy a performance of American composer Gabriela Lena Frank’s first opera, El Último Sueño de Frida y Diego, recorded from the stage of the Metropolitan Opera as part of the company’s award-winning Live in HD series of cinema transmissions. The screening will be preceded by an introduction from Jon Bausor, the set and co-costume designer of the opera. Featuring a libretto by Pulitzer Prize–winning playwright Nilo Cruz, this magical-realist portrait of two of Mexico’s most iconic artists follows Frida Kahlo, sung by leading mezzo-soprano Isabel Leonard, as she leaves the underworld on the Day of the Dead to reunite with Diego Rivera, portrayed by baritone Carlos Álvarez. The famously feuding pair briefly relive their tumultuous love, embracing both the passion and the pain before bidding the land of the living a final farewell. The vibrant new production, taking enthusiastic inspiration from Kahlo and Rivera’s paintings, is directed and choreographed by Deborah Colker. This event is a part of the MoMA exhibition Frida and Diego: The Last Dream, a first-of-its-kind collaboration with the Metropolitan Opera. The presentation features artworks by Kahlo and Rivera in an elaborate setting designed by Jon Bausor. For both the opera and installation, Bausor evokes the artists’ lives and artworks in his theatrical designs. Language: Spanish with English subtitles Accessibility FM assistive-listening devices (headsets and neck loops for T-coil compatibility) are available for sound amplification. American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation is available for public programs upon request with two weeks’ advance notice. MoMA will make every effort to provide accommodation for requests made with less than two weeks’ notice. Please contact members_programs@moma.org to make a request for these accommodations.

title: PINK FLAMINGOS
description: Notorious Baltimore criminal and underground figure Divine goes up against a sleazy married couple who make a passionate attempt to humiliate her and seize her tabloid-given title as “The Filthiest Person Alive.”

title: Rocky (Garrett Brown In Person)             / Bound for Glory
description: His whole life was a million-to-one shot. A Philadelphia fighter who never made the big time… he showed he could take on a challenge… and won something bigger than a championship bout. Legendarily holding onto the sale of his script until he was allowed to play the lead, Sylvester Stallone shines in his signature role as the underdog southpaw who gives it all he’s got when given the once-in-a-lifetime chance to face off against the world heavyweight champion. Talia Shire, Burt Young, Carl Weathers, and Burgess Meredith co-star.

title: Your Name [Kimi no Na wa.]
description: Two teenagers share a profound, magical connection upon discovering they are swapping bodies. Things manage to become even more complicated when the boy and girl decide to meet in person.

title: Late Fame
description: In Kent Jones’s marvelously witty second feature, a once-upon-a-time New York poet (Willem Dafoe) gets an ego boost when he is welcomed into the world of an emerging literary salon, but must reckon with the authenticity of his newfound circle of twentysomething admirers.

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
Silent Running
description: In a future where all flora are extinct on Earth, an astronaut is given orders to destroy the last of Earth's plant samples, kept in a greenhouse aboard a spacecraft.

title: Kiki's Delivery Service
description: Celebrate this beloved coming-of-age story from the legendary Studio Ghibli, creators of Spirited Away , and Academy Award®-winning director Hayao Miyazaki, about a resourceful young witch who uses her broom to create a delivery service, only to lose her gift of flight in a moment of self-doubt. It is a tradition for all young witches to leave their families on the night of a full moon and fly off into the wide world to learn their craft. When that night comes for Kiki, she embarks on her new journey with her sarcastic black cat, Jiji, landing the next morning in a seaside town, where her unique skills make her an instant sensation.

title: Onslaught
description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

title: Chronovisor
description: Inspired by the true story of a “fake” invention, Kevin Walker and Jack Auen’s Chronovisor follows a Columbia professor deep into a Borgesian labyrinth of textual clues pointing to a time-travel device rumored to have been suppressed by the Vatican.

title: Off-Circuit: The Visitor
description: 30-year-old Danielius returns to his hometown to sell his parents’ flat, but the visit lasts longer than expected. With nowhere to rush, he tries to reconnect with the people and the town that no longer feels like his. Vytautas Katkus' debut feature is a delicate study of homecoming, fatherhood, and belated farewells.

title: Solaris (1972)
description: A psychologist is sent to a station orbiting a distant planet in order to discover what has caused the crew to go insane.

title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
Sherman's March
description: Sherman’s March , winner of the Grand Jury Prize for Best Documentary at Sundance in 1987, is Ross McElwee’s monumental documentary which has been officially listed by the International Documentary Association as one of the top 20 documentary films of all time. Intending to make a film about General Sherman’s 1864 March to the Sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. Affected by a recent breakup, he slows his progress through the American South to spend time with a succession of women and explore the possibility of romantic fulfilment in the nuclear age.

description: Pedro Almodóvar is back with his unique brand of storytelling, setting the stage for the tale of a filmmaker who is a little too heavily inspired by the real lives of those around him.

title: A Free Woman
description: On the cusp of marriage, Liana becomes convinced she shouldn't live a life in service of a man. Instead, she leaves for Amalfi, where she embarks on an affair. From there she makes for Paris, but each new adventure is compromised by some kind of emotional constraint, culminating in a final act of tragedy. Vittorio Cottafavi's remarkably modern exploration of female autonomy exhibits the melodramatic finesse of Douglas Sirk with a style reminiscent of Max Ophuls. A Free Woman has been newly restored by Radiance.

title: There Once Was a Singing Blackbird
Spider-Man: Brand New Day
description: A forgotten Peter Parker lives alone as a full-time Spider-Man until mounting pressure triggers a dangerous change and a powerful new enemy emerges.

title: After Hours
description: Cheech and Chong! Sultry sculptress Linda Fiorentino! Bad Brains! These are but a few of the characters that Midtown computer jockey Paul Hackett (Griffin Dunne) will encounter when venturing into the wilds of a pre-gentrification downtown New York without a penny to his name or the means to get back home in Scorsese’s bravura black comedy of class resentment, all-pervasive paranoia, and creeping castration anxiety, in which the director can be briefly spotted manning a spotlight at punk rock dive Club Berlin. As Dick Miller’s diner waiter explains to the hapless Hackett, “Different rules apply when it gets this late…” As true of the city in 1985 as it is today. Part of This Night Has Opened My Eyes

description: The great Willem Dafoe lends his delicate gravitas to the role of Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet who works…

title: The Incomer
description: On an Orkney isle, siblings Isla and Sandy hunt birds and talk to mythical beings while fighting off outsiders. Their lives change when Daniel, an awkward official, arrives to relocate them.

title: The Death of Robin Hood
description: THE DEATH OF ROBIN HOOD is a darker reimagining of the classic Robin Hood tale. Set of its time, the film sees the title character grappling with his past after a life of crime and murder; a battleworn loner who finds himself gravely injured after a battle he thought would be his last. In the hands of a mysterious woman, he is offered a chance at salvation.

title: Bitter Christmas
description:
Presented in Spanish, with English subtitles.

From iconic director Pedro Almodóvar... A dual-timeline story exploring grief, creative block, and the blurry line between real life and fiction.

title: Marketa Lazarova
description: Frequently hailed as the greatest Czech film ever made, František Vláčil’s staggering medieval epic, shot in stark widescreen black and white, plunges into the blood-soaked borderlands of 13th-century Bohemia amid the uneasy transition from paganism to Christianity.

title: The Battle of Algiers
description: Paratrooper commander Colonel Mathieu, a former French Resistance fighter during World War II, is sent to Algeria to reinforce efforts to squelch the uprisings of the Algerian War. There he faces Ali la Pointe, a former petty criminal who, as the leader of the Algerian Front de Liberation Nationale, directs terror strategies against the colonial French government occupation. As each side resorts to ever-increasing brutality, no violent act is too unthinkable.

title: BODY DOUBLE
description:
A struggling actor recovering from a breakup and a failed career opportunity takes care of a luxurious Hollywood Hills house while its owner is away. While watching a beautiful woman perform a private dance through a telescope, he becomes obsessed with her and is drawn into a mystery involving voyeurism, deception, and murder.
Blending elements of Hitchcockian suspense, film noir, and Hollywood satire, the film explores obsession, performance, and the act of watching itself. Its stylised use of Los Angeles locations, erotic tension, and self-conscious references to cinema create one of Brian De Palma’s most elaborate examinations of illusion and desire.

title: Diamonds of the Night
description: Our screening on Thursday 10 September will be introduced by Second Run DVD founder Mehelli Modi. Němec’s debut feature is one…

title: Tony
description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

title: BITTER CHRISTMAS
description: Raúl is a cult filmmaker in the midst of a creative crisis. When tragedy strikes one of his closest collaborators, he draws inspiration from it to write his next film. Little by little, he imagines Elsa, a filmmaker in the midst of writing a script, whose journey begins to mirror his own. The two fi...

title: The Invite
description: A couple invites the neighbours over for cocktails, igniting an evening full of unexpected twists and turns, revealing deeply repressed emotions and unexplored sexuality.

title: SUPER NATURE
description: Filmed exclusively on the original home movie format, Super 8, SUPER NATURE  proposes a new way of seeing. A celebration of all we have and reflecting on all we have to lose, audiences are invited on a journey across 25 different countries, with people embracing both abundance and loss, to feel a se...

title: EC: THE PARSON’S WIDOW
description: (PRÄSTÄNKAN) In this lyrical, early Dreyer comedy, a young parson wins a plum parish in 17th-century Norway, but is obliged to marry the widow of his deceased predecessor and pretend his attractive young fiancée is his sister. Dreyer’s touch is evident in the close-ups of the pastor’s would-be rivals and parishioners, and in a slow pan presaging the 360-degree views of VAMPYR.

title: CF75: Soldier Girls + Q&A
description: Contemporary Films 75th Anniversary Nick Broomfield and Joan Churchill’s riveting documentary, shot over 3 months, following a group of women going through basic training for the US Army. Fifty started out but only thirty made it through to the end. They concentrate on three of the young women: an 18-year old black woman whose constant giggling and grins drive the platoon sergeant to distraction, another who provides encouragement and support to the others who find it hard, and a third woman who also finds she cannot tolerate army life but is more inhibited. You see each of them change as they face the challenges and rigours before them, all captured with startling intimacy by Broomfield and Churchill. As Broomfield states on his own website: “Joan and I went through Basic Training for 14 weeks. Fred Wiseman lent us a tape recorder. [D.A.] Pennebaker and Chris Hegedus lent us a cutting room. We only got funding after it was shot. We both lost 20 pounds making it – it was so hot.” After the screening directors Nick Broomfield (in person) and Joan Churchill (via live Zoom), will discuss the film.

title: Off-Circuit: UK PREMIERE Pin de Fartie + Q&A
description: The latest production from boundlessly imaginative Argentine collective El Pampero Cine sees successive pairs of characters bid farewell: a mother and her son, a caretaker and her charge, two actors endlessly rehearsing a scene that will never be performed. A playful spin on theatrical adaptation, Alejo Moguillansky's new film is a delightfully imaginative take on Samuel Beckett's Fin de Partie , punctuated by music, tennis, and another exceptional turn by Laura Paredes. The UK Premiere screening on the 4 September will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Alejo Moguillansky.

title: Animation in Love: Olivia and the Clouds (15)
Leviticus
description: Teenage boys Naim and Ryan strike up an unexpected connection. But when their bond draws the attention of their community, a ritual is performed on them, releasing a violent entity. An entity that takes the form of its victim's truest desire.

title: TO LOVE, HONOR, AND OBEY
description: Shot in battered women’s shelters, urban and suburban neighborhoods, counseling centers, and even in a county jail where a woman has been incarcerated for the murder of her abusive husband, TO LOVE, HONOR, AND OBEY explores the social, psychological, and cultural factors that contribute to violence against women regardless of ethnicity or economic background. Survivors, safe house administrators, counselors, police officers, and male abusers in counseling explore the many factors that contribute to the pervasiveness of this tragic aspect of American family life. A Third World Newsreel production.

title: Fiddlehead presents: GOOD WILL HUNTING
description: Fiddlehead is a post-hardcore supergroup made up of members of Basement, Have Heart, Big Contest and Intent. Their debut EP, Out Of The Bloom, was meant to be a one-off; a swansong for the mid-noughties emo that encapsulated everything the band was trying to do. However, since signing to Run For Cover Records, they have released several full-length albums and played a run of tours. Catch them while you can – lead singer Patrick Flynn is now a full-time teacher and only plays shows on weekends.

title: UK Premiere: Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie(15)
The Dark Knight
description: The city of Chicago plays an oppressively glum Gotham in Nolan, Christian Bale, and Gary Oldman’s second Batman outing, a film of Langian architectural oppression that pits Bruce Wayne’s alter ego against Heath Ledger’s anarchic Clown Prince of Crime, with Oldman’s Commissioner Gordon the voice of law-and-order in an increasingly Bedlam-like city. Though Oldman may be known for his chameleonic transformations as an actor and his ability to comfortably occupy the skin of vastly different characters, he would in interviews cite Gordon as the character he’d played who is closest to himself: “A good sense of right and wrong… Family man. Just a regular geezer.” Part of Gary Oldman: The Protean Man

title: Red Desert
description: Michelangelo Antonioni’s 1960s panoramas of contemporary alienation were decade-defining artistic events, and Red Desert, his first color film, is perhaps his most epochal. This provocative look at the spiritual desolation of the technological age – about a disaffected woman, brilliantly portrayed by Antonioni muse Monica Vitti, wandering through a bleak industrial landscape beset by power plants and environmental toxins, and tentatively flirting with her husband’s coworker, played by Richard Harris – continues to keep viewers spellbound. With one startling, painterly composition after another – of abandoned fishing cottages, electrical towers, looming docked ships – Red Desert creates a nearly apocalyptic image of its time, and confirms Antonioni as cinema’s preeminent poet of the modern age. (Janus Films)

title: Onslaught
description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

title: THE BEST LITTLE WHOREHOUSE IN TEXAS
description: When a big TV crusader Melvin P. Thorpe threatens to expose the Chicken Ranch to public scandal and close it down, Miss Mona doesn’t go down without a fight. With the help of Sheriff Ed Earl Dodd, the two join together to keep it open and find romance along the way. Sing along through this extraordinary story about passion, scandal and romance.

title: Stella
description: The screening on Thursday 10 September will be introduced by former Judge and human rights advocate, Betty Iliadou. Synopsis: Stella is…

title: The Odyssey
description: The Odyssey (2026), Christopher Nolan’s epic adaptation of Homer’s classic, follows Greek hero Odysseus on a perilous journey home after the Trojan War, encountering gods, monsters, and treacherous seas while his family faces turmoil in Ithaca Photo Id may required for 15 certificate films

title: Wake in Fright
description: It’s the eve of the Christmas holiday, and polite, young middle-class schoolteacher John Grant (Gary Bond), tied to a position at a tiny township in the outback, is on his way to Sydney to see his girlfriend by way of a stopoff in the grubby mining burg Bundanyabba (“The Yabba” to locals) when he pops into the pub for a drink… Five days of debauchery with local degenerates Donald Pleasence and Chips Rafferty later, the fresh-faced Grant has been replaced by a desperate, unshaven, beer-and-booze-pickled maniac, acquainted with species of depravity he could scarcely have imagined a week ago, and with the barbaric rites of the bush. A furious fever dream from Canuck director Kotcheff, who knew a thing or two about chronic self-degradation as practiced in far-flung outposts of the British Commonwealth, and one of the greatest of Australian films. Part of The Worldwide West

title: Tony (15) (AD)
description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, carving out a slice of a summer that will shape the course of his life.

title: Don't Look Back In Anger
description: “Don’t Look Back In Anger” charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s triumphant reunion tour, Oasis Live ‘25, one of the most anticipated rock ‘n’ roll comebacks of our time. The film is an unapologetically uplifting account of the biggest musical event of 2025, capturing the experience and emotions of the band and their fans across the world. The unique perspective includes rehearsal, backstage, and onstage access as well as the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in over 20 years. Alongside the band’s sold-out world tour, the film also explores the profound emotional impact of this phenomenal global cultural moment and what their music means to audiences and generations worldwide. Steven Knight says, “The Oasis world tour united generations, cultures and countries and spoke to a broken world about reconciliation. ‘Don’t Look Back In Anger’ is not only your ticket to the show – it’s a backstage pass and a seat at the table when Liam and Noel sit down together for the first time in 15 years and tell it how it is and how it was.” Featuring unprecedented access and never-before-seen footage, the film is a Magna Studios production, presented by Sony Music Vision in association with Sony Music Entertainment UK. The producers are Sam Bridger (“Lewis Capaldi: How I’m Feeling Now,” “Meet Me in the Bathroom”) and Guy Heeley (“Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man”). The executive producers include Kate Shepherd, Marisa Clifford, Davud Karbassioun, Tom Mackay, Krista Wegener, Isabel Davis, and Tim O’Shea, with Oscar®-winning sound mixers James Mather (“Top Gun: Maverick,” “Belfast”) and Tarn Willers (“The Zone of Interest”), cinematographer Haris Zambarloukos (“Belfast,” “Beetlejuice Beetlejuice”), and editors George Cragg and Martina Zamolo leading the creative technical team.

title: NAMIBIA, INDEPENDENCE NOW + REORIENTING AFRICA
description: Pearl Bowser & Christine Choy NAMIBIA, INDEPENDENCE NOW 1985, 55 min, 16mm-to-DCP This moving film was shot inside refugee settlements in Zambia and Angola in the mid-1980s. It examines how exiled Namibians worked to free their country from illegal South African exploitation and prepare for their country's independence. It shows many aspects of their daily life in exile, especially the women, who were at the forefront of the independence struggle. It focuses on the activities of exiled Namibian independence leader General Toivo ya Toivo, filmed just weeks after his negotiated release from a South African prison. Christine Choy REORIENTING AFRICA 2016, 37 min, DCP This later work by Christine Choy focuses on Chinese workers and Chinese economic development in Ghana, Africa. Total running time: ca. 95 min.

title: Pink Palace 4th Birthday: THE BIRDCAGE (+ Discussion and Party)
description: Pink Palace celebrates it's 4th Birthday with THE BIRDCAGE  Come and join us for a cosy intro chat charting the history of the UK’s only weekly queer film club, the events, the premieres, the guests, the wonderful highs and (very) occasional lows over the past four years. Founder and curator Andrew ...

title: Pressure
description: In the tense 72 hours before D-Day, and the fate of the free world hanging in the balance, PRESSURE follows General Dwight D. Eisenhower and Captain James Stagg as they face an impossible choice—launch the largest and most dangerous invasion in history or risk losing the war altogether.

title: Late Fame
description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

title: Survive Style 5+ • World Premiere of 4K Restoration
description: World Premiere of New 4K Restoration, courtesy of Third Window Films Five bizarre stories with no apparent connection to one another eventually become intertwined, resulting in surreal circumstances. A salaryman wins tickets to the latest stage sensation, the hypnosis show VIVA FRIENDS! In the middle of the act, an assassin shows up and kills the hypnotist, leaving the salaryman stranded and convinced he is a bird! A gang of burglars roam the suburbs while simultaneously dealing with their budding lust for one another! Meanwhile, a man kills and buries his wife, only to have her claw her way out of the grave and go after him with missile arms and fire breath, over and over again. Acclaimed commercial director Gen Sekiguchi pulls all these strands together into a movie that is thrillingly original. Survive Style 5+ jettisons traditional movie tricks and aims for something more, a movie where love means never having to kill your wife more than five or six times.

title: EC: MICHAEL
description: Shot by the great German cinematographers Karl Freund and Rudolph Maté, MICHAEL concerns the unconsummated homosexual love between a painter and his manipulative, larcenous model. The Danish director Benjamin Christensen stars as artist Claude Zoret, modeled in part after Rodin, whose irrepressible love finds its most complete expression in his last painting.

title: Chronovisor
description: Inspired by the true story of a “fake” invention, Kevin Walker and Jack Auen’s Chronovisor follows a Columbia professor deep into a Borgesian labyrinth of textual clues pointing to a time-travel device rumored to have been suppressed by the Vatican.

title: Leviticus (15) (AD)
description: Two teenage boys living in an ultraconservative community in rural Australia are threatened by a violent entity seeking to destroy them in this breath-taking queer horror.

title: WILD THINGS
description:
A high school guidance counsellor in a wealthy Florida community becomes the target of a sexual assault accusation made by two students. As a police investigation begins, a series of revelations, betrayals, and hidden agendas emerge, turning the case into a complex web of manipulation involving students, law enforcement, and local power figures.
A late-1990s neo-noir thriller, the film plays with unreliable characters, shifting alliances, and elaborate twists, using its glossy Florida setting to heighten the contrast between surface respectability and corruption beneath. Its deliberately provocative mix of crime, eroticism, and dark humour has made it a cult favourite of the era.

title: Oasis: Don’t Look Back In Anger
description: An unapologetically uplifting account of the biggest musical event of 2025, capturing the experience and emotions of the band and their fans across the world. The unique perspective includes rehearsal, backstage, and onstage access as well as the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in over 20 years. Alongside the band’s sold-out world tour, the film also explores the profound emotional impact of this phenomenal global cultural moment and what their music means to audiences and generations worldwide.

title: TEENAGE SEX AND DEATH AT CAMP MIASMA
description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director for resurrection. But when she visits the original's star, a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, ...

title: The Dog Stars
description: Set in a post-apocalyptic world in which a virus has wiped out most of humanity, with survivors being terrorized by roaming scavengers called "Reapers." The protagonist is Hig, a pilot who survived the flu that killed everyone he knew, his wife included. He lives in the hangar of a small abandoned airport with his dog, his only neighbor a gun-toting ex-Marine. Hig sometimes heads off in his 1956 Cessna, where he can fish and pretend things are how they used to be. When a random transmission somehow beams through his radio, the voice ignites a hope deep inside him that a better life might exist if he flies a bit further. He risks it all. to chase a possible haven in Grand Junction.

title: I Want Your Sex
description: Gregg Araki's I Want Your Sex tells the story of Elliot (Cooper Hoffman), a kind-hearted if unmotivated twentysomething whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries, and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli XCX) and repressed roommate (Chase Sui Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the film mixes satire, romantic comedy, mystery, and murder through the colourful and edgy visual language for which Araki is best known.

title: Twin Peaks: Fire Walk With Me
description: In the folksy town of Deerfield, Wash., FBI Agent Desmond (Chris Isaak) inexplicably disappears while hunting for the man who murdered a teen girl. The killer is never apprehended, and, after experiencing dark visions and supernatural encounters, Agent Dale Cooper (Kyle MacLachlan) chillingly predicts that the culprit will claim another life. Meanwhile, in the similarly cozy town of Twin Peaks, hedonistic beauty Lara Palmer (Sheryl Lee) hangs with lowlifes and seems destined for a grisly fate.

title: Leviticus
description: Teenage boys Naim and Ryan strike up an unexpected connection. But when their bond draws the attention of their community, a ritual is performed on them, releasing a violent entity. An entity that takes the form of its victim's truest desire.

title: STRAW DOGS
description: A young American and his English wife come to rural England and face increasingly vicious local harassment in this violent, controversial thriller starring Dustin Hoffman and Susan George.

title: Chungking Express
description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’ “Dreams”), its bifurcated structure suggesting the A- and B-sides of a 45. Wong’s international breakthrough introduced new audiences to his rich, sensorial brand of filmmaking, inviting one to disappear into, sink into, live inside, a voluptuary world bigger and brighter than our own—but just as heartbreaking. Part of Like the Wind: Lensed by Christopher Doyle

title: Amelie - 25th Anniversary
description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: Hunt For The Wilderpeople - 10th Anniversary
description: Ricky is a defiant young city kid who finds himself on the run with his cantankerous foster uncle in the wild New Zealand bush. A national manhunt ensues, and the two are forced to put aside their differences and work together to survive.

title: Onslaught
description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

title: Magnolia
description: Written and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson and nominated for three Academy Awards, Magnolia is a cinematic Rubik’s Cube of heightened realism and complexity, that ambitiously interweaves stories set in the San Fernando Valley – brought to life with an exceptional cast. Earl Partridge (Jason Robards) and Jimmy Gator (Philip Baker Hall) each carries with them a gnawing regret like the very cancer they are both fighting, while the majority of the rest of the cast deals with the scars inflicted upon them in their youth, as they head towards their own emotional unravelling. Anderson takes a cue from Newton’s Third Law of Motion, “For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,” and begins to fashion his own law in Magnolia – “There are no coincidences” – as the late-great magician Ricky Jay so convincingly narrates, via the almost supernatural circumstances of seven deaths outlined in the film’s prologue: “This was not just a matter of chance. These strange things happen all the time.” Magnolia put an exclamation mark on 90’s cinema, finding its way into Ingmar Bergman’s “Favorite Films” and Roger Ebert’s “Great Movies List.”

title: Niagara
description: Newlyweds Ray and Polly Cutler (Jean Peters and Casey Adams) take a postponed honeymoon at Niagara Falls, where they encounter Rose and George Loomis (Marilyn Monroe and Joseph Cotten). The Loomis’s rocky relationship hangs over the couple’s romantic getaway, further complicated by a murder. 1953 was an important year for Monroe with the successes of Gentlemen Prefer Blondes and How to Marry a Millionaire in the following months, and her breakout performance as the sensual Rose in Niagara catapulted the actor into superstardom.
director: Henry Hathaway PRODUCED BY: Charles Brackett

title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
description: The epic adventure centers around Indy (Harrison Ford) and his perilous quest for the Ark of the Covenant, a Biblical artifact of unspeakable power also sought after by Hitler's armies. In a race against the Nazis, Indy travels the globe in pursuit of the Ark, reigniting passions with his former flame Marion Ravenwood (Karen Allen), aided by allies Marcus Brody (Denholm Elliott) and Sallah (John Rhys-Davies), and thwarted by danger, double-crosses and enemies at every turn.

title: The Cook, the Thief, His Wife & Her Lover
description: When churlish mobster Albert Spica (Michael Gambon) acquires an upscale French restaurant in London, he dines there nightly, effectively scaring off the clientele with his bad manners. His wife, Georgina (Helen Mirren), is especially disgusted by him, and soon begins an affair with another restaurant guest, Michael (Alan Howard). Despite their efforts to keep it a secret, however, Spica finds out about their trysts, and he plans to exact a terrible revenge.

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
description: Visionary director Jane Schoenbrun ( I Saw the TV Glow ) presents a new kind of horror remake in Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma . Bursting with imagination and surreal wit, their latest genre-bending wonder affirms there’s no such thing as a guilty pleasure.

title: Onslaught
description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

title: Eraserhead
description: First time father Henry Spencer tries to survive his industrial environment, his angry girlfriend, and the unbearable screams of his newly born mutant child. David Lynch arrived on the scene in 1977, almost like a mystical UFO gracing the landscape of LA with its enigmatic radiance. His inaugural work, "Eraserhead" (1977), stood out as a cinematic anomaly, painting a surreal narrative of a young man navigating a dystopian, industrialized America, grappling not only with his tumultuous home life but also contending with an irate girlfriend and a mutant child.

title: Purple Rain
description: A young musician, tormented by an abusive situation at home, must contend with a rival singer, a burgeoning romance, and his own dissatisfied band, as his star begins to rise.

title: FOR Y'UR HEIGHT ONLY
description:
A diminutive secret agent known as Agent 00 is sent on a mission to rescue a kidnapped scientist and stop the evil warlord Mr. Giant from using a powerful invention to take over the world. Equipped with an array of gadgets and relying on his martial arts skills, Agent 00 battles his way through a series of villains in this Filipino spoof of the James Bond films.
A wildly eccentric piece of Filipino exploitation cinema, the film plays as a low-budget spy adventure packed with action, comedy, gadgets, and absurd set pieces. Built around Weng Weng’s unique screen presence, it became an international cult curiosity and one of the most unusual James Bond-inspired films ever made.

title: WHO KILLED VINCENT CHIN?
description: Restored by the Academy Film Archive and The Film Foundation, in association with the Museum of Chinese in America. Restoration funding provided by the Hobson/Lucas Family Foundation, with additional support provided by Todd Phillips. “On a hot summer night in Detroit, Ronald Ebens, an autoworker, killed a young Chinese-American engineer with a baseball bat. Although he confessed, he never spent a day in jail. This gripping Academy Award-nominated film relentlessly probes the implications of the murder in the streets of Detroit, for the families of those involved, and for the American justice system. Not so much a documentary murder investigation as a meticulously constructed meditation on the race relations, economic forces, and failings of the American legal system that comprised the backdrop for the murder of a Chinese-American automotive engineer in Detroit in 1982, WHO KILLED VINCENT CHIN? remains a stirring, absorbing elegy for justice unserved. Drawing from interviews with Chin’s family and friends and Chin’s killer, automotive assembly-line worker Ron Ebens, along with a wealth of archival footage, WHO KILLED VINCENT CHIN? paints a complex and tragically relevant portrait of an America roiled by socioeconomic unease, the crisis of the automotive industry, and the prevalence of xenophobia.” –NEW YORK FILM FESTIVAL “The most important political documentary of the 1980s.” –Bill Nichols

title: Unbreakable
description: M. Night Shyamalan twists the superhero genre into an introspective thriller in this genre-shattering slow burn. An ordinary man makes an extraordinary discovery when a train accident leaves his fellow passengers dead — and him unscathed. The answer to this mystery could lie with the mysterious Elijah Price, a man who suffers from a disease that renders his bones as fragile as glass. The closest cinema has come to picturing superheroes in real life, this banger is best on the big screen!

title: Matches and Days. [excerpt from work in progress]
description: Matches and Days [excerpt from work in progress]. 2027. Romania. Written and directed by Andrei Ujică. In Romanian; English subtitles. 12 min. MoMA premieres a work-in-progress excerpt from Andrei Ujică’s latest project, in which the Romanian filmmaker reflects on a lifetime of watching World Cup football and sharing this passion with his son and grandchildren. “Matches and Days will be an intimate and nostalgic cinematic essay, almost like a family album,” Ujică says, “as well as a meditation on football as a mirror of the struggle for the autonomy of art. The narrative will span the peak of the Pelé project, reached in the victorious 1970 final against Italy, and the tragic failure of the next great Brazilian generation centered around Zico, Sócrates, and Falcão in 1982 and 1986.” TWST / Things We Said Today. 2024. France/Romania. Directed by Andrei Ujică. DCP courtesy Minerva Pictures. In English, French, German; English subtitles. 86 min. TWST | Things We Said Today is Andrei Ujică’s personal reminiscence, created in collaboration with the writer Geoffrey O’Brien, about a watershed cultural and political moment: the arrival of the Beatles in New York for their August 1965 concert at Shea Stadium, which took place against a backdrop of racial upheaval, war, and poverty in the United States. This marked an inflection point in Ujică’s life as a teenager in a Romanian village on the border with Yugoslavia, offering a transformative glimpse of freedom beyond the Iron Curtain and an epiphany about the power of art to transcend the soul-crushing drudgeries, lies, fears, and punishments of life under authoritarian rule. Frenzied images of girls attempting to storm the Beatles’ press conference at the Warwick Hotel in Midtown Manhattan are juxtaposed with television and radio news reports of police brutality and resistance in the poor, neglected Black neighborhoods of Watts and Harlem. This study in jarring contrasts is deepened by 8mm home movies, unearthed by Ujică and his researchers on eBay, of a trio of sheltered white suburban girls visiting the New York World’s Fair on the same grounds as the newly built Shea Stadium in Flushing Meadows. Excerpts from Ujică’s own short story, “Isabella, the Friend of the Butterflies”—which the filmmaker wrote as a teenager in thrall to the Beatles’ White Album—and the animated, spectral presence of our two protagonists, a then-17-year-old O’Brien and Judith Kristen, the girl in the home movies, guide us through the wild and wooly summer of ’65.

title: The School of Rock

But as the school’s stern principal closes in and the Battle of the Bands looms, Dewey must risk everything to prove that rock ‘n’ roll can change lives.

title: Red Desert
description: Michelangelo Antonioni’s 1960s panoramas of contemporary alienation were decade-defining artistic events, and Red Desert, his first color film, is perhaps his most epochal. This provocative look at the spiritual desolation of the technological age – about a disaffected woman, brilliantly portrayed by Antonioni muse Monica Vitti, wandering through a bleak industrial landscape beset by power plants and environmental toxins, and tentatively flirting with her husband’s coworker, played by Richard Harris – continues to keep viewers spellbound. With one startling, painterly composition after another – of abandoned fishing cottages, electrical towers, looming docked ships – Red Desert creates a nearly apocalyptic image of its time, and confirms Antonioni as cinema’s preeminent poet of the modern age. (Janus Films)

title: EC: THE PASSION OF JOAN OF ARC
description: (LA PASSION DE JEANNE D’ARC) Spiritual rapture and institutional hypocrisy are brought to stark, vivid life in one of the most transcendent achievements of the silent era. Chronicling the trial of Joan of Arc in the final hours leading up to her execution, Dreyer depicts her torment with startling immediacy, employing an array of techniques – including expressionistic lighting, interconnected sets, and painfully intimate close-ups – to immerse viewers in her subjective experience. Anchoring Dreyer’s audacious formal experimentation is a legendary performance by Renée Falconetti, whose haunted face channels both the agony and the ecstasy of martyrdom. “With THE PASSION OF JOAN OF ARC, there occurs a most striking change in both the film-maker’s style and his intensity of thematic concentration. A few potent shots in previous movies hardly promise the unique and brilliant imagery which here bursts forth frame after frame. […] The vision of JOAN is inspired or demoniac. Her passion is observed with clinical detail in the sharp-etched, stark compositions, many relentless close-ups. But this is also loving detail, for Joan is the first of Dreyer’s possessed, a lineage which may be traced through the victims of VAMPYR to Anne in DAY OF WRATH and Johannes in ORDET; characters who work out their passions throughout the process of their films with peculiar intensity and directness, so that identification with the director himself is implicit.” –Ken Kelman, FILM CULTURE

title: TEACH OUR CHILDREN + INSIDE WOMEN INSIDE
description: Christine Choy & Susan Robeson TEACH OUR CHILDREN 1972, 35 min, 16mm-to-DCP This film focuses on the historic 1971 Attica prison rebellion in upstate New York. It targets the conditions that caused prisoners to take drastic steps toward securing their basic rights. The film questions the reactions of prison warden Oswald, New York governor Nelson Rockefeller, and President Nixon, as well as the death of 31 inmates and prison guards from bullets fired by the National Guard. Through on-site footage taken during and following the rebellion, and follow-up interviews with inmates, TEACH OUR CHILDREN relates a powerful message concerning prisoner’s rights and represents an important historical document. Christine Choy & Cynthia Maurizio INSIDE WOMEN INSIDE 1978, 21 min, 16mm-to-DCP This film exposes the daily humiliation regularly faced by women in U.S. prisons using firsthand accounts of inmates at the North Carolina Correctional Center for Women and the Correctional Institute for Women at Riker’s Island, New York. Provocative interviews with these women reveal the anger and frustrations of life behind bars. In spite of the realities of their oppression, their optimism and strength are insurmountable. Total running time: ca. 60 min.

Alongside the band’s sold-out world tour, the film also explores the profound emotional impact of this phenomenal global cultural moment and what their music means to audiences and generations worldwide.

When a laser beam zaps a wise-cracking duck from Duckworld to Cleveland, he’s got to make the best on Earth and he makes friends with a rocker chick with enormous hair, and picks up a cigar habit. Can Howard make it back to his home planet? Will evil scientists blast something even more evil through their laserbeams? Does the plot even matter when you’ve got a smoking superhero duck made by human hands in a time before CGI? Do your Friday night a favor and lose your mind over Howard the Duck !

title: Videograms of a Revolution
description: Videograms of a Revolution. 1992. Germany/Romania. Directed by Harun Farocki, Andrei Ujică. DCP. In English, German, Romanian; English subtitles. 106 min. In Andrei Ujică’s seminal collaboration with Harun Farocki, official broadcasts of Nicolae Ceauşescu’s iron rule over Romania seem an impotent sham in the face of on-the-ground, eyewitness accounts of his dramatic demise by ordinary citizens, some of them wielding video cameras. Over five chaotic days in December 1989, street demonstrations in the western Romanian city of Timişoara erupted into violence and brutal state recrimination across the nation. Civilians occupied the national television station in Bucharest while Communist party stooges, attempting to flee or shift blame, were rounded up and put on trial. The Ceauşescus, once fêted by Queen Elizabeth, Jimmy Carter, and Kim Il Sung, were found guilty of “genocide” by an Extraordinary Military Tribunal and executed on Christmas Day. Two days later, viewers in Romania (and throughout the world) tuned in to watch incontrovertible videotape evidence of their bullet-riddled bodies. Ujică and Farocki perform a forensic study of authoritarian propaganda at a climactic moment of flameout, when reality could no longer bend to a dictator’s pernicious fiction of prosperity, progress, and international stature.

title: Out of the Present
description: Out of the Present. 1996. Germany. Written and directed by Andrei Ujică. DCP. In Russian; English subtitles. 96 min. Out of the Present charts the 10-month orbital isolation of Sergei Krikalev, a cosmonaut on the Mir space station who took 5,000 trips around the Earth while, back home, his native Soviet Union imploded and a rave broke out on New Year’s Eve 1991 at the Cosmonautics Pavilion at Moscow’s VDNKh, the “Permanent Exhibition of Achievements of the National Economy.” Framed through the first two sequences ever shot in space on 35mm for a feature film, with guidance from Vadim Yusov, Andrei Tarkovsky’s cinematographer on Solaris, and with allusions to 2001: A Space Odyssey and Solaris itself, Out of the Present oscillates between seriocomic scenes of Krikalev adrift in space—the flight engineer, a kind of good-humored Major Tom, attempts a life of normalcy in his zero-gravity tin-can space station, a gimcrack of exposed wires and floating detritus—and amateur footage of rioting Muscovites and tanks bearing down on the House of Soviets during the tumult of the August Coup. Within four breathless months, Mikhail Gorbachev would resign, and the dissolution of the USSR would be concluded on December 26, 1991. What lingers in the mind and eye, however, are the singular beauty of the cosmic perspective, a humanity that transcends petty politics, and “the smell of the earth…the feeling of being home again.”

title: The Traveler
description: Join us for Abbas Kiarostami’s remarkable feature debut with this simple, intimate, and haunting tale of childish obsessions and the means we’ll use to fulfill them. Hassan Darabi, a troublesome, amoral 10-year-old boy in a small Iranian town wishes to see the Iran national football team play an important match in Tehran. In order to achieve that, he scams his friends and neighbors. A quest film that’s also a study of youthful obsession, it’s filmed in edgy black and white with a quiet energy that matches its hero’s. The Traveler has an acridly ironic ending and one of the best performances by a child in Kiarostami’s early work.

description: Pearl Bowser & Christine Choy NAMIBIA, INDEPENDENCE NOW 1985, 55 min, 16mm-to-DCP This moving film was shot inside refugee settlements in Zambia and Angola in the mid-1980s. It examines how exiled Namibians worked to free their country from illegal South African exploitation and prepare for their country's independence. It shows many aspects of their daily life in exile, especially the women, who were at the forefront of the independence struggle. It focuses on the activities of exiled Namibian independence leader General Toivo ya Toivo, filmed just weeks after his negotiated release from a South African prison. title: HA HA SHANGHAI
description: “HA HA SHANGHAI is an outlier in [Choy’s] oeuvre. Far more personal than most of her other films, this documentary is a family affair that features her mother and son as characters, and her daughter Ku-Ling Siegel behind the lens. Christine herself describes the film as a ‘documentary journal,’ and while HA HA SHANGHAI begins as a personal history, it soon develops into a Kafkaesque farce. In the film, [Choy] returns to Shanghai after 30 years to search for the title of a house built by her mother. She reconnects with friends of her family and a local choir teacher. She storms into government buildings with frenetic energy, demanding to see paperwork. When things seem dire, Christine visits a fortune teller and a palm reader, grasping at straws lost to time. Through anecdotes and recollections, she interrogates the modernization of China as well as the Cultural Revolution, the events of which caused the family home to be lost in the first place. […] Although HA HA SHANGHAI is rooted in Christine’s personal experience, it tells a larger tale of how much China has changed since she left.” –Violet Columbus & Ben Klein

title: The Autobiography of Nicolae Ceaușescu
description: The Autobiography of Nicolae Ceaușescu. 2010. Romania/Germany. Directed by Andrei Ujică. 35mm courtesy the Film Desk. In Romanian; English subtitles. 180 min. Andrei Ujică’s magisterial film stitches together 24 years of state propaganda images of the Romanian dictator and his wife, Elena—painstakingly choreographed pageants, diplomatic visits, party congresses, and unconvincingly merry scenes of home life—into an expansive vision of a nation in thrall to, and at the mercy of, a cult leader. Drawing on archival material that inadvertently reveals moments excised from the sanctioned narrative, Ujică illuminates the fissures and tensions that would lead to the Ceauşescus’ execution by firing squad on Christmas Day 1989. As J. Hoberman observed in The New York Review of Books, “In Cannes, Ujică told interviewers that, for him, The Autobiography was a form of therapy. In effect, his first movie to be made in Romania enabled him to return to his home and reconstruct Ceauşescu’s Potemkin village from its celluloid shards. The result is as monumental as it is ephemeral, and not without a certain ghastly pathos. The misery of Ceauşescu’s dreadful misrule that is the movie’s structuring absence is amplified by the manufactured delusions foisted on a suffering nation.”

title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
description: The first film directed by a woman to receive the Queer Palm at the Cannes Film Festival, Céline Sciamma’s 18th-century romance revels in the sensuous affair between aristocrat Héloïse (Adèle Haenel) and artist Marianne (Noémie Merlant), who is commissioned to paint her portrait. Though betrothed to a wealthy man of the Milanese upper class, the stubborn Héloïse refuses to be captured, either by her male suitor or the artist meant to paint her. Sciamma’s tale of sexual liberation finds beauty in the electric connection between her leading women for a gorgeous and aching story of forbidden love and the fleeting nature of romance.

title: MIRAGE / STRAIT-JACKET
description: An accountant suddenly suffers from amnesia. This appears related to the suicide of his boss. Now some violent thugs are out to get him. They work for a shadowy figure known simply as The Major.

title: The Court Jester
description: A hapless carnival performer masquerades as the court jester as part of a plot against an evil ruler who has overthrown the rightful king.

title: EC: DAY OF WRATH
description: (VREDENS DAG) “Carl Dreyer’s art begins to unfold at the point where most other directors give up. Witchcraft and martyrdom are his themes – but his witches don’t ride broomsticks, they ride the erotic fears of their persecutors. It is a world that suggests a dreadful fusion of Hawthorne and Kafka.” –Pauline Kael

title: Interstellar
description: In Earth's future, a global crop blight and second Dust Bowl are slowly rendering the planet uninhabitable. Professor Brand (Michael Caine), a brilliant NASA physicist, is working on plans to save mankind by transporting Earth's population to a new home via a wormhole. But first, Brand must send former NASA pilot Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) and a team of researchers through the wormhole and across the galaxy to find out which of three planets could be mankind's new home.

title: Sinners
description: From Ryan Coogler—director of “Black Panther” and “Creed”—and starring Michael B. Jordan comes a new vision of fear: “Sinners.” Trying to leave their troubled lives behind, twin brothers (Jordan) return to their hometown to start again, only to discover that an even greater evil is waiting to welcome them back. “You keep dancing with the devil, one day he’s gonna follow you home.” Written and directed by Academy Award-nominated filmmaker Coogler, “Sinners” stars Jordan (the “Black Panther” and “Creed” franchises) in a dual role, joined by Oscar nominee Hailee Steinfeld (“Bumblebee,” “True Grit”), Jack O’Connell (“Ferrari”), Wunmi Mosaku (“Passenger”), Jayme Lawson (“The Woman King”), Omar Miller (“True Lies”), and Delroy Lindo (“Da 5 Bloods”). The film is produced by Zinzi Coogler, Sev Ohanian and Ryan Coogler. The executive producers are Ludwig Göransson, Will Greenfield and Rebecca Cho.

title: Legend
description: Set in a timeless mythical forest inhabited by fairies, goblins, unicorns and mortals, this fantastic story follows a mystical forest dweller, chosen by fate, to undertake a heroic quest. He must save the beautiful Princess Lili and defeat the demonic Lord of Darkness, or the world will be plunged into a never-ending ice age.

title: Death Wish
description: Bronson’s gonna get you, punk! After his wife is murdered by street punks, a pacifistic New York City architect becomes a one-man vigilante squad, prowling the streets for would-be muggers after dark. The ultimate vigilante film with a tough-as-nails Charles Bronson – vengeance has never felt better!

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma

At Category H Film Club, we’re bringing the terror of the fairground Rio’s screen two with a late night double bill of MAL...

title: Christine
description: Hell hath no fury like a ’58 Plymouth. When a bullied teen buys a dilapidated automobile named Christine , he sets out to repair her to her former beauty. But this cursed car has a terrifying mind of its own. Stephen King’s classic novel comes to life in a chiller from director John Carpenter. How do you kill something that can’t possibly be alive?
