title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
description: The epic adventure centers around Indy (Harrison Ford) and his perilous quest for the Ark of the Covenant, a Biblical artifact of unspeakable power also sought after by Hitler's armies. In a race against the Nazis, Indy travels the globe in pursuit of the Ark, reigniting passions with his former flame Marion Ravenwood (Karen Allen), aided by allies Marcus Brody (Denholm Elliott) and Sallah (John Rhys-Davies), and thwarted by danger, double-crosses and enemies at every turn.

title: Clash of the Titans
description: If you love Greek mythology, stop-motion animation, or an all-star adventure, ride your pegasus over to Vidiots for a mythical quest like no other! To win the right to marry his love, the beautiful princess Andromeda, and fulfill his destiny, half-God-half-mortal Perseus must complete various tasks including taming Pegasus, capturing Medusa’s head and battling the feared Kraken. With incredible practical creature effects from the legendary Ray Harryhausen, Harry Hamlin in his hunky prime, and a Mount Olympus that includes Deities Ursula Andress, Sir Laurence Olivier, and Dame Maggie Smith, this 1980s sword and sandal classic has been enchanting audiences for 45 years!

title: The Red Shoes
description: In this classic drama, Vicky Page (Moira Shearer) is an aspiring ballerina torn between her dedication to dance and her desire to love. While her imperious instructor, Boris Lermontov (Anton Walbrook), urges to her to forget anything but ballet, Vicky begins to fall for the charming young composer Julian Craster (Marius Goring). Eventually Vicky, under great emotional stress, must choose to pursue either her art or her romance, a decision that carries serious consequences.

title: Wild Inside
description: Our microcinema is going to the birds with Penny Lane’s rapturous documentary about everyone’s favorite escaped zoo owl Flaco – Wild Inside .

title: 2 Pasolini
description: 2 Pasolini. 2021. Germany. Directed by Andrei Ujică. DCP. In Italian; English subtitles. 11 min. Sopralluoghi in Palestina per il vangelo secondo Matteo (Location Hunting in Palestine). 1965. Italy. Directed by Pier Paolo Pasolini. DCP courtesy Viggo. In Italian; English subtitles. 55 min. Andrei Ujică uses a Tupac Shakur song and Pier Paolo Pasolini’s documentary Sopralluoghi in Palestina (Location Hunting in Palestine) (put together as research for Pasolini’s 1964 film The Gospel According to St. Matthew) to interrogate the making and remaking of history. In his journey to the Holy Land in search of “authentic” locations for his Biblical epic, Pasolini, a heterodox Marxist Catholic, was bound to find a modern landscape inhospitable to the historical presence of Christ. And yet, precisely because he ended up filming instead in southern Italy only two years after Vatican II—a seismic moment of modern Catholic self-reckoning—Pasolini’s true masterpiece is a deeply personal confrontation with ideas of liberation theology, light/faith and dark/blindness, and the role of the artist in aesthetics and spirituality. The montagist Ujică deposits several elements of violent beauty into this dialectic: Christ’s jeremiad against the Pharisees and scribes, images of a tempest-tossed sea from a pair of films by Dominique Pipat, and Tupac’s prophetic “Hit ’Em Up,” which, with lyrics like “Who shot me? But you punks didn’t finish / Now you ’bout to feel the wrath of a menace,” evokes another defiant proto-revolutionary cut down in the prime of youth.

title: Back to the Future Part II
description: Getting back was only the beginning. Now our time traveling teen (Michael J. Fox) and his eccentric mentor (Christopher Lloyd) will have to navigate multiple timelines if they’re going to set their past, present, and future straight. But small changes could have giant consequences, especially when big bully Biff Tannen (Thomas F. Wilson) is involved.

title: Black Narcissus
description: Sister Clodagh (Deborah Kerr) enlists others from her nunnery to found a school and hospital in the Himalayan palace of Mopu, where the unrelenting winds and extraordinary beauty of the landscape distract the sisters from their mission. With hues so vibrant the images seem to breathe, Jack Cardiff, who won his first Oscar for Cinematography (Color) on this project, pushes Technicolor to its limits. He’s supported by the striking, Oscar-winning art direction of frequent Michael Powell-Emeric Pressburger collaborator Alfred Junge in what Powell has called “the most erotic film I have ever made.”

title: Chungking Express
description: Every day, Cop 223 (Takeshi Kaneshiro) buys a can of pineapple with an expiration date of May 1, symbolizing the day he'll get over his lost love. He's also got his eye on a mysterious woman in a blond wig (Brigitte Lin), oblivious of the fact she's a drug dealer. Cop 663 (Tony Leung Chiu Wai) is distraught with heartbreak over a breakup. But when his ex drops a spare set of his keys at a local cafe, a waitress (Faye Wong) lets herself into his apartment and spruces up his life.

title: Amarcord
description: In an Italian seaside town, young Titta gets into trouble with his friends and watches various local eccentrics as they engage in often absurd behavior. Frequently clashing with his stern father and defended by his doting mother, Titta witnesses the actions of a wide range of characters, from his extended family to Fascist loyalists to sensual women, with certain moments shifting into fantastical scenarios.

title: SUNDAY SABBATH - MYSTERY HORROR MATINEE
description:
Sunday Sabbath presents undisclosed deep cuts from the history of horror cinema.
From forgotten masterpieces and overlooked oddities to international nightmares and independently made cult classics, each screening offers a surprise journey into the darker corners of the genre. Expect the unexpected: supernatural terror, psychological unease, grisly slashers, Gothic chillers, folk horror, creature features and everything in between. The only thing we can guarantee is that you'll leave having discovered something you never knew you needed to see.
Adults only.

title: Unknown Quantity
description: Unknown Quantity. 2005. Germany. Directed by Andrei Ujică. With Svetlana Alexiyevich, Paul Virilio. DCP. In French; English subtitles. 67 min. In this theatrical version of a gallery installation, the French philosopher and cultural theorist Paul Virilio and the Belarussian Nobel laureate Svetlana Alexievich, author of Voices from Chernobyl: Chronicle of the Future, grapple with the man-made tragedy of nuclear catastrophe and its implications for irrationality and fear in decision making and technological innovation. With shades of Andrei Tarkovsky’s Stalker—the heroic men and women who volunteered to contain the Chernobyl meltdown referred to themselves, in fact, as “stalkers”—Virilio and Alexievich venture into a black-box zone of epistemological and ontological uncertainty as they contend with human yearning and hubristic overreach, the myth of progress, and the awful, annihilating vastness of destruction in Chernobyl, seemingly as unfathomable as that of the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki, or perhaps even September 11.

The resulting film is an ode to collaborative filmmaking. Made on a micro-budget by a proudly trans, non-binary, queer and neurodive...

title: Perfect Days
description: Hirayama is content with his life as a toilet cleaner in Tokyo. Outside of his structured routine, he cherishes music on cassette tapes, books, and taking photos of trees. Through unexpected encounters, he reflects on finding beauty in the world.

title: UNDER THE VOLCANO
description:
On the Day of the Dead in 1938, Geoffrey Firmin, a former British consul living in a small Mexican town, drifts through the final day of his life in an alcoholic haze. The unexpected return of his estranged wife Yvonne offers the possibility of reconciliation, while the arrival of his half-brother Hugh reopens old tensions and regrets. As political anxieties gather on the eve of the Second World War and the festivities of the holiday unfold around him, Geoffrey moves through cantinas, streets, and memories, unable to escape either his past or his addiction.
Adapted from Malcolm Lowry's long-considered "unfilmable" 1947 novel, Under the Volcano was one of John Huston's most ambitious late-career projects. Filmed on location in Mexico and anchored by Albert Finney's Oscar-nominated performance, the film translates Lowry's dense modernist work into a meditation on self-destruction, mortality, and political uncertainty. Rather than treating alcoholism as a social problem or moral failing, Huston presents it as part of a wider tragedy unfolding against a landscape haunted by death, memory, and impending historical catastrophe. Widely regarded as one of Huston's finest later films, it remains a singular literary adaptation and one of cinema's most powerful portraits of addiction.

title: This Is Buzz w/ Director Mark Pellington Q&A
description: This is Buzz is a documentary by director Mark Pellington that explores the fast-paced, influential 1990 MTV collage series Buzz, serving as a look back at an early, radical precursor to modern internet and meme culture.

title: 20th Anniversary of Marie Antoinette
description: The third feature film from Oscar-winning writer-director Sofia Coppola ( Lost in Translation , 2003) transposes her fascination with the inner lives of young women to 18th century Versailles with this semi-biographical story of Marie Antoinette, Queen of France from 1774 to 1793. Inspired by her favorite period dramas and biopics, including Ken Russell’s Lisztomania (1975) and Milos Forman’s Amadeus (1984), Coppola gained extraordinary access to shoot at the Palace at Versailles, and her attention to production design and costuming details cushion her characters in lavish, insulated surroundings—and garnered the film’s costume designer Milena Canonero her third Oscar win. Punctuated with anachronistic postpunk and new wave music, Coppola’s refreshing take on a centuries-old history brings the woes of the past into sharp comparison with present-day concerns of girls, teens, and young women for a deeply felt and beautifully rendered cinematic achievement. In a separately ticketed event before the screening, Sofia Coppola signs copies of her new book , Making Marie Antoinette , at the Academy Museum Store. Programmed and note by K.J. Relth-Miller.

title: FROM SPIKES TO SPINDLES + FEI TIEN, GODDESS IN FLIGHT
description: Christine Choy FROM SPIKES TO SPINDLES 1976, 46 min, 16mm-to-DCP This raw, gutsy portrait of New York’s Chinatown captures the early days of an emerging consciousness in the community. We see a Chinatown rarely depicted, a vibrant community whose young and old join forces to protest police brutality and hostile real estate developers. With bold strokes, it paints an overview of the community and its history, from the early laborers driving spikes into the transcontinental railroad to the garment workers of today. Christine Choy FEI TIEN, GODDESS IN FLIGHT 1983, 26 min, 16mm-to-DCP Based on the play, “Pigeons”, by Ginny Lim, this film focuses on the meeting between an older immigrant and a younger American-born woman living in NYC’s Chinatown. The linkages in their pasts and possible futures unfold as their friendship grows. Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: The Virgin Suicides
description: Slip into the dark and dreamy world of Sofia Coppola’s directorial debut based on the novel by Jeffrey Eugenides. Suburban Michigan, 1975. Cecilia, one of the five shadowy Lisbon sisters, attempts suicide—an event that unravels the lives of the Lisbon family. Little by little, the family shuts itself off from the world. With the girls forbidden to go out, an obsessed group of local boys plots to rescue them. A hypnotic and ethereal work supported by the sublime soundtrack from Air.

In West Hollywood’s Russian district, Margarita lives out the American Dream: competing on a reality show. Will she slay, serve, or survive? In this sharp, irreverent comedy, a disgraced fashion designer with a dangerously low credit score, Margarita (Anna Baryshnikov) enters a reality show with a six-figure cash prize to save her babushka’s West Hollywood apartment. But as the competition intensifies, slick producer Nicol (Camila Mendes) pushes her to spin her family’s struggle into spectacle, forcing Margarita to decide whether to play along or take control of her own narrative, one unhinged look at a time.

GERTRUD is Dreyer’s statement on love, and it is pure, radiant, and perfect, like a ring.” –Jonas Mekas, MOVIE JOURNAL

title: Mulholland Dr.
description: A dark-haired woman (Laura Elena Harring) is left amnesiac after a car crash. She wanders the streets of Los Angeles in a daze before taking refuge in an apartment. There she is discovered by Betty (Naomi Watts), a wholesome Midwestern blonde who has come to the City of Angels seeking fame as an actress. Together, the two attempt to solve the mystery of Rita's true identity. The story is set in a dream-like Los Angeles, spoilt neither by traffic jams nor smog.

title: We Direct Music Videos Vol. #10 – MARK PELLINGTON
description: We Direct Music Videos is thrilled to present Volume 10 of The Directors Series. This time, our guest is icon of the medium Mark Pellington. Through his celebrated work for artists like Pearl Jam, U2, Foo Fighters, The Fray, Nine Inch Nails, The Flaming Lips, Alice in Chains, Public Enemy, INXS, Leonard Cohen, and numerous others, Mark has crafted a highly influential, completely singular style. Join us for a program of music videos selected by Mark Pellington, alongside a career-spanning discussion.

title: WHO KILLED VINCENT CHIN?
description: Restored by the Academy Film Archive and The Film Foundation, in association with the Museum of Chinese in America. Restoration funding provided by the Hobson/Lucas Family Foundation, with additional support provided by Todd Phillips. “On a hot summer night in Detroit, Ronald Ebens, an autoworker, killed a young Chinese-American engineer with a baseball bat. Although he confessed, he never spent a day in jail. This gripping Academy Award-nominated film relentlessly probes the implications of the murder in the streets of Detroit, for the families of those involved, and for the American justice system. Not so much a documentary murder investigation as a meticulously constructed meditation on the race relations, economic forces, and failings of the American legal system that comprised the backdrop for the murder of a Chinese-American automotive engineer in Detroit in 1982, WHO KILLED VINCENT CHIN? remains a stirring, absorbing elegy for justice unserved. Drawing from interviews with Chin’s family and friends and Chin’s killer, automotive assembly-line worker Ron Ebens, along with a wealth of archival footage, WHO KILLED VINCENT CHIN? paints a complex and tragically relevant portrait of an America roiled by socioeconomic unease, the crisis of the automotive industry, and the prevalence of xenophobia.” –NEW YORK FILM FESTIVAL “The most important political documentary of the 1980s.” –Bill Nichols

title: Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie

title: THE SWEET EAST
description:
During a school trip to Washington, D.C., teenager Lillian becomes separated from her classmates and drifts through a series of encounters across the American East Coast. Moving between political extremists, online radicals, aspiring artists, wealthy intellectuals, and lost idealists, she navigates a fragmented landscape of competing fantasies and ideologies. What begins as an accidental detour gradually becomes an episodic journey through contemporary American life, observed through the perspective of a protagonist who remains both participant and detached witness.
The feature debut of cinematographer Sean Price Williams, The Sweet East combines road movie, picaresque comedy, and social satire to construct a deliberately unstable portrait of the United States in the digital age. Shot on 16mm and written by critic and filmmaker Nick Pinkerton, the film draws on traditions of American independent cinema while reflecting the disorienting overlap of internet culture, political performance, and regional identity. Its succession of encounters functions less as a conventional coming-of-age narrative than as a survey of the myths, anxieties, and self-inventions that shape contemporary America. Starring Talia Ryder, Simon Rex and Jacob Elordi.

title: Out of the Present
description: Out of the Present. 1996. Germany. Written and directed by Andrei Ujică. DCP. In Russian; English subtitles. 96 min. Out of the Present charts the 10-month orbital isolation of Sergei Krikalev, a cosmonaut on the Mir space station who took 5,000 trips around the Earth while, back home, his native Soviet Union imploded and a rave broke out on New Year’s Eve 1991 at the Cosmonautics Pavilion at Moscow’s VDNKh, the “Permanent Exhibition of Achievements of the National Economy.” Framed through the first two sequences ever shot in space on 35mm for a feature film, with guidance from Vadim Yusov, Andrei Tarkovsky’s cinematographer on Solaris, and with allusions to 2001: A Space Odyssey and Solaris itself, Out of the Present oscillates between seriocomic scenes of Krikalev adrift in space—the flight engineer, a kind of good-humored Major Tom, attempts a life of normalcy in his zero-gravity tin-can space station, a gimcrack of exposed wires and floating detritus—and amateur footage of rioting Muscovites and tanks bearing down on the House of Soviets during the tumult of the August Coup. Within four breathless months, Mikhail Gorbachev would resign, and the dissolution of the USSR would be concluded on December 26, 1991. What lingers in the mind and eye, however, are the singular beauty of the cosmic perspective, a humanity that transcends petty politics, and “the smell of the earth…the feeling of being home again.”

title: The Autobiography of Nicolae Ceaușescu
description: The Autobiography of Nicolae Ceaușescu. 2010. Romania/Germany. Directed by Andrei Ujică. 35mm courtesy the Film Desk. In Romanian; English subtitles. 180 min. Andrei Ujică’s magisterial film stitches together 24 years of state propaganda images of the Romanian dictator and his wife, Elena—painstakingly choreographed pageants, diplomatic visits, party congresses, and unconvincingly merry scenes of home life—into an expansive vision of a nation in thrall to, and at the mercy of, a cult leader. Drawing on archival material that inadvertently reveals moments excised from the sanctioned narrative, Ujică illuminates the fissures and tensions that would lead to the Ceauşescus’ execution by firing squad on Christmas Day 1989. As J. Hoberman observed in The New York Review of Books, “In Cannes, Ujică told interviewers that, for him, The Autobiography was a form of therapy. In effect, his first movie to be made in Romania enabled him to return to his home and reconstruct Ceauşescu’s Potemkin village from its celluloid shards. The result is as monumental as it is ephemeral, and not without a certain ghastly pathos. The misery of Ceauşescu’s dreadful misrule that is the movie’s structuring absence is amplified by the manufactured delusions foisted on a suffering nation.”

description: Described by Spike Lee as ‘one of the most underappreciated filmmakers of his time’, African-American playwright turned actor-writer-director Bill Gunn’s radical 1973 vampire movie Ganja & Hess returns as part of our ongoing Rio Forever celebrations marking the 50th anniversary of the cinema in its ...

title: GIRL INTERNET SHOW
description:
Meet Kati Kelli, the late outsider video artist whose subversive online uploads pushed the boundaries of the digital form. GIRL INTERNET SHOW: A KATI KELLI MIXTAPE unearths and reintroduces a surreal, singular body of work by the enigmatic artist. For nearly a decade before her passing in 2019, Kelli ran “Girl Internet Show,” a YouTube channel, parasocial experiment, and epically deranged one-woman universe built from scratch in her bedroom.
This hand-made mixtape from Jane Schoenbrun (I SAW THE TV GLOW) and Jordan Wippell features a lovingly curated selection of Kelli’s online work, unreleased videos, and TOTAL BODY REMOVAL SURGERY—her first (and final) short film opus.

description:
Blue Monday presents undisclosed selections from the deepest recesses of horny cult cinema - encapsulating everything from erotic thrillers, carnal noir, golden age porno and transgressive sleaze from both the underground and the mainstream.
This screening will feature adult-themed content, including sexually explicit and risqué material. Please consider yourself forewarned that these films may (and probably will) contain offensive and upsetting content. Do not attend if you are of a sensitive disposition.

title: DON'T PLAY WITH FIRE
description: After a fatal hit-and-run, three high school friends flee the crime scene. They are witnessed by Pearl, a sadistic young girl, who pursues the group and blackmails them into more crimes, with increasingly disastrous consequences.

title: Joysticks             / Zapped!
description: There’s something going on at the local video arcade – something totally insane, outrageously hilarious, very sexy and thoroughly entertaining: the hit film Joysticks ! Will a local businessman (Joe Don Baker) succeed in shutting down this “den of juvenile delinquency” or will saner heads, faster fingers and shiny quarters prevail? Will leather-clad King Vidiot (Jon Gries) and his troupe of high-tech video addicts ever be satiated? Legendary exploitation filmmaker Greydon Clark distills everything great about the 80s (punks, nerds, valley girls, wild fashion, and Pac-Man) into one video game-fueled, late-night partyblast. Featuring extensive use of classic machines (Galaxian, Pole Position, Super Pac-Man, Satan’s Hollow), an all-time-great theme song and an epic battle against parental disapproval, this is a film for people totally into fun!

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: The Terminator
description: Disguised as a human, a cyborg assassin known as a Terminator (Arnold Schwarzenegger) travels from 2029 to 1984 to kill Sarah Connor (Linda Hamilton). Sent to protect Sarah is Kyle Reese (Michael Biehn), who divulges the coming of Skynet, an artificial intelligence system that will spark a nuclear holocaust. Sarah is targeted because Skynet knows that her unborn son will lead the fight against them. With the virtually unstoppable Terminator in hot pursuit, she and Kyle attempt to escape. 40th Anniversary restoration from a 4K film scan of the 35mm negative and a new Dolby Atmos mix with final sound and picture approved by director James Cameron. Presented by Park Circus with thanks to MGM. Post House: Park Road Post, Colourist: Tashi Trieu, Sound Mixer for Atmos: Mike Hedges

Another Terminator, the revamped T-800 (Arnold Schwarzenegger), has been sent back to protect the boy. As John and his mother (Linda Hamilton) go on the run with the T-800, the boy forms an unexpected bond with the robot.

title: 2 Pasolini
description: 2 Pasolini. 2021. Germany. Directed by Andrei Ujică. DCP. In Italian; English subtitles. 11 min. Sopralluoghi in Palestina per il vangelo secondo Matteo (Location Hunting in Palestine). 1965. Italy. Directed by Pier Paolo Pasolini. DCP courtesy Viggo. In Italian; English subtitles. 55 min. Andrei Ujică uses a Tupac Shakur song and Pier Paolo Pasolini’s documentary Sopralluoghi in Palestina (Location Hunting in Palestine) (put together as research for Pasolini’s 1964 film The Gospel According to St. Matthew) to interrogate the making and remaking of history. In his journey to the Holy Land in search of “authentic” locations for his Biblical epic, Pasolini, a heterodox Marxist Catholic, was bound to find a modern landscape inhospitable to the historical presence of Christ. And yet, precisely because he ended up filming instead in southern Italy only two years after Vatican II—a seismic moment of modern Catholic self-reckoning—Pasolini’s true masterpiece is a deeply personal confrontation with ideas of liberation theology, light/faith and dark/blindness, and the role of the artist in aesthetics and spirituality. The montagist Ujică deposits several elements of violent beauty into this dialectic: Christ’s jeremiad against the Pharisees and scribes, images of a tempest-tossed sea from a pair of films by Dominique Pipat, and Tupac’s prophetic “Hit ’Em Up,” which, with lyrics like “Who shot me? But you punks didn’t finish / Now you ’bout to feel the wrath of a menace,” evokes another defiant proto-revolutionary cut down in the prime of youth.

title: Ghost in the Shell
description: In this Japanese animation, cyborg federal agent Maj. Motoko Kusanagi (Mimi Woods) trails "The Puppet Master" (Abe Lasser), who illegally hacks into the computerized minds of cyborg-human hybrids. Her pursuit of a man who can modify the identity of strangers leaves Motoko pondering her own makeup and what life might be like if she had more human traits. With her partner (Richard George), she corners the hacker, but her curiosity about her identity sends the case in an unforeseen direction.

title: Funeral Parade presents "The Skin I Live In"
description: Funeral Parade is proud to present The Skin I Live In, Pedro Almodóvar’s psychological melodrama about surgery and obsession. After twelve years, prominent plastic surgeon Dr. Robert Ledgard has finally created a new form of damage-resistant skin, a breakthrough which could have saved his late wife. However, this modern miracle of medicine was only achieved through Vera, Ledgard’s captive and human guinea pig. Who is she? And what does she have to do with the doctor’s past? The Skin I Live In is a startling thriller which could have only come from one of queer cinema’s most singular voices. With intro from artist, filmmaker and author Maz Murray. IG: @maz_murray Site: www.mazmurray.com

title: Videograms of a Revolution
description: Videograms of a Revolution. 1992. Germany/Romania. Directed by Harun Farocki, Andrei Ujică. DCP. In English, German, Romanian; English subtitles. 106 min. In Andrei Ujică’s seminal collaboration with Harun Farocki, official broadcasts of Nicolae Ceauşescu’s iron rule over Romania seem an impotent sham in the face of on-the-ground, eyewitness accounts of his dramatic demise by ordinary citizens, some of them wielding video cameras. Over five chaotic days in December 1989, street demonstrations in the western Romanian city of Timişoara erupted into violence and brutal state recrimination across the nation. Civilians occupied the national television station in Bucharest while Communist party stooges, attempting to flee or shift blame, were rounded up and put on trial. The Ceauşescus, once fêted by Queen Elizabeth, Jimmy Carter, and Kim Il Sung, were found guilty of “genocide” by an Extraordinary Military Tribunal and executed on Christmas Day. Two days later, viewers in Romania (and throughout the world) tuned in to watch incontrovertible videotape evidence of their bullet-riddled bodies. Ujică and Farocki perform a forensic study of authoritarian propaganda at a climactic moment of flameout, when reality could no longer bend to a dictator’s pernicious fiction of prosperity, progress, and international stature.

title: SMOOTH TALK
description:
Fifteen-year-old Connie spends a hot Northern California summer escaping family tensions through beach trips, shopping malls and flirtations with boys. Restless, self-conscious and eager to enter the adult world, she catches the attention of Arnold Friend, a charismatic older stranger who arrives at her house while she is alone. What begins as smooth-talking seduction gradually develops into something far more threatening.
Adapted from Joyce Carol Oates’s short story Where Are You Going, Where Have You Been?, SMOOTH TALK gave Laura Dern her first leading role, opposite a deeply unsettling Treat Williams. Director Joyce Chopra captures both the excitement and danger of adolescent sexual awakening, shifting almost imperceptibly from sun-drenched coming-of-age drama into a tense and deeply ambiguous psychological thriller. The film won the Grand Jury Prize at the 1986 Sundance Film Festival.

description: “An intentionally elementary meditation on certain primary functions of film, that could be said to be at the roots of film editing as such – expectations, exploring the picture, perceptual memory, relationships between on-screen and off-screen space – all explored in a series of free-standing sequence shots of perfect simplicity.” –Noël Burch “This cinema ‘au feminin’ reminds us what the imperialist eye had repressed: different modes of editing impulses; what is seen and heard alters our perspective.” –Serge Daney, CAHIERS DU CINÉMA

title: NEVER AFTER DARK
description: A wandering medium, Airi spends her life guiding restless spirits out of the world of the living. Summoned to an isolated country house, she comes face to face with a grotesque apparition with powers that defy Airi’s experience. As she digs deeper into the house’s past, a secret comes to light — and Airi finds herself hunted by a far more unpredictable force. For the first time, her greatest adversary is not the supernatural, but the living.

title: Apocalypse Now : Final Cut
description: In Vietnam in 1970, Captain Willard (Martin Sheen) takes a perilous and increasingly hallucinatory journey upriver to find and terminate Colonel Kurtz (Marlon Brando), a once-promising officer who has reportedly gone completely mad. In the company of a Navy patrol boat filled with street-smart kids, a surfing-obsessed Air Cavalry officer (Robert Duvall), and a crazed freelance photographer (Dennis Hopper), Willard travels further and further into the heart of darkness.

title: EXHIBITION ON SCREEN: James McNeill Whistler
description: In an era of great change and great beauty emerged the character of James McNeill Whistler. Considered by some to be one of the great innovators of 19th century art, he was a contemporary of the Impressionists, much admired by Van Gogh and Manet. Boldly experimental and famously witty, Whistler disrupted the strict conventions of Victorian society in pursuit of a new cult of beauty, creating “art for art’s sake” and earning himself a place in the history of great art. He found a parallel between painting and music, and entitled many of his paintings “arrangements”, “harmonies” and “nocturnes”, emphasizing the importance of tonal harmony in his work. His most famous painting, Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1 (1871), commonly known as Whistler’s Mother, is a revered and often parodied portrait of motherhood. It is arguably one of the most famous paintings in history and this film will unveil the artist behind the art. Tate Britain is now holding the first major retrospective of Whistler in three decades. This blockbuster exhibition promises to reawaken the world to just how important Whistler is to art history, uniting world-famous masterpieces with rarely seen works. Exhibition on Screen will bring these stunning works and the incredible story behind them to cinemas around the world while the exhibition is still running, bringing this truly global artist to a global audience. This will be an unmissable chance to get to know this visually spectacular artist and the influence he has had on those who followed.

title: The Fifth Element
description: The Earth is about to be destroyed by a huge ball of fire racing toward the planet. Cornelius, an old monk, knows how to stop the burning sphere with the help of Korben Dallas, a taxi driver and former secret agent and a woman named Leeloo.

title: THE BLACK ROOM
description:
A serially unfaithful businessman rents a secret room in a Hollywood Hills mansion from a brother and sister, intending to use the space for his extramarital encounters. Unaware that his landlords are serial killers, he soon discovers that the women he brings to the room are being murdered as part of their own sinister scheme.
A strange hybrid of psychological thriller, horror, and erotic exploitation, the film combines sexual obsession, voyeurism, and gruesome violence with a bizarre blood-transfusion plot. Its low-budget atmosphere and unusual premise place it firmly within the oddball American exploitation cinema of the early 1980s.
A

title: EC: DAY OF WRATH
description: (VREDENS DAG) “Carl Dreyer’s art begins to unfold at the point where most other directors give up. Witchcraft and martyrdom are his themes – but his witches don’t ride broomsticks, they ride the erotic fears of their persecutors. It is a world that suggests a dreadful fusion of Hawthorne and Kafka.” –Pauline Kael

title: GANDAHAR
description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

title: Cabaret
description: In Berlin in 1931, American cabaret singer Sally Bowles (Liza Minnelli) meets British academic Brian Roberts (Michael York), who is finishing his university studies. Despite Brian's confusion over his sexuality, the pair become lovers, but the arrival of the wealthy and decadent playboy Maximilian von Heune (Helmut Griem) complicates matters for them both. This love triangle plays out against the rise of the Nazi party and the collapse of the Weimar Republic.

title: Memories of Murder [Salinui chueok]
description: In 1986, Park (Song Kang-ho) and Cho (Kim Roi-ha) are two simple-minded detectives assigned to a double murder investigation in a South Korean province. But when the murderer strikes several more times with the same pattern, the detectives realize that they are chasing the country's first documented serial killer. Relying on only their basic skills and tools, Park and Jo attempt to piece together the clues and solve the case in this thriller based on true events.

title: Gentlemen Prefer Blondes
description: In this 1953 musical comedy, adapted from Joseph Fields and Anita Loos’s searingly funny stage musical based on her 1925 novella, showgirl Lorelei (Marilyn Monroe) is resplendent in beautiful gowns, most notably in the pink satin dress designed by Travilla during the now-classic number “Diamonds Are a Girl’s Best Friend.” Lorelei is seen throughout the picture in jewel tones and literal jewels, carefully selected to play up the lush Technicolor cinematography lensed by Harry J. Wild. Both effervescent and timeless, this witty gem showcases Monroe’s brilliant comic timing as well as her vocal chops. Premiering in the middle of the actress’s career and released the same year as Niagara and How to Marry a Millionaire , Howard Hawks’s film helped to plant Monroe in the hearts of the American public, making her one of the most famous people in the US.

title: Goodfellas

He enjoys his life of money and luxury, but is oblivious to the horror that he causes. A drug addiction and a few mistakes ultimately unravel his climb to the top. Based on the book "Wiseguy" by Nicholas Pileggi.

title: Unknown Quantity
description: Unknown Quantity. 2005. Germany. Directed by Andrei Ujică. With Svetlana Alexiyevich, Paul Virilio. DCP. In French; English subtitles. 67 min. In this theatrical version of a gallery installation, the French philosopher and cultural theorist Paul Virilio and the Belarussian Nobel laureate Svetlana Alexievich, author of Voices from Chernobyl: Chronicle of the Future, grapple with the man-made tragedy of nuclear catastrophe and its implications for irrationality and fear in decision making and technological innovation. With shades of Andrei Tarkovsky’s Stalker—the heroic men and women who volunteered to contain the Chernobyl meltdown referred to themselves, in fact, as “stalkers”—Virilio and Alexievich venture into a black-box zone of epistemological and ontological uncertainty as they contend with human yearning and hubristic overreach, the myth of progress, and the awful, annihilating vastness of destruction in Chernobyl, seemingly as unfathomable as that of the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki, or perhaps even September 11.

title: When Harry Met Sally
description: In 1977, college graduates Harry Burns (Billy Crystal) and Sally Albright (Meg Ryan) share a contentious car ride from Chicago to New York, during which they argue about whether men and women can ever truly be strictly platonic friends. Ten years later, Harry and Sally meet again at a bookstore, and in the company of their respective best friends, Jess (Bruno Kirby) and Marie (Carrie Fisher), attempt to stay friends without sex becoming an issue between them.

title: Drunken Angel [Yoidore tenshi]
description: Thought to be the first depiction of the post-WWII yakuza, Drunken Angel is Akira Kurosawa’s first critical success and first directorial collaboration with Kurosawa regulars Toshirō Mifune and Takashi Shimura. Set in a snapshot of poverty-stricken post-war Tokyo, an uneasy bond is forged when alcoholic doctor Sanada (Shimura) diagnoses low-level yakuza Matsunaga (Mifune) with tuberculosis, nursing his health whilst reflecting on his own internal demons. Their relationship is thrown into turmoil when Matsunaga’s oath-sworn brother returns from prison, turning both men down a path of self-destruction and adversity. Drunken Angel is featured as part of Gangsters Have Feelings Too, a season exploring the sensitive gangster film. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: Kino: Fantasy (15*)

title: Preview: Slow Horses (15) Series 6 + Screen Talk
MY LAST INTERVIEW WITH ÉRIC ROHMER + GOUGNETTE
description: Jackie Raynal MY LAST INTERVIEW WITH ÉRIC ROHMER / MA DERNIÈRE INTERVIEW AVEC ÉRIC ROHMER 2010, 18 min, digital In 2009, just months before he passed away at the age of 89, Raynal recorded an interview with the great filmmaker Éric Rohmer, for whom she had served as an editor on several films, including SUZANNE’S CAREER (1963), THE BAKERY GIRL OF MONCEAU (1963), and LA COLLECTIONNEUSE (1967). This is an invaluable record of Rohmer and of his longstanding collaboration with Raynal. Jackie Raynal GOUGNETTE 2008, 44 min, digital “GOUGNETTE (‘disheveled’ in the Camargue dialect) is a tribute to the memory of my parents (who died in 1983 and 1995) – Resistance fighters during World War II and Communists in the South of France. Through filmed and audio interviews with my parents and people who knew them – recorded between 1979 and 2005 – this film retraces their lives within the context of their political activism.” –Jackie Raynal Total running time: ca. 65 min.

title: Matches and Days. [excerpt from work in progress]
description: Matches and Days [excerpt from work in progress]. 2027. Romania. Written and directed by Andrei Ujică. In Romanian; English subtitles. 12 min. MoMA premieres a work-in-progress excerpt from Andrei Ujică’s latest project, in which the Romanian filmmaker reflects on a lifetime of watching World Cup football and sharing this passion with his son and grandchildren. “Matches and Days will be an intimate and nostalgic cinematic essay, almost like a family album,” Ujică says, “as well as a meditation on football as a mirror of the struggle for the autonomy of art. The narrative will span the peak of the Pelé project, reached in the victorious 1970 final against Italy, and the tragic failure of the next great Brazilian generation centered around Zico, Sócrates, and Falcão in 1982 and 1986.” TWST / Things We Said Today. 2024. France/Romania. Directed by Andrei Ujică. DCP courtesy Minerva Pictures. In English, French, German; English subtitles. 86 min. TWST | Things We Said Today is Andrei Ujică’s personal reminiscence, created in collaboration with the writer Geoffrey O’Brien, about a watershed cultural and political moment: the arrival of the Beatles in New York for their August 1965 concert at Shea Stadium, which took place against a backdrop of racial upheaval, war, and poverty in the United States. This marked an inflection point in Ujică’s life as a teenager in a Romanian village on the border with Yugoslavia, offering a transformative glimpse of freedom beyond the Iron Curtain and an epiphany about the power of art to transcend the soul-crushing drudgeries, lies, fears, and punishments of life under authoritarian rule. Frenzied images of girls attempting to storm the Beatles’ press conference at the Warwick Hotel in Midtown Manhattan are juxtaposed with television and radio news reports of police brutality and resistance in the poor, neglected Black neighborhoods of Watts and Harlem. This study in jarring contrasts is deepened by 8mm home movies, unearthed by Ujică and his researchers on eBay, of a trio of sheltered white suburban girls visiting the New York World’s Fair on the same grounds as the newly built Shea Stadium in Flushing Meadows. Excerpts from Ujică’s own short story, “Isabella, the Friend of the Butterflies”—which the filmmaker wrote as a teenager in thrall to the Beatles’ White Album—and the animated, spectral presence of our two protagonists, a then-17-year-old O’Brien and Judith Kristen, the girl in the home movies, guide us through the wild and wooly summer of ’65.

title: LITTLE WHITE LIES PRESENTS A CELLULOID SURPRISE #2

title: THE FEMALE HAMLET
description:
A young woman named Hamlet returns home after studying drama in America to discover that her father has been murdered by her uncle, who has married her mother. After seeing her father’s ghost and learning the truth behind the crime, Hamlet decides to pretend madness in order to uncover the conspiracy and take revenge.
Metin Erksan’s adaptation transforms Shakespeare’s tragedy into a surreal Turkish revenge drama, replacing the Prince of Denmark with a female protagonist and relocating the story to a contemporary Turkish setting. Blending melodrama, experimentation, and elements of Yeşilçam cinema, the film offers a highly unconventional interpretation of one of literature’s most famous revenge stories.

description: Vidiots is easing our heartbreak over the loss of the eternal Goddess Dolly Parton with a special screening of her rootinest tootinest big screen musical extravaganza The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas .

title: Emma
description: Rachel Portman was the first woman to win an Academy Award for Music (Original Musical or Comedy Score) for Emma . An adaptation of Jane Austen’s novel, this romantic comedy stars Gwyneth Paltrow as the meddling but well-meaning heroine, whose matchmaking aims cause confusion and heartache in her circles. The film was also nominated for Ruth Myers’s costumes, and Portman would go on to be nominated two more times for her scores for The Cider House Rules (1999) and Chocolat (2000).

Witchcraft and martyrdom are his themes – but his witches don’t ride broomsticks, they ride the erotic fears of their persecutors. title: Magnolia
description: An epic mosaic of many interrelated characters in search of happiness, forgiveness, and meaning in the San Fernando Valley.

title: HOTEL NEW YORK
description: With Jackie Raynal, Sid Geffen, Suzanne Fenn, and Gary Indiana. “HOTEL NEW YORK can be seen as a description of a fight; the fight of an immigrant with her new city and the fight of a filmmaker with her desire to make films within precarious boundaries. In HOTEL NEW YORK Jackie Raynal plays and wins.” –CAHIERS DU CINÉMA “One day in New York, I took my linen to a small Chinese laundry. Then I forgot it for a few weeks. When I went back, the laundry wasn’t there anymore, the building had been demolished! I was haunted by the thought of my bedsheets gone forever with the laundry. This experience was the starting point for the NEW YORK HOTEL script. I wanted to write and make this film to show how everything is transient over there. Things change all the time and are immediately replaced, much quicker than in Europe. The story stemmed from my own experience and impressions as a foreigner. It’s a comedy-drama.” –Jackie Raynal, LIBÉRATION Preceded by: Éric Rohmer SIX IN PARIS / PARIS VU PAR…: PLACE DE L’ÉTOILE 1965, 16 min, 35mm-to-DCP. In French with English subtitles. Jackie Raynal was the editor on all of the short films that comprise the French New Wave omnibus film SIX IN PARIS, each of which focuses on a single Paris neighborhood. Arguably the highlight of the collection, Rohmer’s PLACE DE L’ÉTOILE spins a silent-comedy-like tale in and around the chaotic roundabout anchored by the Arc de Triomphe. “A film that is both perfect and unusual in form, closed in on itself, and that seems to have nothing to say, but which actually says everything. A pure diamond.” –Luc Moullet Total running time: ca. 75 min.

title: Mystery Movie
description: Don't miss our fan favourite MYSTERY MOVIE screenings! On a near weekly basis we will serve up a random mystery movie, with No Clues and No Hints as to what they will be. In 2026, we'll be presenting these as STAFF CURATED selections each and every week by our lovely Front of House, Duty Manager, and Projection Team! You can find the schedule below: --- Wed 29th July - Aya's Pick (120 minutes) Wed 5th Aug - Chloe's Pick (91 minutes) Wed 12th Aug - Liv's Pick (92 minutes) Wed 19th Aug - Julia's Pick (82 minutes) Wed 26th Aug - Chevy's Pick (112 minutes) --- You can find a list of every MYSTERY MOVIE we have ever screened HERE ; if a film is on this list, it is not eligible for future Mystery Movie screenings! --- Content Advice : As these films are a mystery, we aren't able to provide specific ratings / guidance on the film's content. We strongly advise that you take this into consideration before purchasing a ticket.

title: AAHHH BELINDA
description:
A young theatre actress named Serap agrees to appear in a television commercial for a shampoo called Belinda. During the production, she suddenly finds herself transported into the life of the character she was portraying, becoming Naciye, a housewife with two children. Unable to convince those around her that she is actually an actress named Serap, she struggles to understand her new reality and find a way back to her former life.
A surreal blend of comedy, fantasy, and social satire, the film uses its body-switching premise to explore identity, gender roles, and the expectations placed on women in Turkish society. Its shifting between performance and reality creates an unusual and often unsettling examination of how easily personal identity can be shaped by external roles.

title: THE THIRD PART OF THE NIGHT
description: Set during the Nazi occupation of Poland, in which Michał witnesses the murder of his mother, wife and child. He is hurled into a life that literally is not his own; a surreal world littered with trapdoors, doppelgängers and wormholes.

title: Peeping Tom             / See No Evil (1971)
description: “Ravishingly beautiful, a shock to the system, and an absolutely lucid picture about the danger of making art.” – Martin Scorsese

title: Mirror
description: Using a nonlinear structure interlaced with dreams and flashbacks, director Andrei Tarkovsky creates a stream-of-consciousness meditation on war, memory and time that draws heavily on events from his own life.

title: The Transformers: The Movie: 40th Anniversary
description: In 1986, THE TRANSFORMERS: THE MOVIE rolled into cinemas and changed the franchise forever. Unicron arrives as a planet-sized threat to the universe, heroes rise, legends are forged and an entire generation of kids were changed forever by THAT moment, which still hits like a truck. Featuring an iconic voice cast, unforgettable animation and a soundtrack that hadabsolutely no business going that hard, the film remains one of the boldest animated classics of its era. Now, forty years later, it returns to the big screen in 4K for a special anniversary celebration of the battle, the music and the legacy. Stay through the credits...because as this journey ends, a new one begins. Features 10-15 mins of never-before-seen exclusive content!

title: Onslaught
description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

title: Taipei Story
description: Edward Yang's second feature is a mournful anatomy of a city caught between the past and the present. Made in collaboration with Yang's fellow New Taiwan Cinema master Hou Hsiao-hsien, TAIPEI STORY chronicles the growing estrangement between a washed-up baseball player (Hou, in a rare on-screen performance) working in his family's textile business and his girlfriend (Tsai Chin), who clings to the upward mobility of her career in property development. As the couple's dreams of marriage and emigration begin to unravel, Yang's gaze illuminates the precariousness of domestic life and the desperation of Taiwan's globalised modernity.

title: Kiki's Delivery Service
description: Celebrate this beloved coming-of-age story from the legendary Studio Ghibli, creators of Spirited Away, and Academy Award®-winning director Hayao Miyazaki, about a resourceful young witch who uses her broom to create a delivery service, only to lose her gift of flight in a moment of self-doubt. It is a tradition for all young witches to leave their families on the night of a full moon and fly off into the wide world to learn their craft. When that night comes for Kiki, she embarks on her new journey with her sarcastic black cat, Jiji, landing the next morning in a seaside town, where her unique skills make her an instant sensation.

title: Onslaught
description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
description: The epic adventure centers around Indy (Harrison Ford) and his perilous quest for the Ark of the Covenant, a Biblical artifact of unspeakable power also sought after by Hitler's armies. In a race against the Nazis, Indy travels the globe in pursuit of the Ark, reigniting passions with his former flame Marion Ravenwood (Karen Allen), aided by allies Marcus Brody (Denholm Elliott) and Sallah (John Rhys-Davies), and thwarted by danger, double-crosses and enemies at every turn.

title: A Room in Town [Une chambre en ville]
description: In this musical melodrama set against the backdrop of a workers' strike in Nantes, Dominique Sanda plays a young woman who wishes to leave her brutish husband (Michel Piccoli) for an earthy steelworker (Richard Berry), though he is involved with another. Unbeknownst to the girl, the object of her affection boards with her no-nonsense baroness mother (Danielle Darrieux). A late-career triumph from Jacques Demy, Une chambre en ville received nine César Award nominations and features a rich, operatic score by Michel Colombier.

title: BLONDE DEATH (ON VHS)
description:
Shot on consumer-grade video and circulating for decades as a near-mythic underground tape, Blonde Death follows the runaway odyssey of Tammy, a teenage misfit fleeing an abusive home with two queer outsiders who christen themselves her new family. Their improvised road trip blends impulsive romance, petty crime, and manic self-invention, gradually collapsing into violence as the trio drifts further from stability. The film’s messy exuberance is threaded with a growing sense of doom, capturing the volatility of youth pushed to the margins.
A seminal artifact of queer DIY cinema, Blonde Death fuses melodrama, punk energy, and camp excess with unexpectedly sharp social commentary. Director James Robert Baker — better known for his incendiary fiction — uses the limitations of shot-on-video production to amplify the film’s immediacy and emotional rawness. The result is a rare, transgressive work whose jagged form reflects the precarity, rebellion, and desperation of its characters, standing at the intersection of outsider art and queer counterculture.
Programme notes by Dominic Hicks

title: Filipiñana
description: Join us in the microcinema for one of the best films of the year and a masterwork of international cinema – Rafael Manuel’s phenomenally composed deadpan social satire Filipiñana . With jaw-dropping shot composition, immaculate color coding, a biting and satiric wit, and a slow deliberateness that builds to a shocking ending, this is a dazzler on another level with class consciousness to boot. If Ruben Ostlund and Wes Anderson had a Filipino baby, it still wouldn’t be as good as Filipiñana ! Don’t miss your chance to see this stunner on a big screen!

title: THERE'S ALWAYS TOMORROW
description: When a toy manufacturer feels ignored and unappreciated by his wife and children, he begins to rekindle a past love when a former employee comes back into his life. Starring Barbara Stanwyck, Fred MacMurray and Joan Bennett.

title: PERMANENT VACATION
description: During her years running and programming the legendary Bleecker Street Cinema, Jackie Raynal discovered or premiered countless now-beloved films, not least of which was Jim Jarmusch’s debut feature, PERMANENT VACATION. For this special screening, Raynal will present the film in person, and speak about her early advocacy of Jarmusch’s work. “Jim Jarmusch’s first feature displays the first hints of the deadpan, minimalist-cool style that he would refine in his breakthrough STRANGER THAN PARADISE (1987). Young, alienated hipster Aloysius Christopher Parker (Chris Parker) wanders an eerily vacant Manhattan searching for a sense of meaning while encountering an array of idiosyncratic characters. Downtown fixtures Sara Driver, Eric Mitchell, and John Lurie (who composed the film’s score) are among the eccentrics and vagabonds populating this existential urban odyssey.” –CRITERION Preceded by: Jacques Rozier PAPARAZZI 1964, 23 min, 16mm-to-DCP. In French with English subtitles. “One of two documentaries Jacques Rozier made chronicling the making of Jean-Luc Godard’s CONTEMPT, PAPARAZZI focuses on the intense media frenzy that accompanied star Brigitte Bardot’s every move, offering a revealing look at the nature of modern celebrity culture.” –CRITERION Total running time: ca. 105 min.

title: Blades of the Guardians (鏢人:風起大漠)
description: Blades of the Guardians (鏢人:風起大漠). 2026. China. Directed by Yuen Woo-ping. With Wu Jing, Nicholas Tse, Sun Yizhou, Chen Lijun, Tony Leung Ka Fai, Kara Wai, Jet Li. DCP courtesy Well Go USA Entertainment. In Mandarin; English subtitles. 130 min. Yuen Woo-ping’s latest directorial effort is a sweeping wuxia epic set against the blazing expanse of the Taklamakan Desert, where a mercenary hired to escort a political fugitive finds himself caught between warring factions, relentless bounty hunters, and age-old rivals. Yuen turns the desert itself into a living combatant, pitting his warriors against the merciless terrain as much as one another. Every set piece is built on movement legibility and spatial clarity, delivering action of breathtaking scale without sacrificing precision. The ensemble spans generations screen royalty—Jet Li, Tony Leung Ka-fai, and Kara Wai alongside contemporary powerhouses Wu Jing, Nicholas Tse, and Max Zhang—all joined by a new generation of rising talent and performing actual combat following rigorous training in martial arts, weapons handling, horsemanship, and archery. The result is a relentless spectacle that reaffirms Yuen’s enduring mastery of cinematic action.

title: Fight Club
description: The first rule of Fight Club is: You do not talk about Fight Club . David Fincher’s stylized adaptation of the Chuck Palahniuk book is a darkly comic and intoxicatingly energetic screen thunderbolt, a visually striking, critically polarizing, and often misunderstood exploration of modern-day man, mischief, madness, mayhem and soap. Brad Pitt, Edward Norton, and Helena Bonham Carter turn in powerful performances, while the Dust Brothers provide a propulsive score.

title: Husbands
description: The quiet, simple family lives of Gus, Harry and Archie (John Cassavetes, Ben Gazzara, Peter Falk) are shattered when their best friend, Stuart, has a heart attack and dies suddenly. Now facing their mortality, the three men fall into their own midlife crises. First by spending their days playing basketball and nights drinking, and eventually by ditching their families altogether for a sudden getaway to London, where they face the temptation to cheat on their wives for the first time.

title: GO GO GO SLOW (book release event!)
description: This evening features a rare screening of John Smith’s SLOW GLASS (1988-91) – which uses the art of glassmaking as a prism to explore themes of memory and transformation – preceded by Marie Menken’s ode to New York City on speed, GO! GO! GO! (1964). Both films utilize layered imagery, in different ways, to alter our perception of time and space. The event celebrates the publication of “Frozen Features”, a new book of photographs by Jason Fulford. For nearly thirty years, Fulford has built a practice on the conviction that meaning lives less inside any single photograph than in the sequence and the things that happen around it – individual pictures forced to rhyme, echo, or collapse into dissonance against their neighbors, across books, exhibitions, publishing, and performance. “Frozen Features” pushes that instinct one step further, into a visual language of layers randomly composed from images made between 1996 and 2026. The results invite us to find the mystical lodged inside the everyday, felt before it’s understood. Fulford will introduce the films, and books will be available for purchase. For more info about “Frozen Features”, visit: https://loosejoints.biz/products/frozen-features Marie Menken GO! GO! GO! (1962-64, 12 min, 16mm, silent. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives.) John Smith SLOW GLASS (1988-91, 40 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 55 min.

title: Fringe! and Pink Palace: JOSIE & THE PUSSYCATS
description: Join Fringe! and Pink Palace for a 25 th anniversary screening of Y2K camp classic Josie & The Pussycats. For all the punk rock Prom Queens and Backdoor Lovers, we hope you DuJour this criminally underrated early 2000’s film just as much as we do! Let’s get subliminal and slip back towards the mille...

title: Showgirls 2: Penny's from Heaven presented by Frowzy Films
description: Screening at the Prince Charles Cinema and in the UK for the first time, Frowzy Films is proud to present SHOWGIRLS 2: PENNY’S FROM HEAVEN. The sequel to Paul Verhoeven's Showgirls, Showgirls 2 is written, edited, directed and produced by Rena Riffel (Showgirls, Mulholland Drive), who reprises her role as Penny in Showgirls and stars in the film. We follow Penny as she hitchhikes from Las Vegas to LA, desperate to become a professional dancer at the exclusive Stardancer club. However, she quickly descends into the city's seedy underbelly, encountering vicious dancers and manipulative men at every turn of her rise to success. Part INLAND EMPIRE, part 70s erotic film, part threadbare reimagining of the original, Rena Riffel’s vision was put together on a crowdfunded budget of just $30,000. Produced via consumer grade camera equipment, borrowed hotel rooms and guerilla filming, Showgirls 2: Penny’s From Heaven is a must watch for any fan of low budget cinema or the original Showgirls. This year marks the 15th anniversary of the film. This screening will include a prerecorded video introduction from Rena Riffel. Showgirls 2: Penny’s From Heaven is presented by Frowzy Films, co-curated by Molly Miles (Category H) and Pete Cann (Scour Cinema). Frowzy Films is a film club which explores microbudget genre cinema from a place of genuine love, putting small budget films on the big screen and celebrating them in a fresh light.

title: Daisies
description: Our screening on Thursday 8 October will be introduced by art historian and Fashion in Film Festival director Marketa Uhlirova. A…

title: The Transformers: The Movie: 40th Anniversary
description: In 1986, THE TRANSFORMERS: THE MOVIE rolled into cinemas and changed the franchise forever. Unicron arrives as a planet-sized threat to the universe, heroes rise, legends are forged and an entire generation of kids were changed forever by THAT moment, which still hits like a truck. Featuring an iconic voice cast, unforgettable animation and a soundtrack that hadabsolutely no business going that hard, the film remains one of the boldest animated classics of its era. Now, forty years later, it returns to the big screen in 4K for a special anniversary celebration of the battle, the music and the legacy. Stay through the credits...because as this journey ends, a new one begins. Features 10-15 mins of never-before-seen exclusive content!

title: THE BEAVER TRILOGY
description:
In 1979, filmmaker Trent Harris encounters an eccentric young man named Groovin’ Gary in Beaver, Utah, who invites him to film a local talent show where he performs in drag as Olivia Newton-John. Fascinated by Gary’s personality and performance, Harris later recreates the story twice more: first with Sean Penn in Beaver Kid 2 (1981), and then with Crispin Glover in The Orkly Kid (1985). The three films are combined into a single work that explores the life, dreams, and outsider identity of its central figure.
Part documentary, part fiction, and part experimental investigation into the act of filmmaking itself, the trilogy examines how a real person’s story changes when filtered through different performers and interpretations. A unique piece of underground cinema, it became a cult landmark for its strange blend of humour, empathy, performance, and questions about identity and representation.

title: Resident Evil
description:
From the mind of visionary filmmaker Zach Cregger (Weapons, Barbarian) comes a thrilling —and terrifying —reinvention of the Resident Evil franchise. In an all-new story, Resident Evil follows

Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos.

title: GANDAHAR
description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

title: Dream Emulator: BENEATH THE BLISTERED MOON
description: The blistered moon whispers a welcome to the eldritch abominations of a twisted internet. We’re wearing our love of all things cosmic horror on our shimmering sleeves tonight, this screening is a celebration of the myriad anomalous destinations digital culture has taken the otherworldly horrors popu...

title: Sexy Beast
description: Ex-villain Gal Dove (Ray Winstone) has served his time behind bars and is blissfully retired to a Spanish villa paradise with a wife he adores. The idyll is shattered by the arrival of his gangster nemesis Don Logan (Ben Kingsley), intent on persuading Gal to return to London for one last big job. Desperate not to sacrifice his enchanted existence, Dove is drawn into a shocking and explosive battle of wills with Logan, and takes part in a sensational underwater heist, risking everything to protect the woman he loves.

title: Resident Evil
description:
From the mind of visionary filmmaker Zach Cregger (Weapons, Barbarian) comes a thrilling —and terrifying —reinvention of the Resident Evil franchise. In an all-new story, Resident Evil follows

Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos.

title: Heat
description: Writer-director Michael Mann’s electrifying crime saga intertwines the fates of two disparate, desperate men in a taut cat-and-mouse thriller across the streets of Los Angeles. While an intelligent master criminal plans one last daring high-stakes heist, the investigating detective’s all-consuming obsession with the case threatens to engulf them both. Robert De Niro and Al Pacino sizzle in one of the great films of the ’90s.

title: Gentlemen Prefer Blondes
description: In this 1953 musical comedy, adapted from Joseph Fields and Anita Loos’s searingly funny stage musical based on her 1925 novella, showgirl Lorelei (Marilyn Monroe) is resplendent in beautiful gowns, most notably in the pink satin dress designed by Travilla during the now-classic number “Diamonds Are a Girl’s Best Friend.” Lorelei is seen throughout the picture in jewel tones and literal jewels, carefully selected to play up the lush Technicolor cinematography lensed by Harry J. Wild. Both effervescent and timeless, this witty gem showcases Monroe’s brilliant comic timing as well as her vocal chops. Premiering in the middle of the actress’s career and released the same year as Niagara and How to Marry a Millionaire , Howard Hawks’s film helped to plant Monroe in the hearts of the American public, making her one of the most famous people in the US.
director: Howard Hawks PRODUCED BY: Sol C. Siegel

title: There Will Be Blood
description: Ruthless silver miner, turned oil prospector, Daniel Plainview moves to oil-rich California. Using his adopted son HW to project a trustworthy, family-man image, Plainview cons local landowners into selling him their valuable properties for a pittance. However, local preacher Eli Sunday suspects Plainviews motives and intentions, starting a slow-burning feud that threatens both their lives.

title: Miracle Mile
description: After 30 years of searching, Harry has finally met the girl of his dreams. Unfortunately, before they even have a chance to go on their first date, Harry intercepts some chilling news: WWIII has begun and nuclear missiles will destroy Los Angeles in less than an hour!

title: Spirited Away (Japanese with English Subtitles)
description: Join us for a screening of the universally acclaimed and beloved animated film Spirited Away from Studio Ghibli and Hayao Miyazaki. A young girl, Chihiro, becomes trapped in a strange new world of spirits. When her parents undergo a mysterious porcine transformation, she must call upon the courage she never knew she had to free her family. A visually astounding feat of imagination and heart, this brilliant and beautiful film was the first non-English language film to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and is considered one of the greatest animated films of all time.

Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier who unwittingly finds himself in an action-packed, non-stop race for survival as one fateful, horrifying night collapses around him in chaos.

title: DON'T PLAY WITH FIRE
description: After a fatal hit-and-run, three high school friends flee the crime scene. They are witnessed by Pearl, a sadistic young girl, who pursues the group and blackmails them into more crimes, with increasingly disastrous consequences.

title: Drunken Master (醉拳)
description: Drunken Master (醉拳). 1978. Hong Kong. Directed by Yuen Woo-ping. Martial arts direction by Yuen Woo-ping, Hsu Hsia. With Jackie Chan, Yuen Siu-tien. DCP. Courtesy Swank Motion Pictures. In Cantonese; English subtitles. 110 min. Building on the runaway success of Snake in the Eagle’s Shadow (1978), Drunken Master, released the same year, reunited director Yuen Woo-ping and Jackie Chan, establishing kung fu comedy as a major genre and hastening Chan’s unstoppable ascendence. Chan stars as a mischievous young Wong Fei-hung, the legendary kung fu master who has inspired countless movies and television series. Yuen’s father, Yuen Siu-tien, once again plays opposite Chan as his kung fu teacher, subjecting the reluctant pupil to an unforgiving regimen of “drunken boxing.” Yuen’s action choreography transforms seemingly clumsy movements into dazzling feats of precision and athleticism. Chan’s extraordinary physical gifts and impeccable comic timing reach exhilarating heights in the film’s breathtaking fight scenes, securing his place as one of the screen’s most original action stars.

title: We Are Fugazi From Washington, DC
description: Created to commemorate the 20 years that have passed since DC-based post-hardcore band Fugazi’s last live appearance (November 4, 2002, at The Forum in London), We Are Fugazi from Washington, D.C. is a 96-minute movie comprising crowd sourced, fan recorded live shows and rare archive footage of Fugazi curated by Joe Gross, Joseph Pattisall and Jeff Krulik. Explicitly billed as a nondocumentary (tHISiSNOTaFUGAZIdOCUMENTARY,) the film pays tribute to Fugazi’s prowess as a live act — for old fans to remember and for a new generation to discover what they missed. This unique archival assemblage celebrates the fans and their cameras, as much as the band itself — a collision/ collusion of the ephemeral moment on stage, and the moments captured on camera.
director: Jeff Krulik, Joe Gross, Joseph Pattisall

title: April X
description: When his twin sister April (Lilly Krug) goes missing, Bax (Connor Storrie) searches every corner of their futuristic, post-Soviet cityscape to find her, ultimately descending into madness.

title: Closely Observed Trains
description: Our screening on Wednesday 9 September will be introduced by the close friend of Jiří Menzel: film critic, broadcaster, and lecturer…

title: Pump Up the Volume
description: Long live Pirate Radio and long live this bangin’ early 90s cult classic starring Christian Slater as a teenage airwave bandit! In Arizona, an introverted and insightful teenager, Mark Hunter (Christian Slater), finds an outlet for his viewpoints through a shortwave radio. Broadcasting as Hard Harry, Hunter uses his pirate radio show to rant against the injustices and hypocrisies taking place in the area, and in society in general. After a tragedy, his principal seeks to get Hunter off the air once and for all. So get ready to stick it to the man, and the FCC with this banger as we pump the killer soundtrack through our dynamite speaker system!

title: THE BIRDCAGE
description: In this hysterical comedy, Armand and Albert have built the perfect life for themselves tending to their gaudy Miami nightclub. But their pastel tranquility is shaken when Armand’s son announces that he’s getting married to the daughter of ultra-conservative Senator Keeley… and they’re all getting together for dinner! Can Armand and Albert transform themselves into Mr. and Mrs. Family Values in time? It’ll take the performance of their lives!

title: WORK IN PROGRESS / EN CONSTRUCCIÓN
description: Documenting the demolition of homes to make way for the M11 highway in East London, John Smith argues that BLIGHT “exploits the ambiguities of its material to produce new meanings and metaphors, fictionalizing reality through framing and editing strategies.” Though the houses are torn down and the residents move away, Smith also consecrates BLIGHT as an archive of visual and oral memory for the residents. Whereas BLIGHT is unambiguous in its representation of antipathy toward the destruction of a community, José Luis Guerín’s EN CONSTRUCCIÓN navigates the nuanced attitudes of people affected by infrastructural changes in a Barcelona neighborhood. In long-takes of (sometimes staged) interactions and crumbling walls, Guerín and his team of Pompeu Fabra University students capture a community being buried under the promise of a better future. Preceded by: John Smith BLIGHT 1994-96, 14 min, 16mm-to-digital. Collaboration with Jocelyn Pook. Total running time: ca. 145 min.

title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon(臥虎藏龍)
description: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon (臥虎藏龍). 2000. Taiwan/Hong Kong/USA. Directed by Ang Lee. Screenplay by Wang Hui Ling, James Schamus, Tsai Kuo Jung, based on the book by Wang Du Lu. Action choreography by Yuen Woo-ping. With Chow Yun Fat, Michelle Yeoh, Zhang Ziyi, Cheng Pei-pei, Chang Chen. 4K DCP courtesy Sony Pictures Classics. In Mandarin; English subtitles. 120 min. Ang Lee’s groundbreaking Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon reimagines the wuxia tradition as an elegant fusion of martial arts, romance, and philosophical drama. When a legendary sword is stolen, two seasoned warriors (Chow Yun Fat and Michelle Yeoh) pursue a young martial artist (Zhang Ziyi) whose rebellious spirit draws her into a world of love, duty, and danger. Yuen Woo-ping’s choreography transforms combat into an extension of character and emotion. Bridging grounded martial discipline with poetic, dance-like wirework, he staged some of the most memorable combat sequences ever filmed, including an iconic duel balanced high atop a swaying bamboo forest. The film became an unprecedented international phenomenon and earned 10 Academy Award nominations, winning four, including Best Foreign Language Film.

title: In-I In Motion + Q&A with Juliette Binoche
Mind Game
description: Nishi is a loser who has a crush on his childhood girlfriend. After an encounter with the Japanese mafia, he journeys to heaven and back, and ends up trapped in an even more unlikely place.
