Piana will be here in person on Fri & Sat for Q&As following the evening screenings; they’ll be joined on Fri evening by star Katy Bolger!

title: Everything Else Is Noise
description: A middle-aged composer allows her friend to use her apartment to film a television interview, opening up a quietly revealing space, in Nicolás Pereda’s feminist-minded domestic comedy, an expert blend of realism and subtle absurdity.

title: Electra, My Love
description: Janscó’s radically original, downright hypnotic retelling of the Ancient Greek myth against the backdrop of the puszta, Hungary’s vast, muddy plains, is among the long-take master’s most bravura stylistic performances, its 70-minute runtime made up of only twelve intricately composed shots. Reworking the tale of Electra and her ill use at the hands of Aegisthus—the man who loved her mother and murdered her father 15 years ago—Janscó produces a timeless meditation on tyranny and rebellion—and a resounding call to resistance. Part of Classical Cinema

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: Hong Kong Film Festival: DEADLINE
description: At the hyper-competitive Enshan school, students are kept in line by state-of-the-art AI surveillance technology and iSmart, a nationwide tech initiative that tracks performance and attendance. In the days before the elite school’s final exams, order descends into chaos when an anonymous note predic...

title: Life of Jorge Luis Borges
description: Argentinean filmmaker Mariano Llinás’s (La Flor, NYFF56) sorta-documentary about the life of Jorge Luis Borges tells the entirety of his life story by rummaging through rediscovered documents, poems, drafts, sketches, manuscripts, and clippings.

title: Drive
description: Driver is a skilled Hollywood stuntman who moonlights as a getaway driver for criminals. Though he projects an icy exterior, lately he's been warming up to a pretty neighbor named Irene and her young son, Benicio. When Irene's husband gets out of jail, he enlists Driver's help in a million-dollar heist. The job goes horribly wrong, and Driver must risk his life to protect Irene and Benicio from the vengeful masterminds behind the robbery.

title: TONEY W. MERRITT PGM 2: VIGNETTES / MINIATURES
description: FINE FRENCH PHRASES AND OTHER FABLES (1976, 4 min, 16mm-to-digital) FALL WORKS (1978, 3.5 min, 16mm-to-digital, silent) GREEN MOUNTAIN (1978, 1.5 min, 16mm-to-digital) EF (1979, 4 min, 16mm, silent) LONESOME COWBOY (1979, 30 sec, 16mm) NOTES (1979, 1 min, 16mm-to-digital, silent) THREE MASKED PIECES (1979, 1 min, 16mm-to-digital, silent) SMALL EVENTS (1979, 2 min, 16mm-to-digital) BY THE SEA (1982, 1.5 min, 16mm, silent) CONQUEST PIECE (1982, 6 min, 16mm) NOT A MUSIC VIDEO (1987, 7 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 40 min. Merritt will be here in person for both screenings, with the Q&As moderated by filmmaker Lynne Sachs (Fri, Sept 25) and writer and film programmer Yasmina Price (Sat, Sept 26).

title: Godzilla Minus Zero
description: An experience that demands the big screen, director Takashi Yamazaki’s follow-up to his triumphant, Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One is a supremely satisfying sequel with even more astounding effects choreography than its predecessor.

title: London
description: Sebastian Brameshuber draws a delicate, perceptive portrait of the contemporary gig economy with the story of a good-natured yet solitary driver in his early seventies who shuttles back and forth between Vienna and Salzburg alongside strangers met via a ride-share app.

title: Remake
description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

title: Program 2: Visible Invisible
description: This program includes James Richards’s Fevers, Artavazd Pelechian’s The End, Johann Lurf’s Forever…Forever, and the world premiere of Morgan Fisher’s Screening Room. Note: Screening Room will be included only at screenings in the Walter Reade Theater.
director: James Richards, Artavazd Pelechian, Johann Lurf, Morgan Fisher

title: Dazed and Confused – Dazed Day!
description: Air raid!!! Yes, it’s that time of year, join us and our besties down the block from Walt’s for Vidiots’ Fourth Annual Dazed Day ! Wiggle into your best bellbottoms and bring all your buds for a full day of Richard Linklater’s singular, stoney classic Dazed and Confused ! Our all-day Emporium Takeover features vintage pinball on freeplay courtesy of Walt’s, plus all-vinyl DJ sets, 16mm psychedelic celluloid mini-shows between screenings, all followed by a late-night screening of The Who’s tripped out pinball rock opera Tommy from the always audacious auteur Ken Russell!

title: The End of Violence
description: In Hollywood, the lives of a successful film producer, his wife, a police detective and a surveillance agent intersect after a botched abduction.

title: Halloween with John Carpenter
description: On Halloween night, 1963, in the small Illinois town of Haddonfield, 6-year-old Michael Myers commits a horribly violent act against his older sister. Fifteen years later, he escapes from a mental institution, returns to Haddonfield on Halloween, and stalks teenage babysitter Laurie Strode (Jamie Lee Curtis, in her feature film debut) while psychiatrist Dr. Loomis (Donald Pleasence) tries to find him. Released in 1978, Halloween is a pioneering slasher film that established Curtis as a scream queen. Driven by John Carpenter’s sharp direction and staging, coupled with the use of POV shots and his now-iconic, eerie piano score, Halloween went on to become one of the most profitable independent films of all time, leading to numerous sequels, reboots, remakes and many other adaptations.
director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Debra Hill

title: Goodfellas
description: Young Henry Hill (Ray Liotta), with his friends Jimmy (Robert De Niro) and Tommy (Joe Pesci), grows up in the mob and works very hard to advance himself through the ranks. He enjoys his life of money and luxury, but is oblivious to the horror that he causes. A drug addiction and a few mistakes ultimately unravel his climb to the top. Based on the book "Wiseguy" by Nicholas Pileggi.

title: Eddington
description: YOUR BEING MANIPULATED. It brings us no pleasure to report that, little more than a year after its release (and mixed critical reception), Aster’s fourth feature has “aged” extraordinarily well—which is to say, more and more people have come to recognize, in its astringent sendup of the lockdown era and attendant lunacy, one of the sharpest fictional depictions of terminally online America and its ever-increasing derangement. You’ve got Pedro Pascal as a small-town Justin Trudeau, Austin Butler as an off-brand Russell Brand, Joaquin Phoenix as a county sheriff of the Jim Thompson school, Antifa supersoldiers, Geronimo’s bones… What’s not to like? “[Eddington] was a meaningful script. You could already feel the depth, and you could feel the potential of what you could do with it… [Ari] can’t stand lies in cinema. In the way you film, you can lie a lot. You can cheat a lot. He doesn’t really work that way; he has to be true, and I love that.” —Darius Khondji Q&A with director Ari Aster and cinematographer Darius Khondji on Saturday, September 26th Part of Radical Chiaroscuro: The Work of Darius Khondji

title: The Boy Friend
description: When the leading lady of a low-budget musical revue sprains her ankle, the assistant stage manager is forced to understudy and perform in her place.

title: Stop Making Sense
description: Stop Making Sense stars core band members David Byrne, Tina Weymouth, Chris Frantz, and Jerry Harrison along with Bernie Worrell, Alex Weir, Steve Scales, Lynn Mabry and Edna Holt. The live performance was shot over the course of three nights at Hollywood's Pantages Theater in December of 1983 and features Talking Heads' most memorable songs.

title: HKFF: Shades of Silk & Shorts + Q&A
Program 3: Surface Noise
description: This program includes the world premiere of Simon Liu’s Procedures, Jonathan Seungjoon Lee’s Practice Towards Light, Laura Kraning’s Interwoven Intervals, Siegfried A. Fruhauf’s Flim Flam, the world premiere of Karissa Hahn’s Moored Shadow, and the world premiere of Cameron Worden’s Day One.
director: Simon Liu, Jonathan Seungjoon Lee, Laura Kraning, Siegfried A. Fruhauf, Karissa Hahn, Cameron Worden

title: The Devils
description: Ken Russell’s infamous adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s novel, about the apparent possession of a group of nuns after one (Vanessa Redgrave) accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, is at long last available in its full, uncensored splendor.

title: Misty Green
description: In the star-making performance at the center of Chris Rock’s L.A. odyssey, Rosalind Eleazar plays a former actress struggling to make ends meet in an unforgiving Hollywood. The marvelous supporting cast includes Rock, Adam Driver, Daniel Kaluuya, Anna Kendrick, and more.

title: Tommy
description: Our Dazed Day extravaganza continues with the most psychedelic cinematic rock opera of all time – Ken Russell’s mind-melting adaptation of The Who’s Tommy . Co-presented by our friends and neighbors at Walt’s Bar!

title: The War of the Worlds: Next Century
description: Poland, Christmastime. A band of hyperintelligent, bloodthirsty Martians take over the country and enlist hapless television newscaster Iron Idem as the voice of their propaganda machine. But when Iron dares to go off message, he makes an enemy even greater than the aliens—the state itself.

title: The Twilight Saga
description: ALL NIGHTER : FAQs, HOUSE RULES & TIPS TWILIGHT : High-school student Bella Swan (Kristen Stewart), always a bit of a misfit, doesn't expect life to change much when she moves from sunny Arizona to rainy Washington state. Then she meets Edward Cullen (Robert Pattinson), a handsome but mysterious teen whose eyes seem to peer directly into her soul. Edward is a vampire whose family does not drink blood, and Bella, far from being frightened, enters into a dangerous romance with her immortal soulmate. THE TWILIGHT SAGA : NEW MOON : Bella Swan is on the cusp of her 18th birthday and blissfully happy with her undead beau Edward Cullen. While celebrating her birthday with Edward's family of `vegetarian' vampires, a frightening incident convinces Edward that he's simply too dangerous to be around his sweetheart. He decides to leave the town of Forks in order to ensure her safety - leaving her behind, angry and depressed. THE TWILIGHT SAGA : ECLIPSE : Danger once again surrounds Bella (Kristen Stewart), as a string of mysterious killings terrorizes Seattle and a malicious vampire continues her infernal quest for revenge. Amid the tumult, Bella must choose between her love for Edward (Robert Pattinson) and her friendship with Jacob (Taylor Lautner), knowing that her decision may ignite the long-simmering feud between vampire and werewolf. THE TWILIGHT SAGA : BREAKING DAWN - Part One : At last, Bella (Kristen Stewart) and Edward (Robert Pattinson) are getting married. When Jacob (Taylor Lautner) finds out that Bella wants to spend her honeymoon as a human, he is horrified -- for Edward's passion could accidentally kill her. Bella does indeed survive her honeymoon, but a new complication arises when she discovers that she's pregnant -- and the child is growing at an alarming rate. The pregnancy sets the wolves against Bella and Edward, but Jacob vows to protect his friend. THE TWILIGHT SAGA : BREAKING DAWN - Part Two : Bella (Kristen Stewart) awakes -- as a vampire -- from her life-threatening labor, and her newborn daughter, Renesmee, proves to be very special indeed. While Bella adjusts to her new state of being, Renesmee experiences accelerated growth. When the Volturi learn of the baby's existence, they declare her to be an abomination and sentence the Cullens to death. Bella, Edward (Robert Pattinson) and the rest of the clan seek help from allies around the world to protect their family. ------------------------------------------------------------------------- NO ADMISSIONS TO THE CINEMA AFTER MIDNIGHT NO ALCOHOL PURCHASED FROM OUTSIDE IS PERMITTED IN THE BUILDING! AGE RESTRICTONS : This is strictly a 16+ event. Due to the event running through the night, anyone under the age 18 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian [aged 18+] for the full duration of the marathon.
director: Bill Condon, Catherine Hardwicke, Chris Weitz, David Slade

title: Chow Yun-Fat-A-Thon
description: ALL NIGHTER : FAQs, HOUSE RULES & TIPS Celebrate one of Hong Kong cinema's greatest icons with five defining performances from Chow Yun-fat, the charismatic star whose effortless cool, emotional depth, and unforgettable screen presence helped redefine the modern action hero. Together, these genre-defining classics capture the style, heart, and kinetic energy that made him an international cinematic icon and continue to influence action filmmaking around the world. CHOW YUN FAT-A-THON line-up: A BETTER TOMORROW (1986): A reforming ex-gangster tries to reconcile with his estranged policeman brother, but the ties to his former gang are difficult to break. A BETTER TOMORROW II (1987): A restaurateur teams up with a police officer and his ex-con brother to avenge the death of a friend's daughter. CITY ON FIRE (1987): An undercover cop infiltrates a gang of thieves who plan to rob a jewellery store. THE KILLER (1989): A disillusioned assassin accepts one last hit in hopes of using his earnings to restore the vision of a singer he accidentally blinded. HARD BOILED (1992): A tough-as-nails cop teams up with an undercover agent to shut down a sinister mobster and his crew ------------------------- NO ADMISSIONS TO THE CINEMA AFTER MIDNIGHT! NO ALCOHOL PURCHASED FROM OUTSIDE IS PERMITTED IN THE BUILDING! AGE RESTRICTIONS: This event is strictly 18 +

title: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
description: In director Wes Anderson’s offbeat adventure comedy, internationally renowned oceanographer Steve Zissou and his eccentric crew embark on an expedition to find the shark that killed his partner. Along the way, they’ll face pirates and personal difficulties, as well as a number of strange figures from Zissou’s past. The all-star cast includes Bill Murray, Owen Wilson, Anjelica Huston, Willem Dafoe, Jeff Goldblum, and more.

title: Hell Ride
description: Two rival bikers gangs, the Victors and the Six-Six-Six's, refuel their decades-old rivalry.

title: Godzilla, Mothra and King Ghidorah: Giant Monsters All Out Attack             / Godzilla 2000
description: Fifty years ago, the Japanese Defense Forces killed Godzilla… or so they thought. When a series of terrifying natural disasters begin to plague Japan, including the inexplicable offshore sinking of a U.S. submarine, a mystic old man warns his nation that Godzilla has come back to destroy Japan as revenge for all the souls lost in the Pacific War. When mere military might cannot squash the monster, the mystic man awakens the Holy Beasts of Yamato – King Ghidorah, Mothra and Baragon, sleeping giants that protected Japan in ancient times. These untamed mammoth beasts take on Godzilla with frightening supernatural brute power that has been 2,000 years in the making. Tradition and technology collide in this chilling high-tech, cutting-edge fable. (Sony Pictures)

title: Munster, Go Home!
description: The Munsters travel to England after Herman discovers he's the new Lord of the Munster Hall.

title: Harry and the Hendersons
description: Academy Award nominee John Lithgow stars in this big-hearted, big-footed family comedy. While returning from a trip to the woods, George…

title: Misty Green
description: In the star-making performance at the center of Chris Rock’s L.A. odyssey, Rosalind Eleazar plays a former actress struggling to make ends meet in an unforgiving Hollywood. The marvelous supporting cast includes Rock, Adam Driver, Daniel Kaluuya, Anna Kendrick, and more.

title: The Sacrifice
description: Andrei Tarkovsky’s visionary final film unfolds in the hours before a nuclear holocaust. Erland Josephson, in an award-winning role, plays retired actor Alexander who is celebrating his birthday with family and friends when a crackly TV announcement warns of an imminent nuclear catastrophe. Alexander makes a promise to God that he will sacrifice all he holds dear, if the disaster can be averted. The next day dawns and, as if in a dream, everything is restored to normality. But Alexander must keep his vow. Among many other awards, The Sacrifice won the Cannes Grand Prix in 1986, the same year that Tarkovsky died of cancer in Paris at the age of 54.

title: My Undesirable Friends Part II
description: In the expansive and equally intimate second chapter of her monumental documentary, Julia Loktev traces the paths of a network of fearlessly outspoken broadcast journalists endangered for dissent against the Putin regime across Europe and even farther afield.

title: Beauty and the Beast Sing-Along
description: Be our guest as we chime in and sing along to the timeless classic songs of Disney’s magical animated classic Beauty and the Beast .  Follow the adventures of Belle, a beautiful but restless bookworm who finds herself in the castle of a prince who’s been turned into a mysterious beast. With the help of the castle’s enchanted staff of anthropomorphic housewares, Belle soon learns the most important lesson of all — that true beauty comes from within. Lend your voice to this Tale as Old as Time and join in on the magic!

title: NAZA
description: Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the co-directors of the 2024 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land (NYFF62), NAZA reveals the systems behind Israel’s bombing of Gaza and its mass killing of Palestinian civilians.

title: Kiki's Delivery Service
description: Celebrate this beloved coming-of-age story from the legendary Studio Ghibli, creators of Spirited Away, and Academy Award®-winning director Hayao Miyazaki, about a resourceful young witch who uses her broom to create a delivery service, only to lose her gift of flight in a moment of self-doubt. It is a tradition for all young witches to leave their families on the night of a full moon and fly off into the wide world to learn their craft. When that night comes for Kiki, she embarks on her new journey with her sarcastic black cat, Jiji, landing the next morning in a seaside town, where her unique skills make her an instant sensation.

title: Program 2: Visible Invisible
description: This program includes James Richards’s Fevers, Artavazd Pelechian’s The End, Johann Lurf’s Forever…Forever, and the world premiere of Morgan Fisher’s Screening Room. Note: Screening Room will be included only at screenings in the Walter Reade Theater.
director: James Richards, Artavazd Pelechian, Johann Lurf, Morgan Fisher

title: Joyce/Snow: Rameau's Nephew by Diderot (Thanx to Dennis Young) by Wilma Schoen on 16mm
A Better Tomorrow III: Love and Death in Saigon
A Night at the Opera
description: The Marx Brothers take on the highbrow with full comedic force in one of their most beloved classics! With non-stop zingers, antics, gags, and fabulous musical interludes, this laugh-a-moment adventure posits Groucho as Otis P. Driftwood, would-be manager and opera producer trying (with Chico and Harpo as co-conspiring con artist stowaways) to kick-start the burgeoning careers and love lives of two young performers, making big Broadway bucks doing it.

title: Doctor Zhivago
description: John Box and his Oscar-winning production design team (art director Terence Marsh and set decorator Dario Simoni) built early 20th century Moscow on elaborate sets in Spain as well as created Zhivago’s unforgettable ice palace for this David Lean-directed romantic epic. The resulting adaptation of the novel by Nobel Prize-winner Boris Pasternak became a box office smash. Omar Sharif and Julie Christie lead the all-star cast, with Maurice Jarre’s score (featuring “Lara’s Theme”) receiving one of the film’s five Oscars, which also included Color Cinematography (Freddie Young), Color Costume Design (Phyllis Dalton) and adapted screenplay (Robert Bolt).

title: Off-Circuit: The Seasons
description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero
description: An experience that demands the big screen, director Takashi Yamazaki’s follow-up to his triumphant, Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One is a supremely satisfying sequel with even more astounding effects choreography than its predecessor.

title: Heil Jupiter!
description: This dreamlike astonishment from Carlos Reygadas (Silent Light, NYFF45) suggests a world balanced on the edge of the corporeal and the mythic—a work of feral cinematic expression that contrasts elemental pleasure and authoritarian brutality.

title: Program 1 The Hidden Dimension
description: This program includes the world premiere of Yixuan Zhang’s Branching Streams Flow in the Darkness, the world premiere of Josh Weissbach and Ben Balcom’s A Correspondence, Natalia Marín’s Chronicle of Tiredness, the world premiere of Jamie Crewe’s Rebecca’s Mess, and Tatsu Aoki’s Harmony.
director: Yixuan Zhang, Josh Weissbach, Natalia Marín, Jamie Crewe, Tatsu Aoki

title: La Haine
description: Hatred breeds hatred... 24 hours in the lives of three young men in the French suburbs the day after a violent riot.

title: It’s a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World
description: Buckle up for a carload of belly laughs with Stanley Kramer’s madcap comedy of treasure hunting starring a cavalcade of some of the best comedians of the day. Stanley Kramer’s first foray into comedy, this all-star laugh riot garnered 6 Oscar nominations. A group of strangers come across a man dying after a car crash who proceeds to tell them about the $350,000 he buried in California. What follows is the madcap adventures of those strangers as each attempts to claim the prize for himself. So join the treasure hunt and get ready to laugh for 3 hours straight in this all-time comedy bonanza!

title: How Deep Is Your Love
description: Our screening on 27 September will be followed by a q&a with director Eleanor Mortimor. Far out on the open sea,…

title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
description: After escaping prison, Ulysses, Delmar and Pete embark on a journey to find a hidden treasure. As lawmen pursue them, a new companion and a brush with antisocial elements turn their lives around.

title: Tibet Film Festival London: FAR FROM HOME + Q&A
description: A father’s fading memory and echoes of a free Tibet lie at the heart of this intimate family story. In 1959 the Dalai Lama escaped Chinese occupation to India, followed by thousands of Tibetans. Over six decades later, as TC Tethong—former deputy to His Holiness—begins to lose his memory, remarkable...

title: STRANGE BEHAVIOUR
description:
In a small Midwestern American town, a series of brutal murders begins after teenagers become involved in a mysterious behavioural experiment. As the killings continue, police chief John Brady investigates a connection between the crimes and a local university research project that appears to be manipulating the minds of young people.
A strange hybrid of slasher, science fiction, and paranoid conspiracy thriller, the film combines the atmosphere of 1950s creature features with the violence and experimentation of early 1980s horror. Its unusual mix of dark humour, bizarre scientific ideas, and Tangerine Dream’s electronic score has helped it develop a cult reputation among fans of offbeat genre cinema.

title: BO HARWOOD RECORD RELEASE EVENT: THE KILLING OF A CHINESE BOOKIE
description: This screening is presented on the occasion of the launch of a new LP devoted to the work of Bo Harwood (1946-2022), the composer whose music appears throughout John Cassavetes’s films and whose songs and compositions were often made with Cassavetes’s participation. The record brings together eleven recordings straight from the master tapes held by Bo during his lifetime, including music from THE KILLING OF A CHINESE BOOKIE, A WOMAN UNDER THE INFLUENCE, OPENING NIGHT, and LOVE STREAMS, as well as “Bach Train” and other compositions. The LP will be available for purchase at the screening (with a discounted price for ticket-holders). The event is organized by Yana Foqué, who initiated the project, with the support of the estate of Bo Harwood. It is hosted by Anthology Film Archives, with support from Grazer Kunstverein, where the LP will also be presented. John Cassavetes THE KILLING OF A CHINESE BOOKIE 1976, 108 min (1978 re-release version), 35mm Cosmo Vittelli (Ben Gazzara) owns a small Los Angeles strip club, the Crazy Horse West. After paying off a gambling debt to a group of gangsters, he finds himself in their debt once again. What begins as a night of obligation gradually pulls Cosmo into a world of violence, performance, loyalty, and survival. Cassavetes follows Cosmo through the clubs, restaurants, cars, and back rooms of Los Angeles, moving between the artificiality of the stage and the uncertain reality beyond it. With its long takes, abrupt shifts in tone, and performances that move freely between theatricality and intimacy, THE KILLING OF A CHINESE BOOKIE is one of Cassavetes’s most elusive and singular films. A classic, the film is graced by a peerless performance from Ben Gazzara as Cosmo.

title: SCREAMPLAY
description: Edgar Allan (Rufus B. Seder) is an aspiring screenwriter who has just come to Hollywood to make it in the movies…only to wind up working as the janitor at a fleabag apartment complex run by the greasy ex-boxer Martin (played by underground film legend George Kuchar). When Edgar begins channeling his frustrations with his kooky neighbors into fodder for his latest screenplay, the vivid murder scenes he writes begin to happen for real. As the bodies begin to pile up and the line between reality and fiction become increasingly blurred, Edgar, who is convinced that the only way to be a real writer is to suffer, is slowly driven mad. SCREAMPLAY is a marvel of campy charm, gothic horror tropes, and astonishingly inventive set design and special effects. Wearing its low-budget resourcefulness on its sleeve, but also genuinely atmospheric and transporting, the spell it casts is all the more remarkable given that it was filmed almost entirely within the confines of the 3,200-square-foot South End Boston loft where director Rufus Butler Seder and his Boston Black and White Movie Company (comprised of fellow students from the city’s School of the Museum of Fine Arts) had previously made a bevy of similarly inspired 16mm short films. Conjured from some of the earliest and still-most-effective cinematic techniques – matte paintings, scale models, ingeniously adaptable sets, animation, highly expressionistic lighting, and the good old-fashioned magic provided by charismatic performers (above all, Seder himself in the central role, and of course the irreplaceable George Kuchar, who broke his ankle during filming of the final fight scene) – SCREAMPLAY is a deliriously entertaining demonstration of the power of low budget invention, and a singularly charming (Boston) salute to Old Hollywood. Premiered (alongside BLOOD SIMPLE) at the 1985 New York Independent Film Festival, initially distributed by Troma (click here for details about our upcoming Troma series), but rarely screened in recent decades, SCREAMPLAY has been newly restored in 4K – scanned from Seder’s personal 16mm print – and is now back in circulation, where it’s poised to charm, delight, and frighten a whole new audience. Preceded by: Rufus Butler Seder IN THE CITY: A TRILOGY (LIVE IN FEAR; SUN RUN; PHANTOM SUBWAYS) 1977, 6 min, 16mm-to-DCP Writer, director, and star Rufus Butler Seder and producer and cinematographer Dennis M. Piana will be here in person on Fri & Sat for Q&As following the evening screenings; they’ll be joined on Fri evening by star Katy Bolger!

title: The Drift
description: An underseen and criminally overlooked work of the Nouvelle Vague, Paula Delsol’s first feature film, about a young woman’s encounters with a succession of different men, is a kind of modernist report on the state of women’s liberation in 1960s France.

title: The Devil
description: The screening on the 26th of August will be introduced by writer Michael Brooke. The screenings on September the 11th and…

title: Interstellar
description: In Earth's future, a global crop blight and second Dust Bowl are slowly rendering the planet uninhabitable. Professor Brand (Michael Caine), a brilliant NASA physicist, is working on plans to save mankind by transporting Earth's population to a new home via a wormhole. But first, Brand must send former NASA pilot Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) and a team of researchers through the wormhole and across the galaxy to find out which of three planets could be mankind's new home.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: La Gradiva
description: Director Marine Atlan’s exceptionally accomplished feature debut turns a high school trip to Naples for a group of French teenagers into a revelatory experience, capturing the intimacies of her youthful characters with pinpoint emotional precision.

title: THIRST
description:
Kate Davis is a wealthy young woman who is kidnapped by a secret organisation known as the Brotherhood, a society of self-proclaimed vampires who reveal that she is a descendant of the infamous Elizabeth Bathory. Taken to a remote facility, she is subjected to psychological conditioning as the group attempts to awaken her supposed vampire heritage and force her to accept their way of life.
One of the strangest entries in Australian horror cinema, the film reimagines vampirism as a modern underground society rather than a supernatural curse, replacing gothic castles with clinical laboratories, blood farms, and corporate-style organisation. Blending science fiction, horror, and social satire, it creates an unsettling vision of immortality, elitism, and control.

title: Remake
description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

title: A Day in the Life of Jo
description: Contemporary suburban Athens becomes the site of astronomical, ethereal beauty in Greek filmmaker Jacqueline Lentzou’s audacious film, which glances at the ephemerality of life with humor and poignancy as it charts a consequential day for 15-year-old Jo.

title: TONEY W. MERRITT PGM 1: PSYCHODRAMAS
description: PSYCHODRAMAS: MASKED FIGURES / MULTIPLE IDENTITIES WHAT’S THIS? (1973, 1.5 min, 16mm-to-digital, silent) A KISS OF DEATH (1974, 9 min, 16mm) 6 TO 8AM (1975, 30 min, 16mm-to-digital) EMBRACABLE YOU (1979, 5 min, 16mm-to-digital) ASIAM (1982, 5 min, 16mm, silent) WELCOME TO THE HOUSE OF RAVEN (1997, 3 min, 16mm) Total running time: ca. 60 min. Merritt will be here in person for both screenings, with the Q&As moderated by filmmakers Peggy Ahwesh (Fri, Sept 25) and David Sherman (Sun, Sept 27).

title: Program 4: The Real World
description: This program includes the world premiere of Calum Walter’s Certainties, Martine Syms’s RW-LO, Jesse McLean’s Placeholder, and Jiaqi Yu’s Moon Palace.
director: Calum Walter, Martine Syms, Jesse McLean, Jiaqi Yu

title: Monster-in-Law
description: It’s a battle of the icons when J. Lo faces off against Jane Fonda in this guiltless pleasure of cinematic bitchery! Office temp Charlotte Cantilini thinks she’s found Mr. Right when she starts dating gorgeous surgeon Dr. Kevin Fields. But there’s a problem standing in the way of everlasting bliss: Kevin’s overbearing and controlling mother, Viola. Fearing she’ll lose her son’s affections forever, Viola decides to break up the happy couple by becoming the world’s worst mother-in-law. If you need those rom com vibes to end your weekend right, we’re happy to oblige with this tasty slice of cinematic comfort food!

title: They Live with John Carpenter
description: When a drifter looking for work stumbles upon a pair of sunglasses that reveal the ruling class as a colonizing alien race, he sets out to expose and destroy the invaders. Roddy Piper and Keith David star as down-on-their-luck, working class men who discover that these undercover aliens are broadcasting subliminal messages, encouraging conformity and consumerism in a plot to rule Earth. Unabashed in its social and political commentary, They Live reflects John Carpenter’s distaste for Reagan-era politics and commercialism. Based on Ray Nelson’s short story “Eight O’Clock in the Morning” and scored by Carpenter, the film has developed a strong cult following and continues to find new fans with messaging that still resonates in our current political climate.
director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Larry Franco

title: HKFF: A Summer's Tale on 35mm + Q&A
Sirāt
description: A father and his son arrive at a rave deep in the mountains of southern Morocco, searching for Mar, their missing daughter and sister. Surrounded by electronic music and a raw, unfamiliar sense of freedom, they follow a group of ravers heading to one last party in the desert. As they venture deeper into the burning wilderness, the journey forces them to confront their own limits.

title: THE PICK-UP
description:
A pair of mob money couriers, Frankie and Tony, are transporting a package containing one million dollars when they encounter two women, Dana and Marcia, who trick them and steal the money. With the threat of their criminal employers hanging over them, the two men must track down the con artists and recover the stolen cash before they become targets themselves.
Lee Frost blends crime thriller, film noir, and exploitation elements in a gritty black-and-white story of betrayal, greed, and revenge. Featuring involvement from exploitation figures including producer and actor David F. Friedman, the film occupies the rougher edge of late-1960s independent American genre cinema, mixing a straightforward crime plot with the era’s emerging “roughie” sensibilities.

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: A Long Winter
description: High in the stark Mountain West, Mikey (Fred Hechinger) watches as his family slowly comes undone in Andrew Haigh’s (All of Us Strangers, NYFF61) beautiful yet forbidding 1950s-set tale of disappearance and growth, adapted from a Colm Tóibín story.

title: London
description: Sebastian Brameshuber draws a delicate, perceptive portrait of the contemporary gig economy with the story of a good-natured yet solitary driver in his early seventies who shuttles back and forth between Vienna and Salzburg alongside strangers met via a ride-share app.

title: Rose
description: Berlin’s Silver Bear winner for Best Leading Performance, Sandra Hüller fully inhabits the daunting role of a 17th-century woman who disguises herself as a male soldier, only to continue the ruse after battle, in Markus Schleinzer’s enthralling fable of faith and social intolerance. Austria’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Everything Else Is Noise
description: A middle-aged composer allows her friend to use her apartment to film a television interview, opening up a quietly revealing space, in Nicolás Pereda’s feminist-minded domestic comedy, an expert blend of realism and subtle absurdity.

title: Godzilla, Mothra and King Ghidorah: Giant Monsters All Out Attack             / Godzilla 2000
description: Fifty years ago, the Japanese Defense Forces killed Godzilla… or so they thought. When a series of terrifying natural disasters begin to plague Japan, including the inexplicable offshore sinking of a U.S. submarine, a mystic old man warns his nation that Godzilla has come back to destroy Japan as revenge for all the souls lost in the Pacific War. When mere military might cannot squash the monster, the mystic man awakens the Holy Beasts of Yamato – King Ghidorah, Mothra and Baragon, sleeping giants that protected Japan in ancient times. These untamed mammoth beasts take on Godzilla with frightening supernatural brute power that has been 2,000 years in the making. Tradition and technology collide in this chilling high-tech, cutting-edge fable. (Sony Pictures)

title: SCS: Rose of Nevada (15)
description: Thirty years after it was lost, a fishing boat reappears in its old harbour. Arthouse Cornish filmmaker Mark Jenkin creates an eerie coastal world lost in time.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Iron Boy
description: Winner of the Un Certain Regard Special Jury Prize at Cannes, Louis Clichy’s gorgeously hand-painted 1980s-set coming-of-age tale is a vision of rustic beauty and spiritual grace about an 11-year-old boy living with his struggling farming family in rural France.

title: Life of Jorge Luis Borges
description: Argentinean filmmaker Mariano Llinás’s (La Flor, NYFF56) sorta-documentary about the life of Jorge Luis Borges tells the entirety of his life story by rummaging through rediscovered documents, poems, drafts, sketches, manuscripts, and clippings.

title: Pelechian Project Program 1
description: Restored under the supervision of Artavazd Pelechian, now 88, these short films blur the categories of documentary essay and the poetic avant-garde.

title: Drive
description: Driver is a skilled Hollywood stuntman who moonlights as a getaway driver for criminals. Though he projects an icy exterior, lately he's been warming up to a pretty neighbor named Irene and her young son, Benicio. When Irene's husband gets out of jail, he enlists Driver's help in a million-dollar heist. The job goes horribly wrong, and Driver must risk his life to protect Irene and Benicio from the vengeful masterminds behind the robbery.

title: Manhunter : The Final Cut
description: A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a serial killer of families and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). The third feature written and directed by Michael Mann is a gripping adaptation of the first of Thomas Harris’s four novels featuring the iconic murderer, and benefits from the filmmaker’s typically striking visuals as well as a top-notch supporting cast , including Tom Noonan as the hunted killer, and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen (The Contender, 2000) as his blind love interest. -- This new 4K Final Cut, overseen by Mann, enhances the film’s depth, visual clarity and sound, offering audiences the ultimate immersive version. Shot in 1985, MANHUNTER was on a frontier in both its subject matter and film form, initiating an impressive list of subsequent films and series. “40 years ago – though armed with Thomas Harris’ excellent novel, “Red Dragon” – its subject matter, the profiling of serial killers, as well as being shocking and raw, was unknown. When adapting, I wanted to make its storytelling deliver audiences into a certain state of threat and emotional engagement. Integral to that was the visualization and use of music with lyrics sometimes working like a libretto. We have carefully remastered the film to try to evoke that mood and intensity, heightened with audio sourced from the original 5.1 35mm analog masters. This latest iteration is that version of the film with which I’m most satisfied.” said director Michael Mann. Under the guidance of Mann, this 4K scan of the original 35mm negative – with a few shots from an interpositive - was conformed and digitally restored at L’Immagine Ritrovata in Bologna. Both the theatrical version and the UHD HDR & SDR video color gradings were performed by Stefan Sonnenfeld at Company 3 in Los Angeles with the director. Sound restoration was done at Audio Mechanics from an original 35mm magnetic 6-track printmaster to release a new 5.1 mix by Luke Schwartzweller at Fox . Technical coordination and deliveries were managed by L’Immagine Ritrovata . This project was supervised by Becca Mann and STUDIOCANAL team, Jean-Pierre Boiget and Delphine Roussel . For Michael Mann, the process is about renewing the film’s immediacy for contemporary audiences: “If the picture was left the way it was, it would be interesting, but you’d feel some distance …you’d be observing it somewhat. I’m more interested in its original intent impacting you the same way it may have in 1986…that is, to bring you into it again in the original way.” As a film distinguished by its striking visual style, including Colleen Attwood’s costume design, Academy Award- winner Mel Bourne’s art direction, Dante Spinotti’s lighting, Mann worked with his long-time collaborator, Stefan Sonnenfeld (Company 3), to develop a new color grade for ‘The Final Cut’ that engages a contemporary audience while honoring the film’s lasting legacy. “A good example is the use of primaries and secondaries in combinations that don’t occur in nature for an unsettling ambiance or the use of blue for night-time imagery. We’ve changed values subtly sometimes, but significantly, to enhance the impact without changing the dramatic intent of the film,” said Stefan Sonnenfeld. He adds: “Michael… wants you to understand the story and the mood and the environment… and then asks you to interpret that in colour… He also tells you what emotion he’s trying to evoke from the scene.” The new version also introduces an HDR presentation, offering an intensified new experience. “So that nobody’s ever seen the movie like that,” noted Sonnenfeld.

title: Marketa Lazarová
description: Our screening on Friday 9 October will be introduced by Czech film expert Peter Hames. Voted the best Czech film ever…

title: Just Like Weather
description: A fascinating, ahead-of-its-time synthesis of fiction and documentary, Allen Fong’s third feature follows a couple from Hong Kong as they navigate domestic trials and tribulations before eventually heading to the United States.

title: River of No Return
description: Marilyn Monroe’s appearance in Western genre films required designer Travilla to create costumes ranging from saloon-style gowns to casual denim looks. Monroe wanted her character, Kay—a kind-hearted saloon singer torn between an ex-convict (Robert Mitchum) and her troubled fiancé (Rory Calhoun)—to have a natural feel. Her acting coach, Natasha Lytess, and director Otto Preminger clashed over whether Monroe should use her typical breathy voice, with the studio backing Monroe’s decision to forgo it.
director: Otto Preminger PRODUCED BY: Stanley Rubin

title: La Gradiva
description: Director Marine Atlan’s exceptionally accomplished feature debut turns a high school trip to Naples for a group of French teenagers into a revelatory experience, capturing the intimacies of her youthful characters with pinpoint emotional precision.

title: Only God Forgives
description: Nicolas Winding Refn (Drive) and Ryan Gosling (The Place Beyond the Pines) reunite in the highly acclaimed Only God Forgives - a stylish, mesmerising and thrilling journey through Bangkok's criminal underworld. Julian (Gosling) runs a boxing club as a front for a drugs operation. He has everything he wants and is respected in the criminal underworld, though deep inside he feels empty. When Julian's brother is murdered, his mother (Kristin Scott Thomas, Salmon Fishing in the Yemen) - the head of a powerful criminal organisation - arrives in Bangkok to collect her son's body. Furious with grief, she dispatches Julian to find his killers and 'raise hell'. The stage is set for a bloody journey of betrayal and vengeance, culminating in a final confrontation and the possibility of redemption.

title: A Long Winter
description: High in the stark Mountain West, Mikey (Fred Hechinger) watches as his family slowly comes undone in Andrew Haigh’s (All of Us Strangers, NYFF61) beautiful yet forbidding 1950s-set tale of disappearance and growth, adapted from a Colm Tóibín story.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
description: Jodie Foster stars as Clarice Starling, a top student at the FBI's training academy. Jack Crawford (Scott Glenn) wants Clarice to interview Dr. Hannibal Lecter (Anthony Hopkins), a brilliant psychiatrist who is also a violent psychopath, serving life behind bars for various acts of murder and cannibalism. Crawford believes that Lecter may have insight into a case and that Starling, as an attractive young woman, may be just the bait to draw him out.

title: Dragonslayer
description: * ON SALE 14th SEPT * A sorcerer and his apprentice are on a mission to kill an evil dragon to save the King’s daughter from being sacrificed according to a pact that the King himself made with the dragon to protect his kingdom.

title: Heil Jupiter!
description: This dreamlike astonishment from Carlos Reygadas (Silent Light, NYFF45) suggests a world balanced on the edge of the corporeal and the mythic—a work of feral cinematic expression that contrasts elemental pleasure and authoritarian brutality.

title: Tender Loving Care
description: Mike Leigh’s portrayal of overwhelmed, resilient lives in post-Brexit England should be received as one of his signature works, a film with a leveling sense of humor about the difficulty of asking for—and accepting—help in a world that continually lets us down.

title: Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair
description: Tarantino’s Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair unites Volume 1 and Volume 2 into a single, unrated epic—presented exactly as he intended, complete with a new, never-before-seen anime sequence. Uma Thurman stars as The Bride, left for dead after her former boss and lover Bill ambushes her wedding rehearsal, shooting her in the head and stealing her unborn child. To exact her vengeance, she must first hunt down the four remaining members of the Deadly Viper Assassination Squad before confronting Bill himself. With its operatic scope, relentless action, and iconic style, The Whole Bloody Affair stands as one of cinema’s definitive revenge sagas—rarely shown in its complete form and now presented with a classic intermission.

title: In Which Annie Gives It Those
description: Featuring the first screenplay by Indian writer Arundhati Roy (who stars as the titular protagonist’s nonconformist friend), Pradip Krishen’s English-language film bounces between hope and cynicism to form a sharp portrait of youth in 1970s New Delhi.

title: Hong Kong Film Festival: MY NAME AIN'T SUZIE
description: In recent years, Angie Chen has been rightfully recognised as a much overlooked contributor to the innovative Hong Kong New Wave of the 1980s. Her second feature was conceived to disenchant the orientalist fairytale of bar hostesses in the Hollywood romance drama The World of Suzie Wong (1960), whic...

title: CRAZY LIPS
description:
After her brother is accused of murdering four people, Satomi Kurahashi desperately searches for a way to prove his innocence. She turns to a mysterious psychic for help, but the investigation quickly spirals into a bizarre series of supernatural events involving disturbing visions, strange rituals, and revelations that go far beyond a simple murder case.
Hirohisa Sasaki’s film is an outrageous collision of horror, comedy, action, and exploitation, pushing Japanese genre cinema into deliberately chaotic territory. Mixing supernatural mystery, grotesque imagery, and absurd humour, it plays like a fever dream of late-1990s/early-2000s underground horror rather than a conventional thriller.

title: SCREAMPLAY
description: Edgar Allan (Rufus B. Seder) is an aspiring screenwriter who has just come to Hollywood to make it in the movies…only to wind up working as the janitor at a fleabag apartment complex run by the greasy ex-boxer Martin (played by underground film legend George Kuchar). When Edgar begins channeling his frustrations with his kooky neighbors into fodder for his latest screenplay, the vivid murder scenes he writes begin to happen for real. As the bodies begin to pile up and the line between reality and fiction become increasingly blurred, Edgar, who is convinced that the only way to be a real writer is to suffer, is slowly driven mad. SCREAMPLAY is a marvel of campy charm, gothic horror tropes, and astonishingly inventive set design and special effects. Wearing its low-budget resourcefulness on its sleeve, but also genuinely atmospheric and transporting, the spell it casts is all the more remarkable given that it was filmed almost entirely within the confines of the 3,200-square-foot South End Boston loft where director Rufus Butler Seder and his Boston Black and White Movie Company (comprised of fellow students from the city’s School of the Museum of Fine Arts) had previously made a bevy of similarly inspired 16mm short films. Conjured from some of the earliest and still-most-effective cinematic techniques – matte paintings, scale models, ingeniously adaptable sets, animation, highly expressionistic lighting, and the good old-fashioned magic provided by charismatic performers (above all, Seder himself in the central role, and of course the irreplaceable George Kuchar, who broke his ankle during filming of the final fight scene) – SCREAMPLAY is a deliriously entertaining demonstration of the power of low budget invention, and a singularly charming (Boston) salute to Old Hollywood. Premiered (alongside BLOOD SIMPLE) at the 1985 New York Independent Film Festival, initially distributed by Troma (click here for details about our upcoming Troma series), but rarely screened in recent decades, SCREAMPLAY has been newly restored in 4K – scanned from Seder’s personal 16mm print – and is now back in circulation, where it’s poised to charm, delight, and frighten a whole new audience. Piana will be here in person on Fri & Sat for Q&As following the evening screenings; they’ll be joined on Fri evening by star Katy Bolger!

title: Program 3: Surface Noise
description: This program includes the world premiere of Simon Liu’s Procedures, Jonathan Seungjoon Lee’s Practice Towards Light, Laura Kraning’s Interwoven Intervals, Siegfried A. Fruhauf’s Flim Flam, the world premiere of Karissa Hahn’s Moored Shadow, and the world premiere of Cameron Worden’s Day One.
director: Simon Liu, Jonathan Seungjoon Lee, Laura Kraning, Siegfried A. Fruhauf, Karissa Hahn, Cameron Worden

title: Wet Hot American Summer: World Theatrical Premiere of the Fart Cut
description: Look man, some of us need to fuck a fridge, right? This is a competitor for world’s greatest film and truly an honour to screen . Summer camps rule: you make-out, eat some shitty beans and swim in the lake Jason Voorhees will inevitablty rise from.

title: Assault on Precinct 13 with John Carpenter
description: John Carpenter's Assault on Precinct 13 locks audiences inside a decommissioned South Central Los Angeles police station while Street Thunder gang members exact revenge against the LAPD. Lieutenant Ethan Bishop (Austin Stoker) is in charge of three convicts, a startled, silent citizen, and a strong-willed secretary as the gang outside their doors wreaks mayhem. Carpenter's direction leads with his own score of high-intensity synthesizer music accompanying Bishop on his crusade to heroism.
director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: J. Stein Kaplan

title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King [Theatrical Cut]
description: As armies mass for a final battle that will decide the fate of the world--and powerful, ancient forces of Light and Dark compete to determine the outcome--one member of the Fellowship of the Ring is revealed as the noble heir to the throne of the Kings of Men. Yet, the sole hope for triumph over evil lies with a brave hobbit, Frodo, who, accompanied by his loyal friend Sam and the hideous, wretched Gollum, ventures deep into the very dark heart of Mordor on his seemingly impossible quest to destroy the Ring of Power.​

title: The Unknown
description: After an impulsive hookup, a Parisian photographer (Niels Schneider) finds that he has somehow swapped bodies with a German actress (Léa Seydoux). Arthur Harari treats this wild metaphysical gambit with the utmost sincerity in this uncanny supernatural drama.

title: GORE FROM OUTER SPACE
description:
A woman named Lucy is sentenced to death for the murder of her daughter, but as she tells her story to a nun, a bizarre chain of events is revealed involving a psychic, a corrupt politician, and two FBI agents investigating a strange alien presence. As the mystery unfolds, the boundaries between reality, science fiction, horror, and absurd comedy become increasingly blurred.
A sequel of sorts to Hirohisa Sasaki’s Crazy Lips (2000), this wildly eccentric Japanese genre mash-up combines alien invasion, horror, comedy, and surreal absurdity. With appearances from cult Japanese filmmakers and actors including Kiyoshi Kurosawa and Hideo Nakata, it plays like an intentionally chaotic parody of UFO movies, police thrillers, and exploitation cinema.

title: Yesterday Girl
description: One of the foundational films of the New German Cinema, the debut feature by the polymath artist and writer Alexander Kluge, about an East German woman’s acclimating to life on the other side of the wall, is a defining work of midcentury cinematic modernism.

title: My Wife Cries
description: Angela Schanelec’s (Music, NYFF62) formally audacious portrait of contemporary anxieties around love, gender, and trauma concerns a withdrawn construction worker whose wife reveals a shocking truth, upending perceptions about their seemingly comfortable marriage.

title: Program 5: The Material Ghost
description: This program includes Peggy Ahwesh’s The Wayfinders, Kevin Jerome Everson’s National Seating, the world premiere of Adam Piron’s The Flesh of the Mountain, and Bani Khoshnoudi’s Elegy for the Forgotten, On an Endless War.
director: Peggy Ahwesh, Kevin Jerome Everson, Adam Piron, Bani Khoshnoudi

title: Ride Clear of Diablo             / Six Black Horses
description: Audie Murphy stars in this action-packed western filled with adventure and romance. Clay O’Mara (Murphy) is out for revenge as he pursues the rustlers who murdered his father and brother. Along the way, he arrests and later befriends gunslinger Whitey Kincaid (Dan Duryea). Together, they face a gang of their enemies and dole out their own brand of justice. (Universal)

title: All That Jazz
description: When he is not planning for his upcoming stage musical or working on his Hollywood film, choreographer/director Joe Gideon (Roy Scheider) is popping pills and sleeping with a seemingly endless line of women. The physical and mental stress begins to take a toll on the ragged perfectionist. Soon, he must decide whether or not his non-stop work schedule and hedonistic lifestyle are worth risking his life. The film is a semi-autobiographical tale written and directed by the legendary Bob Fosse.

title: The Unknown
description: After an impulsive hookup, a Parisian photographer (Niels Schneider) finds that he has somehow swapped bodies with a German actress (Léa Seydoux). Arthur Harari treats this wild metaphysical gambit with the utmost sincerity in this uncanny supernatural drama.

title: Chungking Express
description: Every day, Cop 223 (Takeshi Kaneshiro) buys a can of pineapple with an expiration date of May 1, symbolizing the day he'll get over his lost love. He's also got his eye on a mysterious woman in a blond wig (Brigitte Lin), oblivious of the fact she's a drug dealer. Cop 663 (Tony Leung Chiu Wai) is distraught with heartbreak over a breakup. But when his ex drops a spare set of his keys at a local cafe, a waitress (Faye Wong) lets herself into his apartment and spruces up his life.

title: A Day in the Life of Jo
description: Contemporary suburban Athens becomes the site of astronomical, ethereal beauty in Greek filmmaker Jacqueline Lentzou’s audacious film, which glances at the ephemerality of life with humor and poignancy as it charts a consequential day for 15-year-old Jo.

title: Murder by Death
description: Five famous literary detective characters and their sidekicks are invited to a bizarre mansion to solve an even stranger mystery.

title: Boris Godunov
description: The screening on October 5th will be introduced by writer Daniel Bird. There will be a special screening of Boris Godunov on…

title: London
description: Sebastian Brameshuber draws a delicate, perceptive portrait of the contemporary gig economy with the story of a good-natured yet solitary driver in his early seventies who shuttles back and forth between Vienna and Salzburg alongside strangers met via a ride-share app.

title: In Which Annie Gives It Those
description: Featuring the first screenplay by Indian writer Arundhati Roy (who stars as the titular protagonist’s nonconformist friend), Pradip Krishen’s English-language film bounces between hope and cynicism to form a sharp portrait of youth in 1970s New Delhi.

title: Fallen Angels
description: An assassin goes through obstacles as he attempts to escape his violent lifestyle despite the opposition of his partner, who is secretly attracted to him.

title: Marathon Man
description: Babe Levy, a history student, tragically sees his older brother die in his arms. The ensuing investigation soon thrusts him into a deadly conspiracy involving smuggled diamonds and a war criminal.

title: Making Marie Antoinette
description: Sofia Coppola’s dynamic craftsmanship in creating her personal vision for 2006’s Marie Antoinette (NYFF44) is on full display in this video diary shot by her mother, Eleanor Coppola, on the film’s set in Versailles in 2005. Preceded by Kleber Mendonça Filho’s South of Tehran.

title: Program 4: The Real World
description: This program includes the world premiere of Calum Walter’s Certainties, Martine Syms’s RW-LO, Jesse McLean’s Placeholder, and Jiaqi Yu’s Moon Palace.
director: Calum Walter, Martine Syms, Jesse McLean, Jiaqi Yu

title: Tender Loving Care
description: Mike Leigh’s portrayal of overwhelmed, resilient lives in post-Brexit England should be received as one of his signature works, a film with a leveling sense of humor about the difficulty of asking for—and accepting—help in a world that continually lets us down.

title: Casablanca
description: Rick Blaine (Humphrey Bogart), who owns a nightclub in Casablanca, discovers his old flame Ilsa (Ingrid Bergman) is in town with her husband, Victor Laszlo (Paul Henreid). Laszlo is a famed rebel, and with Germans on his tail, Ilsa knows Rick can help them get out of the country.

title: My Wife Cries
description: Angela Schanelec’s (Music, NYFF62) formally audacious portrait of contemporary anxieties around love, gender, and trauma concerns a withdrawn construction worker whose wife reveals a shocking truth, upending perceptions about their seemingly comfortable marriage.

title: Kino: The Beauty of the Donkey (12A*)
description: Documentary filmmaker Dea Gjinovci captures her father’s return to Kosova and the memories the journey evokes after sixty years of exile.

title: Batman: Mask of the Phantasm
description: Andrea Beaumont leaves her father to return to Gotham, rekindling an old romance with Bruce Wayne. At the same time, a mysterious figure begins to hunt down Gotham's criminals, wrongly implicating Batman in the murders. Now on the run from the law, Batman must find and stop the culprit, while also navigating his relationship with Andrea.

title: Remake
description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

title: THE HEROIC TRIO
description:
Newborn babies are disappearing across a nameless city, abducted by the Invisible Woman and delivered to a monstrous underground master searching for an imperial heir. Standing in her way are Wonder Woman, a masked vigilante hiding her identity from her police-inspector husband, and Thief Catcher, a shotgun-wielding mercenary willing to work for whoever pays. As their shared histories emerge, the three women are drawn together against an enemy commanding an army of killers beneath the city.
Michelle Yeoh, Anita Mui and Maggie Cheung join forces in Johnnie To’s delirious collision of superhero fantasy, wuxia action, gothic horror and Hong Kong New Wave style. Produced and choreographed by Ching Siu-tung, THE HEROIC TRIO tears through motorcycle stunts, invisibility cloaks, flying blades, cannibalistic henchmen and spectacular wirework with the untamed invention of Hong Kong cinema at its early-1990s peak.

title: LRB/London Reviewed: I Hired a Contract Killer (1990) with Owen Hatherley
description: The penultimate film in the current season of LRB Screen, which explores visions of London created by non-British filmmakers, is the…

title: La Gradiva
description: Director Marine Atlan’s exceptionally accomplished feature debut turns a high school trip to Naples for a group of French teenagers into a revelatory experience, capturing the intimacies of her youthful characters with pinpoint emotional precision.

title: Silence
description: In the 17th century, two Portuguese Jesuit priests travel to Japan in an attempt to locate their mentor, who is rumoured to have committed apostasy, and to propagate Catholicism.

title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
description: In 1972, legendary filmmaker William Greaves gathered an extraordinary group of artists, writers, actors, musicians, and thinkers of the Harlem Renaissance. After more than 50 years, his son David Greaves has completed his breathtaking miracle of a movie.

title: All About Lily Chou-Chou
description: For kids around the world, music is often the only salvation when the pain and anxiety of teenage life becomes too much to bear. Yuichi (Hayato Ichihara) is in the 8th grade and he worships Lily Chou-Chou, a Bjork-like chanteuse whose epic music is lush and transcendent. Yuichi only lives for Lily Chou-Chou's big Tokyo concert, where the lies and violence can be washed away by the presence of his goddess and her powerful music. But fate has yet another obstacle in store for Lily's devoted fan.

title: Off-Circuit: The Seasons
description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

title: Program 6: Out of the Present
description: This program includes Laura Poitras and Rachel Lauren Mueller’s They’re Here, Ben Russell’s Another Earth, Vika Kirchenbauer’s This Suffocating Now, and the world premiere of Mara Chavez and doris duhennois’s Morne Fortune.
director: Laura Poitras, Rachel Lauren Mueller, Ben Russell, Vika Kirchenbauer, Mara Chavez, doris duhennois

title: IN THE REALM OF THE SENSES
description:
In 1930s Tokyo, former geisha Sada Abe begins an affair with Kichizo, the married proprietor of the inn where she works. Withdrawing from the world into rented rooms, the pair surrender themselves to an increasingly intense cycle of sex, jealousy and experimentation. Their mutual obsession gradually consumes every other part of their lives, carrying them towards an infamous and violent conclusion.
Based on the true story of Sada Abe, Nagisa Oshima’s IN THE REALM OF THE SENSES became an international sensation through its unprecedented combination of arthouse filmmaking and unsimulated sex. Produced as a French-Japanese collaboration to escape Japan’s censorship laws, the film was seized, banned and cut in numerous countries, while Oshima faced an obscenity trial at home. Fifty years later, it remains one of cinema’s most beautiful, confrontational and genuinely erotic studies of desire taken to its absolute limit.

title: Everytime
description: After a shocking accident befalls a teenage girl in Berlin, her mother, younger sister, and boyfriend drift into a state of suspended grief in Sandra Wollner’s atmospheric, constantly surprising new film, winner of the Cannes Un Certain Regard Prize. Germany’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Minnie and Moskowitz             / Once Around
description: Made between Husbands and A Woman Under the Influence , John Cassavetes’ offbeat romantic fairy tale may be the director’s most accessible & charming movie. A quirky, joyous and punch-drunk love story, the film follows an unlikely, opposites-attract romance blossoming between museum curator Minnie (Gena Rowlands) and parking lot attendant Moskowitz (Seymour Cassel). It’s an acting tour de force with Timothy Carey, Val Avery, Cassavetes and his mother Katherine in key supporting roles.

title: Godzilla (1954)
description: Godzilla is the roaring granddaddy of all monster movies. It’s also a remarkably humane and melancholy drama, made in Japan at a time when the country was reeling from nuclear attack and H-bomb testing in the Pacific. Its rampaging radioactive beast, the poignant embodiment of an entire population’s fears, became a beloved international icon of destruction, spawning almost thirty sequels.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero
description: An experience that demands the big screen, director Takashi Yamazaki’s follow-up to his triumphant, Oscar-winning Godzilla Minus One is a supremely satisfying sequel with even more astounding effects choreography than its predecessor.

title: Everytime
description: After a shocking accident befalls a teenage girl in Berlin, her mother, younger sister, and boyfriend drift into a state of suspended grief in Sandra Wollner’s atmospheric, constantly surprising new film, winner of the Cannes Un Certain Regard Prize. Germany’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Misty Green
description: In the star-making performance at the center of Chris Rock’s L.A. odyssey, Rosalind Eleazar plays a former actress struggling to make ends meet in an unforgiving Hollywood. The marvelous supporting cast includes Rock, Adam Driver, Daniel Kaluuya, Anna Kendrick, and more.

title: Stalker
description: In an unnamed country at an unspecified time, there is a fiercely protected post-apocalyptic wasteland known as The Zone. An illegal guide (Aleksandr Kajdanovsky), whose mutant child suggests unspeakable horrors within The Zone, leads a writer (Anatoliy Solonitsyn) and a scientist (Nikolay Grinko) into the heart of the devastation in search of a mythical place known only as The Room. Anyone who enters The Room will supposedly have any of his earthly desires immediately fulfilled.

title: River of No Return
description: Marilyn Monroe’s appearance in Western genre films required designer Travilla to create costumes ranging from saloon-style gowns to casual denim looks. Monroe wanted her character, Kay—a kind-hearted saloon singer torn between an ex-convict (Robert Mitchum) and her troubled fiancé (Rory Calhoun)—to have a natural feel. Her acting coach, Natasha Lytess, and director Otto Preminger clashed over whether Monroe should use her typical breathy voice, with the studio backing Monroe’s decision to forgo it.
director: Otto Preminger PRODUCED BY: Stanley Rubin

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: Bucking Fastard
description: The oddball brilliance of Werner Herzog—returning to NYFF for the first time since 1982’s Fitzcarraldo (NYFF20)—is in full effect in this tale of two sisters (Kate and Rooney Mara, in total sync) who live by their own social and emotional standards and rules.

title: Making Marie Antoinette
description: Sofia Coppola’s dynamic craftsmanship in creating her personal vision for 2006’s Marie Antoinette (NYFF44) is on full display in this video diary shot by her mother, Eleanor Coppola, on the film’s set in Versailles in 2005. Preceded by Kleber Mendonça Filho’s South of Tehran.
