description: This program includes Peggy Ahwesh’s The Wayfinders, Kevin Jerome Everson’s National Seating, the world premiere of Adam Piron’s The Flesh of the Mountain, and Bani Khoshnoudi’s Elegy for the Forgotten, On an Endless War.
director: Peggy Ahwesh, Kevin Jerome Everson, Adam Piron, Bani Khoshnoudi

title: My Wife Cries
description: Angela Schanelec’s (Music, NYFF62) formally audacious portrait of contemporary anxieties around love, gender, and trauma concerns a withdrawn construction worker whose wife reveals a shocking truth, upending perceptions about their seemingly comfortable marriage.

title: The Valley of the Bees
description: Our screening on Sunday 11 October will be introduced by writer, lecturer, and Czech cinema expert, Peter Hames. Set in a…

title: Joy of Joys
description: This exuberant yet sobering documentary from Jonathan Glazer (The Zone of Interest)—with the help of London schoolkids equipped with cameras—goes behind the scenes at Abbey Road to capture the recording of a charity album from War Child Records, which aids children in conflict zones. The screening will be followed by an extended Q&A with Glazer.

title: Drive
description: Driver is a skilled Hollywood stuntman who moonlights as a getaway driver for criminals. Though he projects an icy exterior, lately he's been warming up to a pretty neighbor named Irene and her young son, Benicio. When Irene's husband gets out of jail, he enlists Driver's help in a million-dollar heist. The job goes horribly wrong, and Driver must risk his life to protect Irene and Benicio from the vengeful masterminds behind the robbery.

title: I Deserve a Lover Whose Every
description: Unorthodox Iranian filmmaker Mani Haghighi’s lively, stimulating documentary profiles Nasser Bakhshi, a painter, conceptual artist, collector, and curator—and some would say hoarder—whose monumental archive creates a record of collective memory. Preceded by Kleber Mendonça Filho’s South of Tehran.

title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
description: In 1972, legendary filmmaker William Greaves gathered an extraordinary group of artists, writers, actors, musicians, and thinkers of the Harlem Renaissance. After more than 50 years, his son David Greaves has completed his breathtaking miracle of a movie.

title: Love is Colder than Death [Liebe ist kälter als der Tod]
description: In Rainer Werner Fassbinder’s French New Wave inspired directorial debut, he stars as Franz, a small-time pimp who finds himself in an offbeat love triangle between prostitute Joanna and handsome gangster Bruno, played by frequent Fassbinder collaborators Hanna Schygulle and Ulli Lommel. When Bruno fails to recruit Franz into his crime syndicate, the three strike up an unlikely allegiance, muddying romantic boundaries as they drift through the streets of Munich, plotting varying degrees of criminal activities. Detached, cool, and branded dilettantism at its Berlinale premiere, Love is Colder Than Death is a nihilistic and impulsive portrait of the relationship between three unanchored criminals. Love is Colder Than Death is featured as part of Gangsters Have Feelings Too, a season exploring the sensitive gangster film. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: Kino: Short Stories from the Balkans (18*)
description: Some of the best recent films from the Balkans, by emerging and established filmmakers, explore sexuality, climate change, recent history and death.

title: HKFF: I Heard That They Are Not Going To See Each Other Anymore + Q&A
Off-Circuit: The Seasons
description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

title: NEUROSPICY IV (+ Q&A with Dean Atta)
description: Prepare to watch amazing brand new short films including award winning short film 'Two Black Boys In Paradise' and an exciting Q&A with BAFTA Winner and Acclaimed Poet Dean Atta. Get ready to be inspired, moved, and entertained by the unique perspectives showcased on screen. Don't miss out on this e...

title: THREE GIANT MEN
description:
A crime wave terrorises Istanbul, and the police call in two unlikely heroes to stop the gang responsible: American superhero Captain America and Mexican masked wrestler Santo. Their investigation leads them to a criminal organisation headed by a ruthless villainous version of Spider-Man, who is involved in a series of violent crimes and sinister schemes.
One of the most infamous examples of Turkish exploitation cinema, Three Giant Men is an unauthorised superhero mash-up that combines comic-book characters, crime melodrama, and action spectacle in typically wild 1970s Turkish genre fashion. Its bizarre reinterpretation of familiar heroes, homemade effects, and complete disregard for established comic-book continuity have made it a cult favourite among fans of “Turksploitation.”

title: SCREAMPLAY
description: Edgar Allan (Rufus B. Seder) is an aspiring screenwriter who has just come to Hollywood to make it in the movies…only to wind up working as the janitor at a fleabag apartment complex run by the greasy ex-boxer Martin (played by underground film legend George Kuchar). When Edgar begins channeling his frustrations with his kooky neighbors into fodder for his latest screenplay, the vivid murder scenes he writes begin to happen for real. As the bodies begin to pile up and the line between reality and fiction become increasingly blurred, Edgar, who is convinced that the only way to be a real writer is to suffer, is slowly driven mad. SCREAMPLAY is a marvel of campy charm, gothic horror tropes, and astonishingly inventive set design and special effects. Wearing its low-budget resourcefulness on its sleeve, but also genuinely atmospheric and transporting, the spell it casts is all the more remarkable given that it was filmed almost entirely within the confines of the 3,200-square-foot South End Boston loft where director Rufus Butler Seder and his Boston Black and White Movie Company (comprised of fellow students from the city’s School of the Museum of Fine Arts) had previously made a bevy of similarly inspired 16mm short films. Conjured from some of the earliest and still-most-effective cinematic techniques – matte paintings, scale models, ingeniously adaptable sets, animation, highly expressionistic lighting, and the good old-fashioned magic provided by charismatic performers (above all, Seder himself in the central role, and of course the irreplaceable George Kuchar, who broke his ankle during filming of the final fight scene) – SCREAMPLAY is a deliriously entertaining demonstration of the power of low budget invention, and a singularly charming (Boston) salute to Old Hollywood. Premiered (alongside BLOOD SIMPLE) at the 1985 New York Independent Film Festival, initially distributed by Troma (click here for details about our upcoming Troma series), but rarely screened in recent decades, SCREAMPLAY has been newly restored in 4K – scanned from Seder’s personal 16mm print – and is now back in circulation, where it’s poised to charm, delight, and frighten a whole new audience. Preceded by: Rufus Butler Seder IN THE CITY: A TRILOGY (LIVE IN FEAR; SUN RUN; PHANTOM SUBWAYS) 1977, 6 min, 16mm-to-DCP Writer, director, and star Rufus Butler Seder and producer and cinematographer Dennis M. Piana will be here in person on Fri & Sat for Q&As following the evening screenings; they’ll be joined on Fri evening by star Katy Bolger!

title: A HEART AS WILLING / LA CORAZONADA
description: Nieves runs a modest inn with her son in the Chilean countryside, leading a quiet life shaped by routine and deferred dreams. When a wandering motorcyclist arrives and falls for her, the prospect of a late-blooming romance offers an unexpected glimpse of happiness – yet their relationship seems destined to falter. Everything changes with the arrival of a filmmaker who casts them in her adaptation of Shakespeare’s “The Tempest”, drawing them into the creative process and gradually blurring the boundaries between performance and reality. As fiction begins to reshape their everyday lives, new emotional possibilities emerge in this playful and deeply human meditation on love, aging, cinema, and the mysterious ways stories transform those who inhabit them.

title: Just Like Weather
description: A fascinating, ahead-of-its-time synthesis of fiction and documentary, Allen Fong’s third feature follows a couple from Hong Kong as they navigate domestic trials and tribulations before eventually heading to the United States.

title: CHAT PILE Presents: Escape from L.A.
description: Into the 9.6-quaked Los Angeles of 2013 comes Snake Plissken. His job: wade through L.A.’s ruined landmarks to retrieve a doomsday device.

title: Apocalypse Now: The Final Cut
description: Francis Ford Coppola’s epic, Vietnam-set reimagining of Joseph Conrad’s novella Heart of Darkness sends Willard (Martin Sheen) on a desperate jungle mission to “terminate with extreme prejudice” the mysterious Col. Kurtz (Marlon Brando). The making of Apocalypse Now was a famously difficult but resulted in an unforgettable film full of remarkable technical achievements. The film received eight nominations, including Best Picture, Art Direction and Film Editing, and won for Vittorio Storaro’s spectacular cinematography and the immersive soundscape created by Walter Murch, Mark Berger, Richard Beggs, and Nat Boxer.

title: Pink Palace: DESERT HEARTS
description: Pink Palace brings you this often overlooked milestone in lesbian cinema. Ground breaking when it appeared in UK cinemas, lesbian director Donna Deitch’s uplifting romance was one of the first films to look at a non-dramatic, non-sensational happy positive romance.  The 1950’s set story follows lite...

title: Interstellar
description: In Earth's future, a global crop blight and second Dust Bowl are slowly rendering the planet uninhabitable. Professor Brand (Michael Caine), a brilliant NASA physicist, is working on plans to save mankind by transporting Earth's population to a new home via a wormhole. But first, Brand must send former NASA pilot Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) and a team of researchers through the wormhole and across the galaxy to find out which of three planets could be mankind's new home.

title: Remake
description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

title: Mystery Movie
description: Don't miss our fan favourite MYSTERY MOVIE screenings! On a near weekly basis we will serve up a random mystery movie, with No Clues and No Hints as to what they will be. In 2026, we'll be presenting these as STAFF CURATED selections each and every week by our lovely Front of House, Duty Manager, and Projection Team! You can find the schedule below: --- Wed 29th July - Aya's Pick (120 minutes) Wed 5th Aug - Chloe's Pick (91 minutes) Wed 12th Aug - Liv's Pick (92 minutes) Wed 19th Aug - Julia's Pick (82 minutes) Wed 26th Aug - Chevy's Pick (112 minutes) --- You can find a list of every MYSTERY MOVIE we have ever screened HERE ; if a film is on this list, it is not eligible for future Mystery Movie screenings! --- Content Advice : As these films are a mystery, we aren't able to provide specific ratings / guidance on the film's content. We strongly advise that you take this into consideration before purchasing a ticket.

title: Edward Said: Between Worlds
description: The life and mind of Edward Said, a professor, author, and world-renowned advocate for the Palestinian cause, fuels Maiken Baird’s rich, engrossing documentary, made up entirely of archival footage.

title: BADI AKA TURKISH E.T.
description:
A young boy discovers a friendly alien who has arrived on Earth and forms a bond with the strange visitor. As the alien attempts to survive in an unfamiliar world, the pair must avoid those who want to capture and study him, leading to a series of adventures involving friendship, curiosity, and the encounter between humans and an outsider from another planet.
A classic piece of Turkish genre cinema, Badi reflects the wave of local science-fiction and fantasy productions that reinterpreted popular international films through limited budgets and local filmmaking traditions. Its affectionate alien-child relationship and homemade effects have given it a cult reputation among fans of Turkish exploitation and “Turkish knockoff” cinema.

title: Program 6: Out of the Present
description: This program includes Laura Poitras and Rachel Lauren Mueller’s They’re Here, Ben Russell’s Another Earth, Vika Kirchenbauer’s This Suffocating Now, and the world premiere of Mara Chavez and doris duhennois’s Morne Fortune.
director: Laura Poitras, Rachel Lauren Mueller, Ben Russell, Vika Kirchenbauer, Mara Chavez, doris duhennois

title: Foreign Travel
description: The latest from Ted Fendt is a gentle exploration of the time, space, and syntax of life and literature centered on a small circle of friends and acquaintances in Berlin who meet over the course of a year for a book club tackling the work of magical realist novelist Anna Maria Ortese.

title: Minnie and Moskowitz             / Once Around
description: Made between Husbands and A Woman Under the Influence , John Cassavetes’ offbeat romantic fairy tale may be the director’s most accessible & charming movie. A quirky, joyous and punch-drunk love story, the film follows an unlikely, opposites-attract romance blossoming between museum curator Minnie (Gena Rowlands) and parking lot attendant Moskowitz (Seymour Cassel). It’s an acting tour de force with Timothy Carey, Val Avery, Cassavetes and his mother Katherine in key supporting roles.

title: Millennium Actress
description: Filmmaker Genya Tachibana begins work on a documentary about famed Japanese actress Chiyoko Fujiwara. Now well into old age, Chiyoko has become reclusive and shy about any publicity, but she eventually warms up to Tachibana and starts to relate her life story. As the decades pass, Chiyoko is transformed from a teen with big dreams into a full-blown celebrity, while her cinematic characters span various eras, from ancient Japan to the distant future.

title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
description: When Sally (Marilyn Burns) hears that her grandfather's grave may have been vandalized, she and her paraplegic brother, Franklin (Paul A. Partain), set out with their friends to investigate. After a detour to their family's old farmhouse, they discover a group of crazed, murderous outcasts living next door. As the group is attacked one by one by the chainsaw-wielding Leatherface (Gunnar Hansen), who wears a mask of human skin, the survivors must do everything they can to escape.

title: Rose
description: Berlin’s Silver Bear winner for Best Leading Performance, Sandra Hüller fully inhabits the daunting role of a 17th-century woman who disguises herself as a male soldier, only to continue the ruse after battle, in Markus Schleinzer’s enthralling fable of faith and social intolerance. Austria’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Possible Love
description: The lives of two married couples from different social strata collide in Lee Chang-dong’s brilliantly unfolding narrative about economic precarity, in which a laid-off factory worker and his wife become the camera subjects for a documentary filmmaker. South Korea’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Making Marie Antoinette
description: Sofia Coppola’s dynamic craftsmanship in creating her personal vision for 2006’s Marie Antoinette (NYFF44) is on full display in this video diary shot by her mother, Eleanor Coppola, on the film’s set in Versailles in 2005. Preceded by Kleber Mendonça Filho’s South of Tehran.

title: Kingdom of Heaven: Director's Cut
description: Ridley Scott's extended cut of an epic adventure about a common man who finds himself thrust into a decades-long war. Orlando Bloom plays a humble blacksmith who discovers that he is the son of a knght, and travels to the Holy Land to fight in the crusades. A stranger in a strange land, he serves a doomed King, falls in love with an exotic and forbidden Queen, and rises to knighthood. Ultimately, he must protect the people of Jerusalem from overwhelming forces, while striving to keep a fragile peace.

title: Pelechian Project Program 2
description: Spanning the late 1960s to the early 1990s, these restored films of Artavazd Pelechian complete a career-spanning survey of his extraordinary body of work.

title: The Godfather
description: Widely regarded as one of the greatest films of all time, this mob drama, based on Mario Puzo's novel of the same name, focuses on the powerful Italian-American crime family of Don Vito Corleone (Marlon Brando). When the don's youngest son, Michael (Al Pacino), reluctantly joins the Mafia, he becomes involved in the inevitable cycle of violence and betrayal. Although Michael tries to maintain a normal relationship with his wife, Kay (Diane Keaton), he is drawn deeper into the family business.

title: A Long Winter
description: High in the stark Mountain West, Mikey (Fred Hechinger) watches as his family slowly comes undone in Andrew Haigh’s (All of Us Strangers, NYFF61) beautiful yet forbidding 1950s-set tale of disappearance and growth, adapted from a Colm Tóibín story.

title: Pelechian Project Program 1
description: Restored under the supervision of Artavazd Pelechian, now 88, these short films blur the categories of documentary essay and the poetic avant-garde.

title: All of a Sudden
description: Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto shared the Best Actress prize at Cannes for Academy Award–winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi’s (Drive My Car, NYFF59) radiant new film about a nursing home director promoting a radical new care program. Japan’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: Manhunter : The Final Cut
description: A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a serial killer of families and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). The third feature written and directed by Michael Mann is a gripping adaptation of the first of Thomas Harris’s four novels featuring the iconic murderer, and benefits from the filmmaker’s typically striking visuals as well as a top-notch supporting cast , including Tom Noonan as the hunted killer, and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen (The Contender, 2000) as his blind love interest. -- This new 4K Final Cut, overseen by Mann, enhances the film’s depth, visual clarity and sound, offering audiences the ultimate immersive version. Shot in 1985, MANHUNTER was on a frontier in both its subject matter and film form, initiating an impressive list of subsequent films and series. “40 years ago – though armed with Thomas Harris’ excellent novel, “Red Dragon” – its subject matter, the profiling of serial killers, as well as being shocking and raw, was unknown. When adapting, I wanted to make its storytelling deliver audiences into a certain state of threat and emotional engagement. Integral to that was the visualization and use of music with lyrics sometimes working like a libretto. We have carefully remastered the film to try to evoke that mood and intensity, heightened with audio sourced from the original 5.1 35mm analog masters. This latest iteration is that version of the film with which I’m most satisfied.” said director Michael Mann. Under the guidance of Mann, this 4K scan of the original 35mm negative – with a few shots from an interpositive - was conformed and digitally restored at L’Immagine Ritrovata in Bologna. Both the theatrical version and the UHD HDR & SDR video color gradings were performed by Stefan Sonnenfeld at Company 3 in Los Angeles with the director. Sound restoration was done at Audio Mechanics from an original 35mm magnetic 6-track printmaster to release a new 5.1 mix by Luke Schwartzweller at Fox . Technical coordination and deliveries were managed by L’Immagine Ritrovata . This project was supervised by Becca Mann and STUDIOCANAL team, Jean-Pierre Boiget and Delphine Roussel . For Michael Mann, the process is about renewing the film’s immediacy for contemporary audiences: “If the picture was left the way it was, it would be interesting, but you’d feel some distance …you’d be observing it somewhat. I’m more interested in its original intent impacting you the same way it may have in 1986…that is, to bring you into it again in the original way.” As a film distinguished by its striking visual style, including Colleen Attwood’s costume design, Academy Award- winner Mel Bourne’s art direction, Dante Spinotti’s lighting, Mann worked with his long-time collaborator, Stefan Sonnenfeld (Company 3), to develop a new color grade for ‘The Final Cut’ that engages a contemporary audience while honoring the film’s lasting legacy. “A good example is the use of primaries and secondaries in combinations that don’t occur in nature for an unsettling ambiance or the use of blue for night-time imagery. We’ve changed values subtly sometimes, but significantly, to enhance the impact without changing the dramatic intent of the film,” said Stefan Sonnenfeld. He adds: “Michael… wants you to understand the story and the mood and the environment… and then asks you to interpret that in colour… He also tells you what emotion he’s trying to evoke from the scene.” The new version also introduces an HDR presentation, offering an intensified new experience. “So that nobody’s ever seen the movie like that,” noted Sonnenfeld.

title: Six Degrees of Separation
description: This screening will include an introduction from Never Watching Movies. Criminally underseen, this exceptional satire exposes the performative roles of New…

title: Bardi
description: For her majestic work of earthy imagination, filmmaker and photographer Tala Hadid immersed herself in the rugged, fraternal world of a group of horse-riders in central Morocco, as they take part in an equestrian military ritual that dates to the 16th century.

title: Edward Said: Between Worlds
description: The life and mind of Edward Said, a professor, author, and world-renowned advocate for the Palestinian cause, fuels Maiken Baird’s rich, engrossing documentary, made up entirely of archival footage.

title: HKFF: Inherited Movements, many migrations + Discussion
Remake
description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

title: COMBAT BREATHING: INSURGENT POIESIS
description: Marking the opening of “Combat Breathing Vol. II”, this film program brings together contemporary artworks that emerge from commitments to or embeddedness within political struggles and streams of anti-imperialist thought. Here, moving images function as social productions made for collective engagement, transforming mere viewership into situated modes of cinematic “spect-actor-ship,” to borrow from theorist Augusto Boal. Taken together, these films, informed by various experimental and militant traditions of image-making, model the inseparability of and dynamic correspondences between form and content. Titled “Insurgent Poiesis”, the program simultaneously proposes the moving image as a means for agitational ideological dissemination and a space for poetic invention: a form capable of circulating ideas while remaining open to a multiplicity of meanings, unexpected encounters, and unbounded experimentation. Refusing the fiction of aesthetic autonomy, the film program begins with the recognition that all artistic and cultural productions are ideologically conditioned. The selected films by Tony Cokes, Filipa César, Basel Abbas and Ruanne Abou-Rahme, Shiva Addanki, Colectivo Los Ingrávidos, and Camila Galaz figure the political and philosophical entwinement of poiesis and revolutionary activity: bringing something into existence that did not exist before, producing “a world where many worlds fit – un mundo donde quepan muchos mundos” by any means necessary. Tony Cokes EVIL.35: CARLIN / OWNERS (2012, 8 min, DCP) EVIL.35: CARLIN / OWNERS, like many of Tony Cokes’s recent works, is structured by a simple formal operation: the pairing of found text and found music. These audiovisual combinations, attuned to the historical and ideological convergences and divergences of their source materials, generate further meanings. In this work, Cokes pairs an excerpt from a characteristically cantankerous screed by the late stand-up comedian George Carlin with two songs by the British agit-prop post-punk group Gang of Four. Carlin’s words directly confront the contradictions of liberal capitalist democracy – the absurd state of affairs whereby a small ruling class owns and controls everything, from government officials to the workforce, despite the juridical pretense of universal political equality – while Gang of Four’s rebellious songs allude to the Irish anti-colonial struggle and the commodification of pleasure. Taken together, and aided by Cokes’s cinematic choreography of sound, background color, and text graphics, audiences are engaged as critical readers capable of piercing through neoliberal capitalism’s false naturalizations. Filipa César TRANSMISSION FROM THE LIBERATED ZONES (2015, 30 min, DCP) TRANSMISSION FROM THE LIBERATED ZONES belongs to a body of work by Filipa César concerned with the conditions and aftermaths of the anti-colonial struggle of the PAIGC (African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde) against the Portuguese between 1963-74. Departing from the concept of the “Liberated Zones” – used to describe areas freed from colonial domination, and organized and managed by PAIGC guerrilla militants – the film partially reconstructs the memory of these autonomous spaces via archival documents and the contemporary testimonies of four Swedes (diplomat Folke Löfgren, filmmaker Lennart Malmer, filmmaker and psychologist Ingela Romare, and politician Birgitta Dahl), all of whom visited Guinea in the early 1970s. Deeply reflexive of the aesthetic and technological mediation of these insurgent histories, the documents and statements are performatively presented by and visually projected onto a young character in a dark room whose image is, in turn, multiplied as an infinite regression through César’s use of experimental optical effects. Through these inventive means, César’s work opens up struggles as contradictory sites of antagonism and solidarity while projecting the radioactive remnants of liberationist practice into the present and future. Basel Abbas & Ruanne Abou-Rahme OH SHINING STAR TESTIFY (2016-19, 10 min, DCP) OH SHINING STAR TESTIFY is an audiovisual poem that seeks to account for and speculate on the possibilities of fugitive resurgences within, under, and beyond the ruins of colonial catastrophe. It invites us to consider the relation between the destruction of bodies and the erasure of images, and the conditions under which those very bodies and images might once again reappear. The film recursively loops CCTV footage taken from an Israeli military surveillance camera. The footage – temporarily released online following a court injunction – depicts an incident from 2014 when 14-year-old Yusuf ­Shawamreh crossed the “separation fence” erected by the Israeli military, near Hebron, to pick some Akoub – an edible plant used in Palestinian cuisine, which blooms for short periods of time. After crossing the fence, Israeli forces ambushed and shot Yusuf dead. Layering poetic verses and evocative images upon one another, which are sampled from online recordings of quotidian acts of corporeal and infrastructural devastation as well as scenes of defiant social rituals and performances, Abbas and Abou-Rahme’s cine-poem critically situates the serial occurrences of such acts of state terror and their ongoing resistances. Formally guided by an accumulative logic, not unlike that which subjects Palestinian land and people to continual displacement and expropriation by a settler regime, OH SHINING STAR attunes viewers to the enduring, latent animacies of the oppressed and the ecological specter of return. Shiva Addanki A PERMANENT OPIUM WAR (2026, 10 min, DCP) A PERMANENT OPIUM WAR grapples with the historical and geographical underpinnings of statist, imperialist, and global-market infrastructures as they are evoked through the sprawl of the Greater New York metropolitan area. The work both poses and problematizes the presumed distinctions between the Global North and Global South, or First and Third Worlds, tracing how ideological, commercial, and political exchanges materialize across networks linking states and corporations. It approaches these infrastructures from the vantage point of the militant and revolutionary struggles that traverse, contest, and resist their hardwired and concretized forms. Charting connections across disparate coordinates – including Delaney Hall, a privately managed immigrant detention facility in Newark, New Jersey; the persecution of Assata Shakur following her capture after the 1973 Turnpike Shooting; commodity exchanges between poor and developed marketplaces; women’s Naxalite training by Maoist revolutionary insurgents in India; and political spectacles of Hindutva–Zionist alliance – the work assembles a constellation in which these violent structures and liberationist histories become materially and politically entangled. Colectivo Los Ingrávidos FACES IN THE CROWD 2: MEMORIAL (2019, 14 min, 16mm-to-DCP) Shot on expired film stock by the anonymous filmmaking collective Colectivo Los Ingrávidos, FACES IN THE CROWD 2: MEMORIAL is an experimental audiovisual meditation on memory, neoliberal and colonial state violence in Mexico, and the forms of social resistance that emerge in response to it. The film moves through politically mobilized crowds, protest ephemera, and historical traces of organized violence with an expiring breath – as if these images and the memories they carry are themselves at risk of extinction. It embraces the material qualities of analog film through grainy textures, layered images, and an unstable frame, transforming the filmic surface into an alchemical site where memory is simultaneously preserved, fractured, and regenerated. Centered on the fiftieth commemoration of the 1968 Tlatelolco massacre and the nationwide leftist movement that led to it, the resulting work becomes a contemplation on how struggles reemerge and transform, and how protesting crowds become social bodies that carry historical memory and continually innovate practices of dissent. In the work, images and sounds fragment, overlap, and repeat, producing a dreamlike, almost trance-inducing experience rather than a linear or chronological account of events. Such formal disruptions reflect Colectivo Los Ingrávidos’s broader interest in challenging dominant audiovisual languages and resisting the ways mainstream media can organize, discipline, and control perception. Camila Galaz VECINO, VECINO (2022, 20 min, DCP) Set against the backdrop of Chile’s 2019 social uprising, VECINO VECINO returns to a 1986 French television documentary on MAPU Lautaro, a left-wing armed organization that resisted the Pinochet dictatorship. For filmmaker Camila Galaz, the archive is at once historical record and intimate inheritance, as her father was connected to this organization, binding her personal history to the political memory embedded within the footage. Moving between archival and newly filmed material, and incorporating annotations and choreographic scores, the film unsettles the authority of the documentary image by opening a mediated space where memory can be questioned, re-performed, and reimagined. The past emerges not as a fixed record, but as something continually reconstructed through fragments, gestures, and acts of translation. In the potent aftermath of the recent national uprising, VECINO VECINO traces the echoes between generations, reflecting on social and historical questions of inheritance while asking how histories of resistance are encountered, remembered, and embodied. Total running time: ca. 95 min. Followed by a conversation between KJ Abudu, Basel Abbas and Ruanne Abou-Rahme, Omar Berrada, Camila Galaz, and Adam HajYahia!

title: CLUB LINGERIE (on VHS)
description:
When Renae inherits her grandfather’s failing nightclub, she revamps it with lingerie models and the customers come running. Unfortunately, so does a mysterious killer.
Jared Masters’ gleefully disreputable microbudget slasher-comedy is a neon-lit cocktail of bare flesh, bad taste and backstage bloodshed - the kind of handmade Hollywood sleaze that feels beamed in from a vanished late-night cable channel.

Seder) is an aspiring screenwriter who has just come to Hollywood to make it in the movies…only to wind up working as the janitor at a fleabag apartment complex run by the greasy ex-boxer Martin (played by underground film legend George Kuchar). As the bodies begin to pile up and the line between reality and fiction become increasingly blurred, Edgar, who is convinced that the only way to be a real writer is to suffer, is slowly driven mad. SCREAMPLAY is a marvel of campy charm, gothic horror tropes, and astonishingly inventive set design and special effects. Wearing its low-budget resourcefulness on its sleeve, but also genuinely atmospheric and transporting, the spell it casts is all the more remarkable given that it was filmed almost entirely within the confines of the 3,200-square-foot South End Boston loft where director Rufus Butler Seder and his Boston Black and White Movie Company (comprised of fellow students from the city’s School of the Museum of Fine Arts) had previously made a bevy of similarly inspired 16mm short films. Conjured from some of the earliest and still-most-effective cinematic techniques – matte paintings, scale models, ingeniously adaptable sets, animation, highly expressionistic lighting, and the good old-fashioned magic provided by charismatic performers (above all, Seder himself in the central role, and of course the irreplaceable George Kuchar, who broke his ankle during filming of the final fight scene) – SCREAMPLAY is a deliriously entertaining demonstration of the power of low budget invention, and a singularly charming (Boston) salute to Old Hollywood. Premiered (alongside BLOOD SIMPLE) at the 1985 New York Independent Film Festival, initially distributed by Troma (click here for details about our upcoming Troma series), but rarely screened in recent decades, SCREAMPLAY has been newly restored in 4K – scanned from Seder’s personal 16mm print – and is now back in circulation, where it’s poised to charm, delight, and frighten a whole new audience. Preceded by: Rufus Butler Seder IN THE CITY: A TRILOGY (LIVE IN FEAR; SUN RUN; PHANTOM SUBWAYS) 1977, 6 min, 16mm-to-DCP Writer, director, and star Rufus Butler Seder and producer and cinematographer Dennis M. title: Foreign Travel
description: The latest from Ted Fendt is a gentle exploration of the time, space, and syntax of life and literature centered on a small circle of friends and acquaintances in Berlin who meet over the course of a year for a book club tackling the work of magical realist novelist Anna Maria Ortese.

title: Pan's Labyrinth in 3D
description: Ofelia (Ivana Baquero), a 10-year-old girl in Francoist Spain, discovers a magical underworld in one of writer-director Guillermo del Toro’s most richly imagined fantasies. When Ofelia is lured into a labyrinth hidden in the forest, a faun emerges to reveal she is a long-lost princess. To return to her mystical kingdom, Ofelia must complete three magical tasks. The film earned six Academy Award nominations , including Foreign Language Film, and won for its stunning Art Direction, Cinematography, and Makeup, with del Toro regular Doug Jones playing the Faun and the Pale Man. Pan’s Labyrinth appears here in a brand-new 4K restoration and in 3D. Del Toro, who personally supervised every stage of the new restoration from the original 35mm negative, introduces the film in person. Special thanks to Cineverse.

description: The screening on August 23rd will be introduced by writer Daniel Bird. The screening on October 1st will be introduced by…

title: Radiohead X Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror
description: Silents Synced pairs classic silent movies with epic rock music to bring audiences a unique big screen experience. This reimagining of the iconic Nosferatu (1922) features Radiohead’s Kid A (2000) and Amnesiac (2001) albums. An unauthorized adaptation of Bram Stoker’s Dracula, Nosferatu (1922) is the quintessential silent vampire film, crafted by legendary German director F. W. Murnau. Rather than depicting Dracula as a shape-shifting monster or debonair gentleman, Murnau’s Graf Orlok (as portrayed by Max Schreck) is a nightmarish, spidery creature of bulbous head and taloned claws - perhaps the most genuinely disturbing incarnation of vampirism yet envisioned. Don’t miss out on the chance to experience this imaginative new take on an iconic horror classic!

title: Off-Circuit: The Seasons
description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

title: The Drift
description: An underseen and criminally overlooked work of the Nouvelle Vague, Paula Delsol’s first feature film, about a young woman’s encounters with a succession of different men, is a kind of modernist report on the state of women’s liberation in 1960s France.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
description: Jodie Foster stars as Clarice Starling, a top student at the FBI's training academy. Jack Crawford (Scott Glenn) wants Clarice to interview Dr. Hannibal Lecter (Anthony Hopkins), a brilliant psychiatrist who is also a violent psychopath, serving life behind bars for various acts of murder and cannibalism. Crawford believes that Lecter may have insight into a case and that Starling, as an attractive young woman, may be just the bait to draw him out.

title: BLONDE DEATH (ON VHS)
description:
Shot on consumer-grade video and circulating for decades as a near-mythic underground tape, Blonde Death follows the runaway odyssey of Tammy, a teenage misfit fleeing an abusive home with two queer outsiders who christen themselves her new family. Their improvised road trip blends impulsive romance, petty crime, and manic self-invention, gradually collapsing into violence as the trio drifts further from stability. The film’s messy exuberance is threaded with a growing sense of doom, capturing the volatility of youth pushed to the margins.
A seminal artifact of queer DIY cinema, Blonde Death fuses melodrama, punk energy, and camp excess with unexpectedly sharp social commentary. Director James Robert Baker — better known for his incendiary fiction — uses the limitations of shot-on-video production to amplify the film’s immediacy and emotional rawness. The result is a rare, transgressive work whose jagged form reflects the precarity, rebellion, and desperation of its characters, standing at the intersection of outsider art and queer counterculture.
Programme notes by Dominic Hicks

title: I Deserve a Lover Whose Every
description: Unorthodox Iranian filmmaker Mani Haghighi’s lively, stimulating documentary profiles Nasser Bakhshi, a painter, conceptual artist, collector, and curator—and some would say hoarder—whose monumental archive creates a record of collective memory. Preceded by Kleber Mendonça Filho’s South of Tehran.

title: Birth
description: It took Anna (Nicole Kidman) 10 years to recover from the death of her husband, Sean, but now she's on the verge of marrying her boyfriend, Joseph (Danny Huston), and finally moving on. However, on the night of her engagement party, a young boy named Sean (Cameron Bright) turns up, saying he is her dead husband reincarnated. At first she ignores the child, but his knowledge of her former husband's life is uncanny, leading her to believe that he might be telling the truth.

Over the course of several days, the students interview townspeople and gather clues to support the tale's veracity. But the project takes a frightening turn when the students lose their way in the woods and begin hearing horrific noises.

Japan’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

title: River of No Return
description: Marilyn Monroe’s appearance in Western genre films required designer Travilla to create costumes ranging from saloon-style gowns to casual denim looks. Monroe wanted her character, Kay—a kind-hearted saloon singer torn between an ex-convict (Robert Mitchum) and her troubled fiancé (Rory Calhoun)—to have a natural feel. Her acting coach, Natasha Lytess, and director Otto Preminger clashed over whether Monroe should use her typical breathy voice, with the studio backing Monroe’s decision to forgo it.

title: Yi Yi
description: The extraordinary, internationally embraced Yi Yi (A One and a Two . . .), directed by the late Taiwanese master Edward Yang, follows a middle-class family in Taipei over the course of one year, beginning with a wedding and ending with a funeral. Whether chronicling middle-age father NJ’s tentative flirtations with an old flame or precocious young son Yang-Yang’s attempts at capturing reality with his beloved camera, the filmmaker deftly imbues every gorgeous frame with a compassionate clarity. Warm, sprawling, and dazzling, this intimate epic is one of the undisputed masterworks of the new century. 4K digital restoration carried out by Pony Canyon Inc., with analog and digital processes provided by Imagica Entertainment Media Services, Inc.

title: The Unknown
description: After an impulsive hookup, a Parisian photographer (Niels Schneider) finds that he has somehow swapped bodies with a German actress (Léa Seydoux). Arthur Harari treats this wild metaphysical gambit with the utmost sincerity in this uncanny supernatural drama.

title: Scream
description: Wes Craven re-invented and revitalised the slasher-horror genre with this modern horror classic, which manages to be funny, clever and scary, as a fright-masked knife maniac stalks high-school students in middle-class suburbia. Craven is happy to provide both tension and self-parody as the body count mounts - but the victims aren't always the ones you'd expect.

title: Misty Green
description: In the star-making performance at the center of Chris Rock’s L.A. odyssey, Rosalind Eleazar plays a former actress struggling to make ends meet in an unforgiving Hollywood. The marvelous supporting cast includes Rock, Adam Driver, Daniel Kaluuya, Anna Kendrick, and more.

title: In Which Annie Gives It Those
description: Featuring the first screenplay by Indian writer Arundhati Roy (who stars as the titular protagonist’s nonconformist friend), Pradip Krishen’s English-language film bounces between hope and cynicism to form a sharp portrait of youth in 1970s New Delhi.

title: Nosferatu
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . "I first saw Murnau’s Symphony of Horror when I was nine years old. The film’s expressionistic images continue to haunt me, the chiaroscuro compositions tapping vividly into timeless subconscious fears. My improvisations on viola and piano draw inspiration from the leitmotifs and sound effects of 70s horror soundtracks and the languages of Second Viennese School composers contemporary to Murnau, also Jewish Traditional Music that informs my personal approach to creating a score for the film." - Hugo Max Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work. Photo Credit - Richard Ecclestone An iconic film of the German expressionist cinema, and one of the most famous of all silent movies, F. W. Murnau's Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror continues to haunt — and, indeed, terrify — modern audiences with the unshakable power of its images. By teasing a host of occult atmospherics out of dilapidated set-pieces and innocuous real-world locations alike, Murnau captured on celluloid the deeply-rooted elements of a waking nightmare, and launched the signature "Murnau-style" that would change cinema history forever. In this first-ever screen adaptation of Bram Stoker's Dracula, a simple real-estate transaction leads an intrepid businessman deep into the superstitious heart of Transylvania. There he encounters the otherworldly Count Orlok — portrayed by the legendary Max Schreck, in a performance the very backstory of which has spawned its own mythology — who soon after embarks upon a cross-continental voyage to take up residence in a distant new land... and establish his ambiguous dominion. As to whether the count's campaign against the plague-wracked populace erupts from satanic decree, erotic compulsion, or the simple impulse of survival — that remains, perhaps, the greatest mystery of all in this film that's like a blackout...

title: COMBAT BREATHING: THE TIME BENEATH THE CONCRETE
description: “I’m in jail out here, I’m in jail in there.” –Hugh Masekela The prison is the institutionalization of a logic central to the systemic formation and reproduction of racial capitalism and colonialism. It remains the primary form in modernity through which states (either under ostensibly opposing but in truth co-constituting liberal democratic and fascistic guises) manage surplus populations, extract surplus value, break social and kinship relations, and utilize the captive body to control not only those within its walls, but also those on the outside. This film program borrows its title – and something of its poetic and conceptual grammar – from the writing of scholar Nasser Abourahme, who in his book “The Time Beneath the Concrete” brings the prison into immediate relation with the colony and the refugee camp in Palestine. Extending his analysis to the ghetto and the reservation within the U.S. context as additional sites of enclosure, this program with works by Alex Johnston, Sky Hopinka, and Larry Clark attends not only to the violence of imprisonment, but also to the ways such sites have and continue to be made into focal points of struggle by those whose lives they seek to crush and mold. What emerges is a transnational, historically grounded, and situated account of the carceral system that traces the prison’s many reinventions while insisting that the project of enclosure, however violently renewed, is never complete. Alex Johnston EVIDENCE OF THE EVIDENCE (2018, 20 min, DCP) The 1971 Attica Prison Rebellion remains a defining moment of radical resistance – not only in the history of prison struggles and the American anti-racist and anti-state movement, but also for international struggles against enclosure and carcerality. The state’s retaking of the prison on the fourth and final day of the uprising, described as the bloodiest one-day encounter between Americans since the Civil War, remains an open wound. EVIDENCE OF THE EVIDENCE examines this fraught and contested history through a granular interrogation of the archival record. Drawing on previously unseen video footage recorded by a state trooper during the four-day rebellion, the film offers a visceral, ground-level account of the events at Attica while tracing how they were simultaneously mediated and narrativized through the images being produced. Recalling Harun Farocki and Andrei Ujică’s seminal VIDEOGRAMS OF A REVOLUTION (1992), the film considers the manifold roles moving images play in producing history and memory – as well as in their erasure and destruction. At a moment of escalating racism and authoritarianism across the West, when prisons and other regimes of enclosure remain indispensable to imperial domination, EVIDENCE OF THE EVIDENCE emerges as a timely and urgent work of agitprop and media criticism. Sky Hopinka SUNFLOWER SIEGE ENGINE (2022, 12 min, DCP) The Occupation of Alcatraz (1969-71) marked a historic moment of indigenous resistance in the United States. Led by Indians of All Tribes (IAT), eighty-nine Native activists and their supporters occupied the abandoned federal prison island, demanding self-determination, tribal sovereignty, and land rights, forcefully recentering the question of indigenous land against the settler-colonial foundations of the U.S. empire. Although the occupation also brought to the fore the many unresolved contradictions within pan-Indian political discourse and organizing, particularly around the contested meanings of sovereignty and indigeneity, its memory and legacy continue to offer a vital site of reflection and empowerment in struggles for land and decolonization. In SUNFLOWER SIEGE ENGINE, distinct moments and scales of resistance are collapsed and woven together: documentation of the Alcatraz occupation; the reclamation of Cahokia and the repatriation of ancestors; and intimate reflections on inhabiting one’s body in the present while looking back upon historical struggles and their continuities, excesses, and impasses. Through experimental visual gestures and poetry, the film meditates on the carceral origins and enduring logic of the reservation system, asking where sovereignty and belligerence converge, and where they break away. Larry Clark AS ABOVE, SO BELOW (1973, 52 min, 16mm-to-DCP) One of the most politically radical films to emerge from the L.A. Rebellion, AS ABOVE, SO BELOW offers an uncompromising portrayal of the formation of revolutionary consciousness, the underground organization of black insurgency in the United States, and the place of these processes within the broader project of Third World liberation. The film centers on Jita-Hadi, who grows up in the structurally abandoned neighborhoods of postwar Chicago. He later joins the Marine Corps, only to become disillusioned when he is deployed across Asia and the Caribbean to suppress leftist governments and protect U.S. imperial and capitalist interests. Returning to an increasingly ghettoized United States, Jita-Hadi is discreetly recruited into a black insurrectionary group. The narrative is interwoven with archival radio broadcasts and film excerpts that evoke the carceral state’s suppression of racialized groups, as well as parodic scenes – including narcotizing church services and the monologues of a black centrist. Through these different registers, the film sharply articulates the internal and external, national and transnational obstacles confronting black liberation. Total running time: ca. 90 min.

title: Hunt for the Wilderpeople
description: Ricky Baker (Julian Dennison), a Māori foster teen with a knack for getting into trouble, is placed into the warm care of Bella Faulkner (Rima Te Wiata) and her stern, indifferent husband, Hec (Sam Neill). When an unexpected tragedy strikes, Ricky runs away into the New Zealand bush, obligating Hec to seek him out. Thanks to a set of comical mishaps and misconceptions, the two become subjects of a manhunt, forcing them to go on the run and brave the wilderness. Sam Neill’s portrayal of Hec is one of the actor’s most cherished performances as he deftly evolves from reluctant guardian to a quietly tender father figure for Dennison’s rambunctiously endearing Ricky. Adapted from the 1986 novel Wild Pork and Watercress by Barry Crump, Hunt for the Wilderpeople premiered at the Sundance Film Festival to critical acclaim. The film also broke box office records in New Zealand that year, becoming the most successful film made locally—excluding international co-productions—an achievement the film still holds today.

Sam and his new friends must save Michael and Star from the undead.

title: COMBAT BREATHING: PERPETUAL RECURRENCES, PART 1: CINÉ-GUERRILLAS
description: What characterizes the militant image? What historical conditions produced it and what kinds of histories were, in turn, produced by it? Where might it be found today? This program brings together a selection of contemporary works that frontally engage the legacies and continuities of Third Cinema and the tricontinental geographies of leftist, anti-colonial collaboration and mobilization that were this cultural movement’s primary condition of possibility. These works, as with Third Cinema, refuse clear-cut divisions between formal acuity and socio-political signification, and ground cinema’s documentative, archival, and imaginative powers as useful tools in the ongoing decolonizing process. Such a process involves grappling with the positive and negative lessons of prior movements in order to deduce alternative pathways to liberation. The selected films in this program revisit various sites of unfinished and unfolding anti-colonial struggle, from Ghana and Palestine to Yugoslavia and Algeria. Orienting viewers toward critical reflections on the historical twists and turns of the capitalist world-system on macro and interpersonal scales while remaining firmly rooted in their respective presents, the works by Mila Turajlić, John Akomfrah with Black Audio Film Collective, and Reem Shilleh further articulate the persisting structures of colonialism in their intensifications and mutations following from these mid-twentieth-century decolonization movements. The continuity of said conditions into this millennium can only ever engender, as these films themselves embody, the “perpetual recurrence” of a countervailing militant image. Mila Turajlić CINÉ-GUERRILLAS: SCENES FROM THE LABUDOVIĆ REELS 2022, 94 min, DCP Based on resurrected 35mm footage shot by Stevan Labudović, the official cameraman of former Yugoslav President Tito, this documentary by Mila Turajlić takes viewers on an archival road trip through the insurgent historical streams and collaborative Third World networks that constituted and sustained the Algerian anti-colonial struggle from 1954-62. Turajlić follows Labudović’s work in Algeria through intimate interviews with him and Algerian revolutionary contemporaries, matching his newsreel footage – audiovisual testaments to tricontinental solidarity – with excerpts from his diary. Employing only images of the Algerian War not shown from a French perspective, CINÉ-GUERRILLAS wades through the media and propaganda battle that played out during the liberation struggle, where cinema was mobilized as a political weapon of resistance against colonialism and empire as well as a social, imaginative medium of world-making. The screening will be introduced by artist, filmmaker, and researcher Carmen Amengual!

description: Manila-based filmmaker John Torres’s ambitious, visually striking sci-fi neo-noir about a mysteriously deadly driver-app functions as a thought-provoking inquiry into the larger forces—political, technological—that conspire to control our bodies and identities.

title: KAMA SUTRA: A TALE OF LOVE
description: In KAMA SUTRA: A TALE OF LOVE, Mira Nair examines the stigmatization of sexually promiscuous and unmarried women by the upper class in 16th-century India. The film follows Maya, a servant, who embarks on a journey of self-discovery through the art and spiritual practice of being a courtesan. Though ultimately a film about love, as signaled in the title, the film presents a rare historical fictional account of the spiritual art of working sex in the 16th-century.

title: Halloween (1978)
description: Fifteen years after murdering his sister on Halloween Night 1963, Michael Myers escapes from a mental hospital and returns to the small town of Haddonfield, Illinois to kill again.

title: Suicide Note
description: Shot largely in New York between 1976 and 1984, this newly restored, seldom-screened film from critic and artist Fred Camper is a fragmentary, diaristic work, capturing a cluttered and melancholic world on silent Super 8 Ektachrome reversal film.

title: In the Mouth of Madness
description: When horror novelist Sutter Cane (Jürgen Prochnow) goes missing, insurance investigator John Trent (Sam Neill) scrutinizes the claim made by his publisher, Jackson Harglow (Charlton Heston), and endeavors to retrieve a yet-to-be-released manuscript and ascertain the writer's whereabouts. Accompanied by the novelist's editor, Linda Styles (Julie Carmen), and disturbed by nightmares from reading Cane's other novels, Trent makes an eerie nighttime trek to a supernatural town in New Hampshire.

title: A Statement
description: In 1980, a group of environmental activists, scientists, and policymakers convened to discuss an alarming government study on climate change. Tom McCarthy (Spotlight) re-creates this historical moment with a brilliant ensemble cast including Paul Rudd, Amy Ryan, Paul Giamatti, John Turturro, and more.

title: Escape From New York with Escape from LA
description: Escape from New York in 4K Set in a grim, not-too-distant future where a walled-off Manhattan Island has been converted to a massive prison, John Carpenter’s Escape from New York confronts issues of social unrest, government surveillance and corruption. Kurt Russell plays Snake Plissken, a former bank robber and classic anti-hero, promised a pardon if he rescues the American president, who is trapped in Manhattan. The now-iconic character allowed Russell to shed his image as a Disney live-action leading man and kindled a long collaborative relationship with Carpenter. An early example of the cyberpunk genre in cinema, the film was a critical and commercial success, influencing many screenwriters and authors.
director: John Carpenter PRODUCED BY: Larry Franco, Debra Hill

title: COMBAT BREATHING: PERPETUAL RECURRENCES, PART 2: TESTAMENT
description: What characterizes the militant image? What historical conditions produced it and what kinds of histories were, in turn, produced by it? Where might it be found today? This program brings together a selection of contemporary works that frontally engage the legacies and continuities of Third Cinema and the tricontinental geographies of leftist, anti-colonial collaboration and mobilization that were this cultural movement’s primary condition of possibility. These works, as with Third Cinema, refuse clear-cut divisions between formal acuity and socio-political signification, and ground cinema’s documentative, archival, and imaginative powers as useful tools in the ongoing decolonizing process. Such a process involves grappling with the positive and negative lessons of prior movements in order to deduce alternative pathways to liberation. The selected films in this program revisit various sites of unfinished and unfolding anti-colonial struggle, from Ghana and Palestine to Yugoslavia and Algeria. Orienting viewers toward critical reflections on the historical twists and turns of the capitalist world-system on macro and interpersonal scales while remaining firmly rooted in their respective presents, the works by Mila Turajlić, John Akomfrah with Black Audio Film Collective, and Reem Shilleh further articulate the persisting structures of colonialism in their intensifications and mutations following from these mid-twentieth-century decolonization movements. The continuity of said conditions into this millennium can only ever engender, as these films themselves embody, the “perpetual recurrence” of a countervailing militant image. John Akomfrah & Black Audio Film Collective TESTAMENT 1988, 80 min, 16mm-to-DCP TESTAMENT is among the earliest feature-length works created by the pioneering UK-based art group, Black Audio Film Collective (of which John Akomfrah was a founding member). Synthesizing the languages of Third Cinema and avant-garde montage with the lamentational affects of postcolonial disillusionment, TESTAMENT offers a probing spectral meditation on the condition of the African postcolony. The film’s protagonist, Abena, is an exiled activist turned television reporter who returns to Ghana two decades after the 1966 coup that brought an end to President Kwame Nkrumah’s experiment in Pan-African socialism. Adrift in a “war zone of memories,” Abena is caught in the cleavage between public history and private memory. Characteristic of the collective’s now-signature blend of archival documents, fictional sequences, and layered sound scores, TESTAMENT enfolds depopulated frames, frigid tones, allegories of mourning, and a cast of enigmatic characters to evoke an emotional landscape of loss and arrested political possibility. Introduced by Christian Nyampeta.

title: HKFF: Remanence: The (Un)erasable - Moving Image+ Lecture Performance
What Can't Be Mentioned
description: Jackie (Tallie Medel) is a social worker in training picking at the knots of her own unresolved issues in microbudget maestro Dan Sallitt’s sequel to his notorious-yet-gentle 2012 taboo-buster The Unspeakable Act. Preceded by Nathan Silver’s Sounds From Home.

title: FUCKTOYS
description: Set in the alternate universe of Trashtown (but filmed in the American South), Annapurna Sriram’s debut feature film FUCKTOYS is a surrealist queer black comedy about a young woman on a mission to break a curse. Throughout a chaotic 24-hour journey, the protagonist (and her compatriots) navigate the intersecting oppressive systems of capitalism that make hustlers out of us all in pursuit of a spiritual, if not ecstatic, release of the body and soul.

title: Heil Jupiter!
description: This dreamlike astonishment from Carlos Reygadas (Silent Light, NYFF45) suggests a world balanced on the edge of the corporeal and the mythic—a work of feral cinematic expression that contrasts elemental pleasure and authoritarian brutality.

title: On the Silver Globe
description: The screening on August 22nd will feature an introduction by writer Daniel Bird. Subsequent screenings of On the Silver Globe will feature…

title: There Will Be Blood
description: Ruthless silver miner, turned oil prospector, Daniel Plainview moves to oil-rich California. Using his adopted son HW to project a trustworthy, family-man image, Plainview cons local landowners into selling him their valuable properties for a pittance. However, local preacher Eli Sunday suspects Plainviews motives and intentions, starting a slow-burning feud that threatens both their lives.

title: COMBAT BREATHING: PERPETUAL RECURRENCES, PART 3: PERPETUAL RECURRENCES
description: What characterizes the militant image? What historical conditions produced it and what kinds of histories were, in turn, produced by it? Where might it be found today? The continuity of said conditions into this millennium can only ever engender, as these films themselves embody, the “perpetual recurrence” of a countervailing militant image. Reem Shilleh PERPETUAL RECURRENCES 2016, 60 min, DCP A meta-reflection on the militant image and its contemporary reappearances, PERPETUAL RECURRENCES montages scenes extracted from numerous films and videos created over the last four decades by Palestinians and about Palestine, tracking thematic, gestural, and compositional repetitions between works produced during the Palestinian revolutionary period of 1968-82, the period following the 1993 Oslo Accords, and the volatile twenty-first century. Through Reem Shilleh’s methodical stitching together of repeating filmic occurrences – with respect to location, political discourse, mise-en-scene, objects, and so on – various scenes become unfixed from their narrative contexts and historical conditions, inviting expansive associations and haunting correspondences. Meandering in a seemingly improvised fashion between cinematic fragments of classroom instruction and conversing militants gathered under trees to handheld camera shots of refugee camps and moving car shots of streets, checkpoints, and landscapes, Shilleh’s vast media traversal materializes an equally lyrical and deconstructive reimagination of exercises in film programming. Introduced by Tiffany Malakooti.

title: Possession
description: After Anna (Isabelle Adjani) reveals to her husband, Mark (Sam Neill), that she is having an affair, she leaves him and their son. Mark is devastated, and seeks out Heinrich (Heinz Bennent), the man who cuckolded him, only to receive a beating. After a series of violent confrontations between Mark and Anna, Mark hires a private investigator to follow her. Anna descends into madness, and it's soon clear that she is hiding a much bigger secret -- one that is both inexplicable and shocking.

title: At Night
description: An expansive and provocative work of rich nocturnal beauty, British experimental filmmaker Beatrice Gibson’s feature is a shapeshifting, feminist meditation on the mind and body that follows an array of women over the course of one night in Paris. Winner of Best Emerging Director at the 2026 Locarno Film Festival.

title: Club Kid
description: Jordan Firstman’s wildly funny and remarkably assured feature debut about a washed-up thirtysomething New York scenester who discovers he has a 10-year-old British son swerves from irreverent satire to genuine pathos.

title: L'Innocente
description: In his final film, Luchino Visconti offers a poison-pill variation on the theme that consumed his career—the moral decay of the soul-sick aristocracy—while achieving a masterful synthesis of stylistic splendor and emotional intensity.

title: The Princess and the Frog
description: In New Orleans during the Jazz Age, a beautiful girl named Tiana (Anika Noni Rose) dreams of owning her own restaurant.…

title: Dao
description: French Senegalese filmmaker Alain Gomis’s (Félicité, NYFF55) ecstatic epic plunges headfirst into two separate yet intrinsically interconnected ceremonies—a memorial in Guinea-Bissau and a wedding in Paris—which Gomis cuts between with kinetic abandon.

title: Fatherland
description: Oscar-nominated director Paweł Pawlikowski (Cold War, NYFF56) won Best Director at Cannes for his most potent film yet, following novelist Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika Mann (Sandra Hüller) on a road trip across Germany in the aftermath of World War II.

title: What Can't Be Mentioned
description: Jackie (Tallie Medel) is a social worker in training picking at the knots of her own unresolved issues in microbudget maestro Dan Sallitt’s sequel to his notorious-yet-gentle 2012 taboo-buster The Unspeakable Act. Preceded by Nathan Silver’s Sounds From Home.

title: Young Frankenstein
description: Respected medical lecturer Dr. Frederick Frankenstein (Gene Wilder) learns that he has inherited his infamous grandfather's estate in Transylvania. Arriving at the castle, Dr. Frankenstein soon begins to recreate his grandfather's experiments with the help of servants Igor (Marty Feldman), Inga (Teri Garr) and the fearsome Frau Blücher (Cloris Leachman). After he creates his own monster (Peter Boyle), new complications ensue with the arrival of the doctor's fiancée, Elizabeth (Madeline Kahn).

title: Just Like Weather
description: A fascinating, ahead-of-its-time synthesis of fiction and documentary, Allen Fong’s third feature follows a couple from Hong Kong as they navigate domestic trials and tribulations before eventually heading to the United States.

title: Perfect Blue
description: "THE COLOUR OF ILLUSION IS PERFECT BLUE" A young Japanese singer is encouraged by her agent to quit singing and pursue an acting career, beginning with a role in a murder mystery TV show.

title: Cabaret
description: The second feature from director-choreographer Bob Fosse is one of his greatest works in any medium. It’s a dazzling adaptation of the John Kander-Fred Ebb Broadway show, inspired by Christopher Isherwood’s The Berlin Stories , and a fine demonstration of how a movie musical rooted in realism can be as satisfying as the more traditional variety. When naïve young Brian Roberts (Michael York as the Isherwood figure) moves into a Berlin boardinghouse in 1931, he is unprepared for his new neighbor—the brash, would-be star Sally Bowles, played by Liza Minnelli in her Oscar-winning, career-defining performance. The film received 10 nominations (including Best Picture) and won eight Oscars, including for Fosse’s direction, Joel Grey’s supporting performance, and the art direction of Rolf Zehetbauer, Jurgen Kiebach and set decorator Herbert Strabel. Their work brought the film’s time and place to life and provided Fosse with a realistically claustrophobic Kit Kat Klub, which nonetheless made room for the filmmaker’s typically thrilling musical numbers.

title: Yesterday Girl
description: One of the foundational films of the New German Cinema, the debut feature by the polymath artist and writer Alexander Kluge, about an East German woman’s acclimating to life on the other side of the wall, is a defining work of midcentury cinematic modernism.

title: Barry Lyndon
description: Stanley Kubrick bent the conventions of the historical drama to his own will in this dazzling vision of a pitiless aristocracy, adapted from a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray. In picaresque detail, Barry Lyndon chronicles the adventures of an incorrigible trickster (Ryan O’Neal) whose opportunism takes him from an Irish farm to the battlefields of the Seven Years’ War and the parlours of high society. For the most sumptuously crafted film of his career, Kubrick recreated the decadent surfaces and intricate social codes of the period, evoking the light and texture of eighteenth-century painting with the help of pioneering cinematographic techniques and lavish costume and production design, all of which earned Academy Awards. The result is a masterpiece—a sardonic, devastating portrait of a vanishing world whose opulence conceals the moral vacancy at its heart. Please Note: The film will be presented with a brief 5-10min intermission.
