title: The Witches
description: Accessible screening On the last Saturday of every month, the museum's Family Matinee is an accessible screening where we offer open captioning, keep the theater dimly lit, and maintain a lower volume for viewers who are neurodiverse. They walk among us, often appearing as ordinary women, but when one notices those purple eyes, gloved hands, and keen smell for children, it can mean only one thing: a witch. Luke, an orphaned 9-year-old, is vacationing in a seaside hotel with his grandma. So is an undercover witch convention. After the Grand High Witch turns Luke into a mouse, he finds himself scurrying to save the rest of the world’s children from a similar fate. This wicked tale, adapted from Roald Dahl’s children’s novel of the same name, features the work of Jim Henson’s Creature Shop in the iconic and terrifying reveal of the witches' true forms, and an unforgettable performance by Anjelica Huston as the Grand High Witch.

Craven is happy to provide both tension and self-parody as the body count mounts - but the victims aren't always the ones you'd expect.

title: EC: HOLLIS FRAMPTON
description: ZORNS LEMMA (1970, 60 min, 16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives.) “A major poetic work. Created and put together by a very clear eye-head, this original and complex abstract work moves beyond the letters of the alphabet, beyond words and beyond Freud. If you don’t understand it the first time you see it, don’t despair, see it again! When you finally ‘get it,’ a small light, possibly a candle, will light itself inside your forehead.” –Ernie Gehr & HAPAX LEGOMENA I: (nostalgia) (1971, 36 min, 16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives, MoMA, and the NYU Moving Image Archiving and Preservation Program, with funding from the National Film Preservation Foundation.) “In (nostalgia) the time it takes for a photograph to burn (and thus confirm its two-dimensionality) becomes the clock within the film, while Frampton plays the critic, asynchronously glossing, explicating, narrating, mythologizing his earlier art, and his earlier life, as he commits them both to the fire of a labyrinthine structure; for Borges too was one of his earlier masters, and he grins behind the facades of logic, mathematics, and physical demonstrations which are the formal metaphors for most of Frampton’s films.” –P. Adams Sitney Total running time: ca. 100 min. CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

title: Nosferatu
description: This performance will feature a live score performed by Hugo Max . "I first saw Murnau’s Symphony of Horror when I was nine years old. The film’s expressionistic images continue to haunt me, the chiaroscuro compositions tapping vividly into timeless subconscious fears. My improvisations on viola and piano draw inspiration from the leitmotifs and sound effects of 70s horror soundtracks and the languages of Second Viennese School composers contemporary to Murnau, also Jewish Traditional Music that informs my personal approach to creating a score for the film." - Hugo Max Please view this YouTube video for a sample of Hugo's work. Photo Credit - Richard Ecclestone An iconic film of the German expressionist cinema, and one of the most famous of all silent movies, F. W. Murnau's Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror continues to haunt — and, indeed, terrify — modern audiences with the unshakable power of its images. By teasing a host of occult atmospherics out of dilapidated set-pieces and innocuous real-world locations alike, Murnau captured on celluloid the deeply-rooted elements of a waking nightmare, and launched the signature "Murnau-style" that would change cinema history forever. In this first-ever screen adaptation of Bram Stoker's Dracula, a simple real-estate transaction leads an intrepid businessman deep into the superstitious heart of Transylvania. There he encounters the otherworldly Count Orlok — portrayed by the legendary Max Schreck, in a performance the very backstory of which has spawned its own mythology — who soon after embarks upon a cross-continental voyage to take up residence in a distant new land... and establish his ambiguous dominion. As to whether the count's campaign against the plague-wracked populace erupts from satanic decree, erotic compulsion, or the simple impulse of survival — that remains, perhaps, the greatest mystery of all in this film that's like a blackout...

title: PSYCHO
description: A secretary on the run for embezzlement takes refuge at a secluded California motel owned by a repressed man and his overbearing mother.

title: EC: FRANJU / GENET
description: Georges Franju BLOOD OF THE BEASTS / LE SANG DES BÊTES 1949, 20 min, 16mm. In French with English subtitles. “This documentary on the slaughterhouses of Paris is one of the great masterpieces of the subversive cinema; here, for once, we are face to face with death, and are neither protected nor cheated. […] A dream-like quality permeates the intense realism of the images; a surrealist intent – akin to Buñuel’s slitting of the eyeball in UN CHIEN ANDALOU – is discernible in this anti-bourgeois film. But the eyeball, however shocking, was fictional; BLOOD OF THE BEASTS is real.” –Amos Vogel, FILM AS A SUBVERSIVE ART Jean Genet UN CHANT D’AMOUR 1950, 26 min, 35mm, silent. Brand-new 35mm print by Anthology! “Genet’s only film – hounded by the censors, unavailable, secret – is an early and remarkably moving attempt to portray homosexual passions. Already a classic, it succeeds as perhaps no other film to intimate the explosive power of frustrated sex…. Like all Genet’s early work, the entire film is, in effect, a single onanistic fantasy, filled with desperate frustration and sensuous nostalgia.” –Amos Vogel, FILM AS A SUBVERSIVE ART “There’s no smoke without fire; UN CHANT D’AMOUR is a communion in which Genet takes us into the prison in order to liberate us from it.” –Derek Jarman Total running time: ca. 50 min. title: 30th Anniversary of The Craft
description: Sarah Bailey (Robin Tunney), a teen with a troubled past, moves to Los Angeles with her parents for a fresh start. Upon arrival in a Catholic school, Sarah is introduced to Bonnie (Neve Campbell), Rochelle (Rachel True), and Nancy (Fairuza Balk), a clique of outsiders rumored to practice witchcraft. Born a natural witch herself, Sarah is welcomed to the group, completing their coven. Together they invoke the ancient spirit of Manon, a pagan deity. Critically panned upon release, the film has since gained a cult following for its fierce, defiant portrayal of sisterhood, female agency, and rage, resonating with independent spirits, outcasts, and, as Balk so proudly puts it onscreen, “the weirdos, mister.” Join us as we gather after hours on All Hallows' Eve to commemorate 30 years since the release of a spellbinding classic.

HALLOWEEN II (1981): After failing to kill stubborn survivor Laurie and taking a bullet or six from former psychiatrist Dr. Sam Loomis, Michael Myers has followed Laurie to the Haddonfield Memorial Hospital, where she’s been admitted for Myers’ attempt on her life. title: Gosford Park
description: A weekend party at an English mansion in the 1930s leads to murder in this seriocomic whodunit, with Robert Altman directing an all-star cast. The Oscar-winning screenplay came via Julian Fellowes, who later explored the same milieu for Downton Abbey . The remarkable transatlantic cast includes Alan Bates, Bob Balaban (who also produced and came up with the story idea with Altman), Clive Owen, Kristin Scott Thomas, Emily Watson, and Helen Mirren and Maggie Smith, who were both nominated for their performances. The film’s seven nominations include Best Picture, Directing, and Art Direction, with production designer Stephen Altman and set decorator Anna Pinnock mixing authentic English mansions and soundstage sets to evoke the glamour and class divisions of the era.

title: Eungyo
description: Renowned poet Lee Juk-yo, 70, has become a recluse, mechanically pushing through his bland days, until they are pleasantly disrupted by high school student Eun-gyo, who comes into his life, bringing fresh energy. Lee starts working on a new novel, the dullness of his life giving way to color, possibilities, even daydreams. But that color starts to dim when Seo Ji-woo, Lee’s former student/assistant, becomes involved with Eun-gyo, and jealousy moves in instead. Based on a novel of the same name by Park Beom-shin, Eungyo explores themes of youth, and the poignant notion of its loss and redemption, with Park Hae-il delivering a notable interpretation of those themes through his character’s numbness and dissociation.

title: F. W. Murnau’s Faust
description: The haunting tale of a scholar, tempted by the Devil to sign away his soul in exchange for universal knowledge, has been a resonant cultural motif across five centuries. If the essential literary text for the Faustian myth is Johan Wolfgang von Goethe’s 19th century poetic drama, its cinematic equivalent is F. W. Murnau’s visionary 1926 silent adaptation, a masterpiece of haunting visual design that explores rich themes of morality and materialism. Starring Oscar-winning actor Emil Jannings as the terrifying trickster Mephisto, Murnau’s tale emerges from the disturbing underworld into the dreams of lost innocence for one of the most remarkable films from the German Expressionist milieu. A century later, scores of international filmmakers, including Guillermo del Toro, Jennifer Kent, and Robert Eggers, continue to be influenced by this masterwork. The Academy Museum is thrilled to present this film with live accompaniment on the occasion of its centennial and of MUBI’s newest publication, The Faust Bible: The Making of F. W. Murnau’s Masterpiece , which will be available for purchase in the Academy Museum Store. Programmed and note by K.J. Relth-Miller.

Bus Stop
description: This contemporary Western—in which Marilyn Monroe stars as saloon singer Cherie, who dreams of one day making it big in Hollywood—marked a turning point in Marilyn Monroe’s career. She had recently formed Marilyn Monroe Productions and signed a new contract with 20th Century-Fox, earning a higher salary and more creative agency in the process. For the role of Cherie, which was one of the more dramatic and serious of her career to date, she began working with Method acting pioneers Lee and Paula Strasberg, who placed an emphasis on delving into an actor’s own experiences.
director: Joshua Logan PRODUCED BY: Buddy Adler

title: Arrival: A Conversation with Denis Villeneuve and Dr. Nina Beguš
description: Inspired by Denis Villeneuve's 2016 sci-fi drama Arrival, the director joins artificial-humanities scholar Dr. Nina Beguš live in the David Geffen Theater for an inspiring conversation about how language acts as a technology; how fiction shapes artificial intelligence; and how encounters with non-human intelligence might transform our most basic understanding of thinking, learning, consciousness, time, and more. To mark the 10th anniversary of this thought-provoking film, an 8pm screening follows the discussion. About Nina Beguš Nina Beguš is a scholar and author working on AI, literature, and film. She is a researcher at the University of California, Berkeley, where she leads the Artificial Humanities research group. Her work examines how stories, concepts, and cultural archetypes shape technology. She is the author of Artificial Humanities: A Fictional Perspective on Language in AI and the editor of First Encounters with AI: Writers on Writing . Beguš holds a PhD in comparative literature from Harvard University and edits the Artificial Humanities book series at the University of Exeter Press. About Denis Villeneuve Denis Villeneuve is an Academy Award-nominated director, screenwriter and producer whose masterful world-building and unique visuals have established him as one of the premier filmmakers working today. In 2021, Dune: Part One earned six Academy Awards and multiple guild and critics' awards. Its sequel, Dune: Part Two (2024), expanded with bolder visual ambition and complexity, surpassing $700 million worldwide and winning two Academy Awards, with additional recognition from BAFTA, Critics Choice and major guilds. Villeneuve will conclude the trilogy with Dune: Part Three this December, reuniting its core cast. He is also set to direct the next James Bond film for Amazon MGM Studios. About the film In director Denis Villeneuve’s thoughtful science-fiction drama, adapted from Ted Chiang’s award-winning novella Story of Your Life , a linguistics expert (Amy Adams) is recruited by the government when massive alien spaceships suddenly land across the globe. The film’s production designer, Patrice Vermette (nominated with set decorator Paul Hotte) also designed the film’s alien language—one of Arrival ’s many remarkable and imaginative visuals. The film was nominated in seven categories, including Best Picture and Production Design; it won an Oscar for Sound Editing.

title: The Last Princess
description: In the early 20th century, the last princess of the Korean royal family under Japanese rule is forced to move to Japan to attend school, leaving behind her family, friends, and the only home she has ever known. Kim Jang-han (Park Hae-il), a childhood friend and Japanese army officer, helps to plan an escape route for her. This film, based on the real story of Princess Deokhye (Son Ye-jin), weaves fact with fiction to retell the story of a once-lost princess who stopped at nothing to return to the home she yearned for. –note written by Hannah Farkas.

title: The Zone of Interest
description: The commandant of Auschwitz, Rudolf Höss, and his wife Hedwig, strive to build a dream life for their family in a house and garden next to the camp.The commandant of Auschwitz, Rudolf Höss, and his wife Hedwig, strive to build a dream life for their family in a house and garden next to the camp.

title: Souls of Sin 35 mm & Miracle in Harlem 35 mm (12)
Bus Stop
description: This contemporary Western—in which Marilyn Monroe stars as saloon singer Cherie, who dreams of one day making it big in Hollywood—marked a turning point in Marilyn Monroe’s career. She had recently formed Marilyn Monroe Productions and signed a new contract with 20th Century-Fox, earning a higher salary and more creative agency in the process. For the role of Cherie, which was one of the more dramatic and serious of her career to date, she began working with Method acting pioneers Lee and Paula Strasberg, who placed an emphasis on delving into an actor’s own experiences.
director: Joshua Logan PRODUCED BY: Buddy Adler

title: Lost Boundaries (12)
description: This 1949 American drama looks at how 'liberal ideals' presented on screen back then; in which the groundbreaking filmmaker William Greaves stars as a young college graduate.

title: Fantastic Planet
description: On the planet Ygam, the Draags, extremely technologically and spiritually advanced blue humanoids, consider the tiny Oms, human beings descendants of Terra's inhabitants, as ignorant animals. Those who live in slavery are treated as simple pets and used to entertain Draag children; those who live hidden in the hostile wilderness of the planet are periodically hunted and ruthlessly slaughtered as if they were vermin.

title: My Dad is 100 Years Old with Rome, Open City
description: My Dad Is 100 Years Old This short tribute casts celebrated actress Isabella Rossellini as herself as well as various filmmakers who influenced or were influenced by her father, filmmaker Roberto Rossellini. Conceived by Isabella on the eve of her father’s centenary, she took a “docu-fantasia” concept to avant-garde filmmaker Guy Maddin after her delightful experience on his 2003 feature, The Saddest Music in the World. A beautiful cinema poem for a beloved father and artist.
director: Guy Maddin PRODUCED BY: Jody Shapiro

title: CAMP - A SHORT FILM SHOWCASE
description:
THE NICKEL teams up with cyberfemme studio EVERYONE IS A GIRL for a showcase of short films centred on the theme of CAMP, accompanied with readings.
The Nickel Cinema’s regular roster of B-movies, softcores, and underrated gems has begun to shed some buttery spotlight on underrepresented cinematic traditions. At EIAG, we make collaborative projects about the feminine, the seductive, the virtual, and the covert. For this CAMP showcase, we are joining forces to present films from our community that are not afraid to play, deceive, and perform. Join us for a night of London’s most sparkliest, performative, abject, delicious, and scandalicious emerging cinema.
Programme of films to be announced.

title: Memories of Murder
description: Bong Joon Ho’s phenomenal breakthrough film stars Park Hae-il as an enigmatic young loner and observer whose innocent demeanor seems too wholesome to be true. Inspired by a true story, Memories of Murder centers around the gruesome serial killings of women in South Korea in the 1980s, investigated by Doo-man (Song Kang-ho), a detective who relies on instinct rather than fact. Bong’s vision, which challenges conventional components of storytelling and blurs the boundaries between genres, is meticulously orchestrated in this crime thriller, and Park’s elegantly simple depiction of a complicated character is phenomenal.

title: Viva Ingrid! with Journey to Italy
description: Viva Ingrid! A moving documentary tribute to a mother, wife, and actress, this mix of home movies, newsreels, and clips from films by Roberto Rossellini paints a shortform portrait of three-time Academy Award-winning Swedish actress Ingrid Bergman, as realized by one of Rossellini’s grandsons.

title: Excalibur
description: Arthur fulfills his fate by bringing together the Knights of the Round Table at Camelot and unifying the country. However, this flawed monarch faces greater tests ahead in pursuit of love, the Holy Grail, and his nation's survival.

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: The Haunted Mansion
description: Based on the iconic Disneyland ride, The Haunted Mansion stars Eddie Murphy as real estate agent Jim Evers, a workaholic who wants to close a mansion deal before going on a much-needed vacation with his wife, Sara, and his kids. Upon their arrival, the family is lured apart by ghosts who believe Sara can set them free by joining them in the afterlife. The Evers family battles ghosts, zombies, and spiders to save Sara from eternal damnation, also encountering – of course -- references to the amusement park ride, including Hidden Mickeys and the theme song, “Grim Grinning Ghosts.”
director: Rob Minkoff PRODUCED BY: Don Hahn, Andrew Gunn

description: A free screening of an episode from the long-running TV series launched in 1968, one of the first to offer alternative media representations of Black politics and concerns.

title: Rossellini Through His Own Eyes
description: “Neo-realism is above all a moral standpoint from which to look at the world,” Roberto Rossellini proclaimed in 1954, and this conviction led him not just to make lasting contributions to the neo-realist mode, but also equipped him to articulate his artistic ideas into spoken language. In this loving documentary portrait of the father of the cinematic movement, scholar Adriano Aprà uses archival footage and interviews with Rossellini to underscore the filmmaker’s unique eloquence, and the ways his life and work combined into his singular vision.

title: Rome, Open City
description: Made for less than $20,000 just after the liberation of Italy by US forces, Rossellini’s first installment in his Neo-Realist Trilogy, which also includes Paisan (1946, screening on November 15) and Germany, Year Zero (1948, screening the same day), is also considered the first product of neo-realism. The devastation of Nazi-occupied Rome serves as an all-too-real backdrop for a story that could have been ripped from the headlines: a resistance leader (Aldo Fabrizi) is pursued through town as he seeks shelter and a safe escape. With “the terror of German occupation [...] still vivid in the minds of everyone,” (Patrizio Rossi, 1988) including Rossellini’s lead actress, the great Anna Magnani, Rome, Open City serves as a prototype for a series of films that characterize the best of Italian cinema.

title: The 7th Voyage of Sinbad
description: When a princess is shrunken by an evil wizard, Sinbad must undertake a quest to an island of monsters to cure her and prevent a war.

title: Imamura: Profound Desires of the Gods
Chicago
description: Wannabe celeb Roxie Hart murders her lover and is sent to jail, only to discover that a tabloid scandal may be her best route to true stardom in this stylish and lively version of the stage musical. Rob Marshall, making his feature directing debut, pays due homage to the distinctive style of Bob Fosse’s original Broadway production while bringing his own energetic approach to the material, which features such classic Kander and Ebb songs as “All That Jazz,” “Cell Block Tango,” and “Mister Cellophane.” The first movie musical to win Best Picture in the 34 years since Oliver! (1968), it received 13 nominations and also won for Costume Design, Film Editing, Sound, Catherine Zeta-Jones’s commanding performance as Roxie’s frenemy Velma Kelly. Production designer John Myhre and set decorator Gordon Sim also won for their Art Direction, featuring just the right blend of fantasy and reality.

title: Waikiki Brothers
description: Park Hae-il’s big-screen debut is Yim Soon-rye’s second feature, which received critical praise upon its 2001 release, establishing Yim as one of Korea’s most significant directors. Seong-woo, lead singer and guitarist of Waikiki Brothers—a band formed with his friends back in high school—returns to his hometown with his bandmates in hopes of repairing their fragile relationship. But the band stagnates, and Seong-woo is torn between a dream that’s out of reach and his thin grasp on reality. Park, who portrays the teen version of Seong-woo, generates youthful energy, evoking the purity that Seong-woo and his bandmates once carried and now long for. Yim’s insightful and humane perception of the cruel split between dreams and reality in modern Korea permeates this portrayal of her sympathetic and intricate characters.

title: SCC: Persepolis (12A) x Marsm
description: Revisit Marjane Satrapi's acclaimed animated film about growing up in Tehran during and after Iran’s 1979 revolution, based on her autobiographical graphic novel.

title: Some Like It Hot
description: Marilyn Monroe’s work in director Billy Wilder’s comedic classic is often cited as her best. The film was controversial for its racy humor and story about two musicians (Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon) who disguise themselves as women to evade the Mafia. But of equal scandal were the Oscar-winning costumes made by Orry-Kelly for Monroe’s Sugar Kane Kowalczyk. Both dresses are on display in the exhibit Marilyn Monroe: Hollywood Icon , on view through February 28, 2027. Some Like It Hot was made during a year of dramatic highs and lows for Monroe, with this film standing as a high point.
director: Billy Wilder PRODUCED BY: Billy Wilder

title: Moss
description: Hae-guk (Park Hae-il) receives word that his estranged father has passed away, bringing him to an unusual village for the funeral. Sensing his presence is unwelcome, Hae-guk grows suspicious and begins to sense a deeper truth behind his father's death . Adapted from a Korean webtoon, Moss submerges audiences in a dark and thrilling mystery, blending suspense and horror to create a world of uncertainty. –Note written by Hannah Farkas.

description: Two films that explore psychodrama as a way of analysing and addressing racial inequality through group workshops, from 1969 and 1988.

title: War for the Planet of the Apes
description: The third film in the contemporary version of the Planet of the Apes series finds the ape leader Caesar (another remarkable motion capture performance by Andy Serkis) seeking a safe haven for the survivors of a human-led massacre, only to wind up in a labor camp run by a vicious military officer (Woody Harrelson). The film was nominated for the visual effects by Joe Letteri, Daniel Barrett, Dan Lemmon and Joel Whist, who depict the film’s ape characters and wintry, post-apocalyptic setting with astonishing realism.
director: Matt Reeves PRODUCED BY: Peter Chernin, Dylan Clark, Rick Jaffa, Amanda Silver

title: Kingdom of Heaven: Director's Cut
description: Ridley Scott's extended cut of an epic adventure about a common man who finds himself thrust into a decades-long war. Orlando Bloom plays a humble blacksmith who discovers that he is the son of a knght, and travels to the Holy Land to fight in the crusades. A stranger in a strange land, he serves a doomed King, falls in love with an exotic and forbidden Queen, and rises to knighthood. Ultimately, he must protect the people of Jerusalem from overwhelming forces, while striving to keep a fragile peace.

title: The Love Witch
description: “She Loved Men... To Death.” Addicted to love, Elaine – the love witch – casts love and sex spells to seek her perfect man, finding herself with more dead bodies than she does a long-term partner… A visually-striking, humorous and thought-provoking film by the continuously playful Anna Biller, The Love Witch has caused immense debate by audiences through its feminist themes. Visually drenched in 1970s fashion and cinematography, the film´s style feels as magical as the love witch herself. The Love Witch is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: Jason and the Argonauts
description: Jason, a fearless sailor and explorer, returns to his home land of Thessaly after a long voyage to claim his rightful throne. He learns, however, that he must first find the magical Golden Fleece. To do so, he must embark on an epic quest fraught with fantastic monsters and terrible perils.

title: The Time Masters
description: Directed by visionary science-fiction animator René Laloux (Fantastic Planet) and designed by the legendary Jean Giraud (a.k.a. Mœbius) The Time Masters is a visually fantastic foray into existentialist space adventure. After his parents are killed on the dangerous planet Perdide, young Piel (voiced by Frédéric Legros) survives by maintaining radio contact with Jaffar (Jean Valmont), a pilot transporting the exiled Prince Matton (Yves-Marie Maurin) and Princess Belle (Monique Thierry) from their former kingdom. Jaffar seeks the help of Silbad (Michel Elias), a cheerful old-timer who knows how to circumvent Perdide’s hazards, including brain-devouring insects and watery graves. Along the way, Jaffar and company encounter a pair of impish homunculi stowaways, identity-less angels controlled by an amorphous hive mind, and the Masters of Time, mysterious beings who can bend reality and perhaps reveal to the heroes their secret origins and destinies. title: Black Fire
description: Since 2013, artist Kevin Jerome Everson and author and historian Claudrena N. Harold have cooperated on a series of lyrical short films—13 to date—that explore Black intellectual, social, and political life at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, where both are professors. Collectively titled Black Fire , these works highlight the spaces where Black students have studied, learned, and organized through the years, including the school's student-run newspaper and a bus stop that became a locus for collective action. Through short films spotlighting figures such as Paulette Jones Morant, one of the first Black woman scholastic athletes at UVA, and Vivian Gordon, the director of UVA’s Black Studies program from 1974–1980, Black Fire creates significant space for otherwise under-the-radar figures. Employing interviews and reenactment, often casting their students as performers, Everson and Harold's films bring the history of UVA, as well as the historical experiences of Black students and faculty across the US, into meaningful conversation with the present day. Filmmakers Kevin Jerome Everson and Claudrena N. Harold appear in conversation after the films, moderated by filmmaker Cauleen Smith. Special thanks to Madeleine Molyneaux, Sam Raphael, and Now Instant Image Hall.

title: Evangelion: Death (True)² + The End of Evangelion : Double Feature
description: EVANGELION: DEATH (TRUE)²: A recap of the first 24 episodes of Neon Genesis Evangelion. Fifteen years after the Second Impact, apathetic teen Shinji joins his father's group NERV to fight the Angels. But the truth may destroy them all. THE END OF EVANGELION: Concurrent theatrical ending of the TV series Neon Genesis Evangelion (1995). Seele orders an all-out attack on NERV, aiming to destroy the Evas before Gendo can trigger Third Impact and Instrumentality under his control.

title: Troy
description: In year 1250 B.C. during the late Bronze age, two emerging nations begin to clash. Paris, the Trojan prince, convinces Helen, Queen of Sparta, to leave her husband Menelaus, and sail with him back to Troy. After Menelaus finds out that his wife was taken by the Trojans, he asks his brother Agamemnon to help him get her back. Agamemnon sees this as an opportunity for power. They set off with 1,000 ships holding 50,000 Greeks to Troy.

title: Frankenweenie
description: Based on Tim Burton’s 1984 short film, Frankenweenie follows young Victor Frankenstein as he goes about his childhood making short films with his four-legged canine friend, Sparky. When Sparky is killed by a car, a distraught Victor resurrects him. Soon other children start resurrecting their own pets, and a horde of undead creatures wreaks havoc, spurring the adults to plot Sparky’s permanent demise. This black-and-white stop motion Frankenstein adaptation features a score by frequent Burton collaborator Danny Elfman and is filled with homages to the classic horror films Burton grew up loving, resulting in a scary and sweet fairytale that will dazzle children and charm adults.
director: Tim Burton PRODUCED BY: Allison Abbate, Tim Burton

title: Jealousy Is My Middle Name
description: Park Hae-il plays Lee Won-sang, the hero of Park Chan-ok’s debut feature, in his second big-screen appearance. Lee is a 27-year-old graduate student in literature, finishing up his thesis before he leaves for London. When he starts writing an article for a magazine as a favor, he realizes that the head editor, Han Yun-shik, is the reason his girlfriend left him. Lee’s complicated feelings toward Han, a mixture of admiration and jealousy, brings more confusion when he is introduced to a mesmerizing photographer, Park Sung-yeon, a cool, down-to-earth woman who is also having an affair with Han. Calm on the surface but roiling underneath, the story explores human emotions in a macro lens, excavating endless variables that shape characters while they struggle to stay composed. Park’s undefinable approach to Lee allows his character’s purity and honesty to roam free.

The Grand Budapest Hotel
description: Writer-director Wes Anderson was inspired by Austrian novelist Stefan Zweig (1881-1942) for his seriocomic and visually dazzling story about a posh resort, its vain concierge (Ralph Fiennes in a peerless comic performance) and a young lobby boy (Tony Revolori). Anderson directed an all-star international cast and brought his distinctive visual sensibilities to his original story (written with Hugo Guinness), set in a fictional European country on the eve of war. The film received nine nominations including Best Picture and won Oscars for Alexandre Desplat’s effervescent score, Milena Canonero’s costume design, the makeup and hair creations of Frances Hannon and Mark Coulier, and the production design of Adam Stockhausen and his set decorator, Anna Pinnock, who transformed a vacant German department store into the eponymous hotel.

title: Paisàn
description: The second installment in his WWII trilogy and one of Rossellini’s favorites of his films, the episodic Paisàn is another depiction of the tribulations of the Italians under German occupation. Its title translates to “fellow countryman” and takes a broader view of Italy than his previous Rome, Open City (1945) , moving the action outside the capital to focus on the interactions between American armed forces and the country residents impacted by conflict. Future Italian auteur Federico Fellini co-wrote the screenplay, which came together on the fly, with dialogue of each sequence written just before it was filmed.
director: Roberto Rossellini PRODUCED BY: Rod E. Geiger, Roberto Rossellini

title: Germany Year Zero
description: Released the same year the first theories of neo-realism were published in film magazines Esprit, La Revue du Cinéma , and Bianco e Nero by acclaimed critics, including André Bazin, Germany Year Zero rounds out Rossellini’s WWII trilogy and brings a continental scope to the devastating impact of Hitler’s final solution. By centering the story on a young boy navigating the devastating implications of war, Rossellini accentuates the stark contrast between generations. A major influence on François Truffaut’s The 400 Blows (1959) and cast with people the director found by exploring the four zones of Berlin, Germany Year Zero would, Rossellini hoped, “reproduce the truth exactly as the camera saw it for that audience through the entire world which has a heart capable of love and a brain capable of thought.”

title: The Misfits
description: Penned by Arthur Miller, this contemporary Western centers on the recently divorced Roslyn (Marilyn Monroe) and her relationship with an aging former cowboy, Gay (Clark Gable), who now survives by rounding up wild mustangs to sell them to a slaughterhouse. Considered a commercial failure at the time of its original release, the film has since been regarded as a classic by critics and audiences, perhaps notably because it was the final completed film of both Gable and Monroe, and a fitting bookend to Monroe’s career—she credited Huston for her first big break in his The Asphalt Jungle (1950).
director: John Huston PRODUCED BY: Frank E. Taylor

title: Relaxed Screening: Animation in Love: Night is Short (15)
L’amore
description: “I’ve made films in episodes because I feel more at ease like that.” —Roberto Rossellini, 1952 Rossellini’s appreciation for episodic storytelling, which his later forays into television allowed him to explore with more freedom, first began in feature-length filmmaking. Part one, titled “Una voce umana,” is based on a play by Jean Cocteau and features the filmmaker’s then-lover, esteemed actress Anna Magnani, known only as the woman on the phone, speaking to a former flame. In part two, “Il miracolo,” a woman is sure she is pregnant with the child of a saint. Dubbed the best foreign film that year by New York critics, Amore was also met with derision when Rossellini was charged with blasphemy by the city’s archbishop due to the content of the film’s second half.

description: “Doc” McCoy (Steve McQueen) is unexpectedly freed from a lengthy prison sentence to take part in a bank robbery, but there may be no one he can trust, not even his seemingly loyal wife (Ali MacGraw). For one of his first produced screenplays, Walter Hill adapted one of noir master Jim Thompson’s darkest novels into a more light-hearted but still cynical romantic thriller, with director Sam Peckinpah staging the film’s action sequences with his usual vividness.

title: We Are the Night
description: Spotted and romantically pursued by the leader of a matriarchal vampire trio, down-on-her-luck Lena is bitten and turned into one of them. Overcoming the initial shock, she finds the eternal lifestyle agreeable – riches, partying, fashion – all until the bloodthirst of her companions become too much. Sink your teeth into this rarely screened vampire film, Wir sind die Nacht! Not officially released in the UK, director Dennis Gansel offers a campy and biting adventure set in the heart of Berlin. The film both plays with traditional vampire rules and introduces new, playful ways to depict the immortal creature. Some fans claim that they would do “anything for lesbian vampire Nina Hoss”, and for the avid vampire fan, this film has become a must-watch. We Are the Night is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: Carrie
description: Celebrate the 50th anniversary of Brian De Palma’s horror classic Carrie (1976) with a screening of the film and a conversation with its star, Sissy Spacek. Tickets go on sale mid-August, with early access for Academy Museum members. This event has early access for Academy Museum members. Please check back for ticket on-sale information. Not a member? Join now for early access to this program, plus year-round discounts and free general admission.

title: Ten Years of Monkey Tennis (with Peter Serafinowicz)
description: "One of the best TV and film podcasts" - The Telegraph Join the hosts of chart-topping, award-winning Alan Partridge fan podcast Monkey Tennis as they celebrate a full decade of dissecting, discussing and celebrating Norwich's finest broadcaster, joined by very special guest, BAFTA nominee, comedy legend and Partridge alumni Peter Serafinowicz . This special intimate one-off anniversary live podcast recording sees your four dalendless hosts return to the scene of their first ever live show, to recognise and revel in Alan Gordon Partridge's glory. They'll also be speaking to star of I'm Alan Partridge (as well as Guardians of the Galaxy, Amandaland, Parks & Recreation, Shaun of the Dead, Spaced and 100+ more), Peter Serafinowicz , about his epic career and his time as Alan's antagonist and lover of American things, Tex. In the meantime, catch up on over 150 episodes of the Monkey Tennis podcast, covering almost everything Alan's ever done, at podfollow.com/monkeytennis

title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: The Misfits
description: Penned by Arthur Miller, this contemporary Western centers on the recently divorced Roslyn (Marilyn Monroe) and her relationship with an aging former cowboy, Gay (Clark Gable), who now survives by rounding up wild mustangs to sell them to a slaughterhouse. Considered a commercial failure at the time of its original release, the film has since been regarded as a classic by critics and audiences, perhaps notably because it was the final completed film of both Gable and Monroe, and a fitting bookend to Monroe’s career—she credited Huston for her first big break in his The Asphalt Jungle (1950).
director: John Huston PRODUCED BY: Frank E. Taylor

title: Your Name [Kimi no Na wa.]
description: Two teenagers share a profound, magical connection upon discovering they are swapping bodies. Things manage to become even more complicated when the boy and girl decide to meet in person.

title: Gandahar
description: An entire civilisation must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux's final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet's outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society's strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar's very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

title: Journey to Italy
description: US restoration premiere “It was very important for me to show Italy, Naples,” Rossellini said in 1954, “that strange atmosphere so imbued with a very real, very immediate, very deep feeling: the sense of eternal life.” The fantastic Ingrid Bergman and George Sanders play Katherine and Alex Joyce, an unhappily married English couple of eight years whose trip to Italy takes them along separate, and possibly permanently diverging, paths. Bergman’s fourth film with then-husband Roberto Rossellini allows her to relax into a natural acting style that would become a blueprint for 1960s actors and filmmakers interested in presenting fresh, grounded performances.

title: La La Land
description: Sebastian (Ryan Gosling) and Mia (Emma Stone) are drawn together by their common desire to do what they love. But as success mounts they are faced with decisions that begin to fray the fragile fabric of their love affair, and the dreams they worked so hard to maintain in each other threaten to rip them apart.

title: The Prestige
description: Period thriller set in Edwardian London where two rival magicians, partners until the tragic death of an assistant during a show, feud bitterly after one of them performs the ultimate magic trick - teleportation. His rival tries desperately to uncover the secret of his routine, experimenting with dangerous new science as his quest takes him to the brink of insanity and jeopardises the lives of everyone around the pair.

title: Matilda (30th Anniversary)
description: Based on the beloved book from Roald Dahl, this film adaptation directed by Danny DeVito tells the story of Matilda, a…

title: Wendell & Wild
description: The director of Coraline (2009) and The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993) brings his eerie whimsy to a macabre tale of an orphaned punk, Kat. Haunted by her parents' death and disappointed with other adults, she is shuttled off to a failing boarding school, where she discovers her ability to summon demons. Two of them, voiced by Keegan-Michael Key and Jordan Peele, manipulate Kat into bringing them to the land of the living with a promise of resurrecting her parents, but bringing people back from the dead never turns out quite as planned. With spectacular stop-motion animation, an inspired Afro-punk soundtrack, and kooky antics aplenty, this is a charming take on the importance of community, standing up for what's right, and befriending your demons.
director: Henry Selick PRODUCED BY: Henry Selick, Ellen Goldsmith-Vein, Jordan Peele, Win Rosenfeld

title: John Jeremey: Blues Like Showers of Rain (cert tbc)
The Misfits
description: Penned by Arthur Miller, this contemporary Western centers on the recently divorced Roslyn (Marilyn Monroe) and her relationship with an aging former cowboy, Gay (Clark Gable), who now survives by rounding up wild mustangs to sell them to a slaughterhouse. director: John Huston PRODUCED BY: Frank E. Taylor

title: The Films of Madeline Anderson and St. Clair Bourne 196-1974 (15)
Tenet
description: Armed with only one word—Tenet—and fighting for the survival of the entire world, the Protagonist journeys through a twilight world of international espionage on a mission that will unfold in something beyond real time.

title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: Stromboli
description: Named for the volcanic island in the Tyrrhenian Sea, Rossellini's first collaboration with Swedish actress Ingrid Bergman is a heartbreaking tale about a young Baltic woman who follows an Italian fisherman to his tiny, isolated village. Married swiftly after their release from an internment camp, she begins to struggle as her refined upbringing clashes with the rough local lifestyle, causing strain on her marriage and her psyche. It was Bergman who first contacted Rossellini after seeing Paisàn in 1948 in hopes of collaborating, and the making of Stromboli marks the beginning of a love affair that ended the filmmaker’s marriage and caused an international scandal when Bergman announced their pregnancy. For Rossellini, the project also signals a creative shift, at least to some critics, away from realism and into a deeply psychological phase.

title: Matilda (30th Anniversary)
description: Based on the beloved book from Roald Dahl, this film adaptation directed by Danny DeVito tells the story of Matilda, a…

title: Clash of the Titans
description: To win the right to marry his love, the beautiful princess Andromeda, and fulfil his destiny, half-God-half-mortal Perseus must complete various tasks including taming Pegasus, capturing Medusa's head and battling the feared Kraken.

title: Insomnia
description: Under the glare of the permanent Alaska sun, two veteran Los Angeles police officers close in on their suspect in the murder of a teenage girl. But when officer Will Dormer (Al Pacino) accidentally shoots his partner, their murder suspect, reclusive novelist Walter Finch (Robin Williams), witnesses the shooting--and blackmails Dormer. Now, as an idealistic local detective (Hillary Swank) investigates the case, and the stakes rise, Dormer's sanity begins to falter.

title: The Favourite
description: Olivia Colman won the Best Actress Oscar for her richly detailed performance as England’s Queen Anne, who finds two women competing for her affections in their quest for power: the aristocratic Lady Sarah (supporting actress nominee Rachel Weisz) and the impoverished Abigail Hill (supporting actress nominee Emma Stone). Working from a darkly comic, fact-based screenplay by Deborah Davis and Tony McNamara, director Yorgos Lanthimos ( Poor Things , 2023) subverts the cliches of historical dramas to startling effect. The Favourite’s 10 nominations include Best Picture, Directing and Original Screenplay. Nominated production designer Fiona Crombie and set decorator Alice Felton used a stark, black-and-white palate for their regal settings, matching Sandy Powell’s elegant, nominated costume designs.

title: Inception
description: A thief who steals corporate secrets through the use of dream-sharing technology is given the inverse task of planting an idea into the mind of a C.E.O., but his tragic past may doom the project and his team to disaster.

title: The Flowers of St. Francis
description: Inspired by the writings of Saint Francis of Assisi and the hagiographic texts about his loyal follower Brother Juniper, The Flowers of St. Francis is composed of simple vignettes that beautifully illustrate the humane life lessons of the People’s Saint. Using only one professional actor, with the rest of the cast comprised of friars from the Franciscan monastery, Rossellini’s film brings into focus, as he put it in 1950, “the merrier aspect of the Franciscan experience, the playfulness, the ‘perfect delight,’ the freedom that the spirit finds in poverty, and in absolute detachment from material things.”

title: Interstellar
description: In Earth's future, a global crop blight and second Dust Bowl are slowly rendering the planet uninhabitable. Professor Brand (Michael Caine), a brilliant NASA physicist, is working on plans to save mankind by transporting Earth's population to a new home via a wormhole. But first, Brand must send former NASA pilot Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) and a team of researchers through the wormhole and across the galaxy to find out which of three planets could be mankind's new home.

title: SCC: The Odyssey (15)
description: Christopher Nolan brings one of the world's most famous ancient texts to life in this mythic action epic starring Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Tom Holland and more, screened on glorious 35mm film.

title: Gandahar
description: An entire civilisation must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux's final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet's outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. title: Short Films by William Greaves 1981-1988 (
description: This programme brings together films by William Greaves exploring Black history and the lives of women working at NASA, created in 1980s America.

title: The Machine That Kills Bad People
description: One of Roberto Rossellini's most singular and unheralded works, this potent blend of neorealism and fantasy is an idiosyncratic, lighthearted fable. In a fishing village on the Amalfi Coast, a stranger claiming to be a saint bestows a photographer’s camera with the power to kill bad people by photographing existing pictures of them. Initially, the photographer uses his newfound weapon to eliminate abusers of power. But before long, he succumbs to the very same amoral selfishness he once claimed to despise. When asked in a 1970 interview whether the film was about filmmaking, Rossellini replied, "It's rather a game, an attempt at comedy, [...] an isolated experiment."
director: Roberto Rossellini PRODUCED BY: Salvo D’Angelo

title: The Grandmaster (Extended Cut)
description: Ip Man's peaceful life in Foshan changes after Gong Yutian seeks an heir for his family in Southern China. Ip Man then meets Gong Er who challenges him for the sake of regaining her family's honor. After the Second Sino-Japanese War, Ip Man moves to Hong Kong and struggles to provide for his family. In the mean time, Gong Er chooses the path of vengeance after her father was killed by Ma San. Wong Kar-wai’s original 130-minute cut on the big screen in the UK for the first time, courtesy Janus Films

title: Thief
description: A highly skilled jewel thief, Frank (James Caan) longs to leave his dangerous trade and settle down with his girlfriend, Jessie (Tuesday Weld). Eager to make one last big score in order to begin living a legitimate life, Frank reluctantly associates with Leo (Robert Prosky), a powerful gangster. Unfortunately for Frank, Leo wants to keep him in his employ, resulting in a tense showdown when he finally tries to give up his criminal activities once and for all.

title: Booker T. Washington: The Life and the Legacy of Ida B. Wells (15)
Boogie Nights
description: In the San Fernando Valley in 1977, teenage busboy Eddie Adams (Mark Wahlberg) gets discovered by porn director Jack Horner (Burt Reynolds), who transforms him into adult-film sensation Dirk Diggler. Brought into a supportive circle of friends, including fellow actors Amber Waves (Julianne Moore), Rollergirl (Heather Graham) and Reed Rothchild (John C. Reilly), Dirk fulfills all his ambitions, but a toxic combination of drugs and egotism threatens to take him back down.

title: Imamura: Sun in the Last Days of the Shogunate
Miami Vice
description: A case involving drug lords and murder in South Florida takes a personal turn for undercover detectives Sonny Crockett (Colin Farrell) and Ricardo Tubbs (Jamie Foxx). Unorthodox Crockett gets involved romantically with the Chinese-Cuban wife of a trafficker of arms and drugs, while Tubbs deals with an assault on those he loves.

title: Ginger Snaps
description: “I get this ache... And I, I thought it was for sex, but it's to tear everything to fucking pieces.” A wild and bloodthirsty hound has ravaged through the small town of Bailey Downs, attacking the neighbourhood's pet dogs. When the two teenage outcasts, the Fitzgerald sisters, stumble upon the creature one night, their lives change forever as Ginger is bitten, and her body starts to change. A true feast of practical effects, 2000s grunge, and snappy one-liners; Ginger Snaps has been credited in hindsight as a predecessor to the “maneater” supernatural woman most famously seen in Jennifer´s Body (2009). A coming-of-age story told in a fresh perspective; for maybe the true terror lies in growing up, or maybe it lies in the bloodthirsty hound who calls herself your sister. Ginger Snaps is featured as part of MANEATERS, a season exploring the female supernatural on screen. The season is presented with the National Film and Television School’s Film Studies, Programming and Curation MA.

title: Solve Along A Murder She Wrote
description: Cult hit event Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote returns to the Prince Charles Cinema with an interactive screening of a classic Murder, She Wrote episode. Watch as Cabot Cove gets caught up in a murder mystery only JB Fletcher (or you!) can solve! Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote is a unique and hilarious night featuring games, prizes and audience participation, with special permission from NBC Universal Television. See the show Time Out rated one of 2021 and 2019’s 50 Great Nights Out in London that has played to sell-out audiences across the UK and Australia. Hosted by super-fan Tim Benzie, Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote features: * A race to solve to the crime, via the Fameometer and the Suspiciometer! * A Cabot Cove quiz! * A singalong to the theme tune with new lyrics! * Clips and biogs of the campy guest stars! Tim Benzie is obsessed with Murder, She Wrote, having watched the original series when it was first broadcast, and now relishing the repeats on television everywhere. Tim is the writer/performer of “It’s a Mystery!”, all about our love of whodunnits. An award-winning playwright and co-writer of the Royal Vauxhall Tavern’s 2017-2023 pantos (‘Goosed’, ‘Rubbed’, ‘Slipped’, ‘Pricked’, ‘Cracked’ and ‘Tossed’). He is the co-producer of the camp club night PopHorror. Visit us at www.solvealongamurdershewrote.com , or follow us on Instagram, Twitter and Facebook @solvealonga. 2026 SCHEDULE: Tuesday 8th September 2026 "Dead Man's Gold" Directed by Seymour Robbie Starring Angela Lansbury, Leslie Nielsen, Tom Bosley 1986 | 120mins | USA Thursday 22nd October 2026 Encore Halloween special - "The Witch's Curse" Directed by Jerry Jameson Starring Angela Lansbury, Robert Vaughn, Mary Crosby 1992 | 120mins | USA Thursday 26th November 2026 New episode TBC Thursday 17th December 2026 Encore screening - "A Christmas Secret" Directed by Anthony Pullen Shaw Starring Angela Lansbury, Larry Wilcox, Amy Brenneman 1992 | 120mins | USA *** The Critics speak! “You’ll be swept away with Jessica Fletcher feels … it has the BEST HOST.” - Time Out London "A cinematic, theatrical and hilarious experience ... Before the night I had never seen an episode of Murder, She Wrote before, unlike some dedicated fans who had even dressed up. However, this really was an evening everyone could enjoy.” - Nottingham Post "As soon as I saw it was on at the [Edinburgh] Fringe I elbowed my way through the other BW reviewers, pushed a couple of them over … just so I could get to the front of the queue and see this show again. And it did not disappoint ... I'd go again in a heartbeat.” 5 stars ***** - Broadway World "The self-confessed super-fan and award-winning playwright will lead you into a silly whirlwind of nostalgic giggle, using his wealth of camp trivia and sound logic to solve these killings.” 5 stars ***** - One4Review "Benzie knows how to put on a great show ... I would happily see it again, with all the fervour of the ‘Jessica Fletcher eating popcorn’ meme." 5 stars ***** - Everything Theatre “Whodunnit? Tim dunnit – and he did it so well I can’t wait for the next one!" 5 stars ***** - Fairy-Powered Productions “I’d challenge anyone to sit through this show and not get utterly invested in figuring out whodunit.” 4 stars **** - West End Wilma “This is a highly entertaining production even if you have never seen an episode, filled with outrageous fun." 4 stars **** - British Theatre Guide "For a funny, campy evening, there is little that could beat Solve-Along-A-Murder-She-Wrote’s unique qualities and Benzie’s wit and charm. Personally this reviewer can’t wait to revisit Cabot Cove. Never mind 'whodunnit', more like 'yougottadoit!" 4 stars **** - The Reviews Hub “A lighthearted two hours of entertainment that both die-hard devotees and Cabot Cove novices will enjoy ... A solve-along, sing-along hit." 4 stars **** - Broadway Baby “Benzie's passion and knowledge shines through." 4 stars **** - West End Best Friend "Tim Benzie is the perfect host ... Benzie’s insights help keep the audience engaged with the show and not just passively watching the episode unfold.” 4 stars **** - The Nerd Party “It didn’t take long for Benzie to have the audience in stitches and he had the whole crowd in the palm of his hand the entire evening.” - Bristol 24/7 “A unique and thoroughly enjoyable theatre experience” - Blue Curtains Brisbane *** For links to the full reviews visit www.solvealongamurdershewrote.com

title: Akira
description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988 - World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo...As the leader of a group of young robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy - the product of human experimentation and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness..

title: A Confucian Confusion
description: Art versus commerce, friendship versus status, independence versus conformity—values clash and collide in Edward Yang's study of an increasingly Westernized country heading into the twenty-first century without moral guideposts. Moving from breakout hit A Brighter Summer Day's investigation of the past to a critical survey of the present, A Confucian Confusion charts the tangled web of emotional and professional manipulations among a group of young urbanites. At its center is Molly (Ni Shu-chun), director of a floundering public-relations firm. Alienated by the childish fiancé (Bosen Wang) who bankrolls her enterprise—and frustrated by the demands of an assistant, Qiqi (Chen Shiang-chyi), and her own fiancé, Ming (Wang Wei-ming)—Molly lashes out at everyone in her path and threatens to dismantle the company altogether. Meanwhile (amid several other subplots), Molly's talk-show-host sister (Chen Li-mei) attempts to dissuade her separated husband from continuing to write a dark novel about the return of Confucius to a jaded modern society. Injecting comedic elements into his patented brand of earnest soul-searching, Yang finds humor as well as pathos in the desperate behavior of a lost and lonely generation.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
description: Stanley Kubrick's daring last film is many things. It is a compelling psychosexual journey. A haunting dreamscape. A riveting tale of suspense. A major milestone in the careers of stars Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman. And "a worthy final chapter to a great director's career" (Roger Ebert). Cruise plays Dr William Hartford, who plunges into an erotic foray that threatens his marriage - and may even ensnare him in a lurid murder mystery - after his wife's (Kidman) admission of sexual longings. As the story sweeps from doubt and fear to self-discovery and reconciliation, Kubrick orchestrates it with masterful flourishes. Graceful tracking shots, controlled pacing, rich colours, startling images: bravura traits that make Kubrick a filmmaker for the ages are here to keep everyone's eyes wide shut.

title: Amelie - 25th Anniversary
description: 23-year-old Amélie is lonely. After an isolating childhood, she moves to Paris and becomes a waitress at the Café des Deux Moulins, a bar restaurant filled with a colourful cast of diners and employees. One night, Amélie happens across a box of treasures hidden in her apartment, left by a little boy in the Fifties, that changes the course of her life. Henceforth, she dedicates herself to giving back to her community, tracking down the owner of these keepsakes, consoling a widowed neighbour and befriending a reclusive artist. When completing these good deeds, she crosses paths with Nino, a photobooth collagist who shares her oddball sensibilities. She quickly falls in love with him.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. Costumes aren't mandatory, but 'Tis the season, and we love seeing you dressed up in your favourite Christmas Jumpers! All this, and a few more surprises up our sleeves, makes this one of the must-see events this Christmas! If you're wanting to Sing Along with The Muppet Christmas Carol, simply book for the performances marked SING ALONG [it's next to the start time]. All other screenings will be regular performances, and nothing will be written next to the start time.

title: Unzipped
description: Designer Isaac Mizrahi proved a force of nature on the road to his legendary fall 1994 collection, a career-defining triumph that was documented with an effervescent intimacy by Douglas Keeve, Mizrahi’s then-partner. Both a time capsule of the buoyant, raucous 1990s, when pop culture and high art became interchangeable, and a vérité-style, in-the-trenches report on the daily agonies and ecstasies of the creative process, this seminal artistic portrait—sumptuously shot by Ellen Kuras and Robert Leacock—transcends glitz and glamour to offer an extraordinary view of the charisma and force of will inherent to genius, as well as its personal costs. Digitally restored by the Sundance Institute and UCLA Film & Television Archive. Funding provided by Isaac Mizrahi Entertainment. Laboratory services by Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. and Deluxe Media Audio Services.

title: Love Actually
description: Nine intertwined stories examine the complexities of the one emotion that connects us all: love. Among the characters explored are David (Hugh Grant), the handsome newly elected British prime minister who falls for a young junior staffer (Martine McCutcheon), Sarah (Laura Linney), a graphic designer whose devotion to her mentally ill brother complicates her love life, and Harry (Alan Rickman), a married man tempted by his attractive new secretary.

title: Sing-A-Long-A Rocky Horror Picture Show
description: The Campest Cult Classic of all time gets the Singalonga treatment it’s been SCREAMING for! Featuring the film, starring Tim Curry, Susan Sarandon, Meatloaf and Richard O’Brien, it’s the most outrageous, riotous, kitsch, wonderful romp ever. If you’ve done The Time Warp before, you’ll never have done it quite like this! The evening begins with your host leading a vocal warm-up before they show you how to use your free interactive props bag. Fancy dress is not obligatory but highly recommended! Please Note : The 15 rating we have placed upon this screening is due to the Adult content of the hosted pre-show which may not be suitable for those under 15. Please Note : This is a screening of the movie not a live stage show. Also this screening may contain sudden loud noises and flashing lights. For Sing-a-long-a Grease, Rocky Horror, Dirty Dancing and The Greatest Showman at the Prince Charles Cinema, London we can offer a discount for groups of 10+. Simply get in touch with us via email at boxofficemanager@princecharlescinema.com before buying so we can arrange!

title: Jurassic Park
description: In Steven Spielberg's massive blockbuster, paleontologists Alan Grant (Sam Neill) and Ellie Sattler (Laura Dern) and mathematician Ian Malcolm (Jeff Goldblum) are among a select group chosen to tour an island theme park populated by dinosaurs created from prehistoric DNA. While the park's mastermind, billionaire John Hammond (Richard Attenborough), assures everyone that the facility is safe, they find out otherwise when various ferocious predators break free and go on the hunt.

title: Cars
description: Lightning McQueen, a hotshot rookie race car driven to succeed, discovers that life is about the journey, not the finish line, when he finds himself unexpectedly detoured in the sleepy Route 66 town of Radiator Springs. On route across the country to the big Piston Cup Championship in California to compete against two seasoned pros, McQueen gets to know the town's offbeat characters.

title: Gremlins
description: Accessible screening On the last Saturday of every month, the museum's Family Matinee is an accessible screening where we offer open captioning, keep the theater dimly lit, and maintain a lower volume for viewers who are neurodiverse. When Billy receives a mysterious creature called a mogwai, affectionately named Gizmo, from his father for Christmas, he must follow three rules: keep it away from sunlight, don’t get it wet, and above all else, never feed it after midnight. When the creature accidentally gets wet and more mogwai spawn with much more devious intentions than the docile Gizmo, mayhem erupts. With the town’s adults out of their depth, it is up to Billy and Gizmo to defeat these menacing creatures. The violence in the PG-rated Gremlins was one of the reasons the Motion Picture Association later created the PG-13 rating; the film is often cited as kick-starting a trend of small creature features in the 1980s. Please note: This film contains discussions about Santa Claus that might not be appropriate for younger viewers.
director: Joe Dante PRODUCED BY: Michael Finnell

title: The Odyssey
description: Odysseus, the legendary King of Ithaca, embarks on a long and perilous journey home following the Trojan War. Throughout his voyage, he is forced to confront the whims of gods, mythological monsters, and trials that stretch both his cunning and his humanity to the breaking point.

title: The Worst Person in the World
description: On the verge of turning thirty, Julie is faced with a series of choices that force her to pursue new perspectives on her life in contemporary Oslo. Over the course of four years, she navigates love affairs and existential uncertainty as she starts deciding who she wants to become.

title: Moulin Rouge!
description: A young Englishman in the Paris of 1899, becomes infatuated with Satine, a singer at the Moulin Rouge. However, she has been promised by the manager to a Duke in return for funding his next production. As the young lovers meet in secret, Satine's wedding day draws closer but she hides a fatal secret from both Christian and the Duke.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
description: 'Tis the season for love, laughter, and one of the most cherished stories of all time! Join Kermit the Frog, Miss Piggy, and all the hilarious Muppets in this merry, magical version of Charles Dickens' classic tale. Academy Award® winner Michael Caine (Best Supporting Actor) gives a performance that's anything but "bah, humbug!" as greedy, penny-pinching Ebenezer Scrooge. One fateful Christmas Eve, Scrooge is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future. Together with kind, humble Bob Cratchit (Kermit the Frog) and his family, the Spirits open Scrooge's eyes -- and his heart -- to the true meaning of Christmas. Filled with original music and dazzling special effects, THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL will become a holiday tradition your family will treasure all the days of the year. Featuring the film’s famous long-lost song ‘When Love is Gone’! ------ As always you can expect SING ALONG performances of this new version of THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL this Christmas - and now we don't need to pretend that we weren't going to just play the lost scene regardless! Performances will feature a Hosted Pre-Show with our very own Father Christmas, where you will be prepped on what to do throughout the film. Costumes aren't mandatory, but 'Tis the season, and we love seeing you dressed up in your favourite Christmas Jumpers! All this, and a few more surprises up our sleeves, makes this one of the must-see events this Christmas! If you're wanting to Sing Along with The Muppet Christmas Carol, simply book for the performances marked SING ALONG [it's next to the start time]. All other screenings will be regular performances, and nothing will be written next to the start time.

title: Sonic Cinema: Daïchi Saïto
description: Sonic Cinema and the Japan Foundation present the films of Montreal-based artist Daïchi Saïto, projected from his personal 35mm prints. A rare encounter with a singular voice in artisanal film practice, this programme highlights Saïto’s skill in bridging metaphysical concepts with sensory experience. Originally from Japan, Daïchi Saïto makes films of intense beauty and power, grounded in abstract approaches to landscape, rhythm, and perception. Produced through expressive use of optical manipulation and painstaking frame-by-frame photochemical treatments, the films in this programme carry a tactile and elemental intensity, teasing out the sensual poetry of the natural world and human subjectivity. Drawing on Saïto's studies in philosophy, literature, and the languages of Hindi and Sanskrit, as much as the language of cinema, these are films built on a poetic dialogue of sound and image. Guided by the expressive improvised soundtracks of Malcolm Goldstein and Jason Sharp, we'll traverse exterior and interior landscapes, from the darkened primordial deserts of Saïto's most recent film earthearthearth (2021), through the stained glass forest of Trees of Syntax , Leaves of Axis (2009), before the torrent of memories and cool mountain vistas carries us away in Engram of Returning (2015). Daïchi will join us in person for a Q&A with series curator Oliver Dickens following the screening. Programme earthearthearth , Canada 2021, 30 min., 35mm Trees of Syntax, Leaves of Axis , Canada 2009, 10 min., 35mm Engram of Returning , Canada, Japan 2015, 18’30 min., 35mm Programmed by Oliver Dickens for Sonic Cinema, presented in partnership with the Japan Foundation.

title: The Holiday
description: Dumped and depressed, English rose Iris agrees to swap homes with similarly unlucky in love Californian Amanda for a much-needed break. Iris finds herself in a palatial Hollywood mansion while Amanda navigates the lanes of a picture-perfect English village. Soon enough, both lovelorn ladies bump into local lads perfect for a romantic pick-me-up.

title: Europe ’51
description: According to Roberto Rossellini, Europe ’51 is a retelling of his film The Flowers of St. Francis ( Francesco, giullare di Dio , 1950) , from a female perspective. Ingrid Bergman portrays a wealthy American socialite living in Rome, moving through grief and guilt over the death of her son. As she sets out on a journey of newfound selflessness, devoting her time and money to the less fortunate, her husband and the community question her sanity. With Rossellini often pushing his actors to improvise dialogue, Ingrid would receive her lines only minutes before rolling. She would often reference this time as a difficult challenge. Working with first-time actors, with no written dialogue, and all during a Roman heat wave while Ingrid was pregnant with twins Isabella and Isotta, the director and actress proved their grit as a filmmaking duo.
director: Roberto Rossellini PRODUCED BY: Roberto Rossellini

title: Stop Making Sense
description: Stop Making Sense stars core band members David Byrne, Tina Weymouth, Chris Frantz, and Jerry Harrison along with Bernie Worrell, Alex Weir, Steve Scales, Lynn Mabry and Edna Holt. The live performance was shot over the course of three nights at Hollywood's Pantages Theater in December of 1983 and features Talking Heads' most memorable songs.

title: In The Mood For Love
description: In 1962 Hong Kong, neighbors Su Li-zhen (Mrs. Chan) and Chow Mo-wan (Mr. Chow) discover their spouses are having an affair. As they spend time together, they develop feelings for each other, but their relationship remains chaste and unspoken, reflecting societal constraints and their own moral compass.

title: The Royal Tenenbaums
description: Royal Tenenbaum and his wife Etheline had three children and then they separated. All three children are extraordinary --- all geniuses. Virtually all memory of the brilliance of the young Tenenbaums was subsequently erased by two decades of betrayal, failure, and disaster. Most of this was generally considered to be their father's fault. "The Royal Tenenbaums" is the story of the family's sudden, unexpected reunion one recent winter.

Wong Kar Wai’s loose sequel to In the Mood for Love combines that film’s languorous air of romantic longing with a dizzying time-hopping structure and avant-sci-fi twist. Tony Leung Chiu Wai reprises his role as writer Chow Mo-Wan, whose numerous failed relationships with women who drift in and out of his life (and the one who goes in and out of room 2046, down the hall from his apartment) inspire the delirious futuristic love story he pens. 2046’s dazzling fantasy sequences give Wong and two of his key collaborators—cinematographer Christopher Doyle and editor/costume designer/production designer William Chang Suk Ping—license to let their imaginations run wild, propelling the sumptuous visuals and operatic emotions skyward toward the sublime.

title: Once Upon a Time...in Hollywood
description: Quentin Tarantino’s alternate history of the late-’60s film scene focuses on the intertwining lives of three figures: fading TV Western star Rick Dalton (Best Actor nominee Leonardo DiCaprio), his stunt double and best friend Cliff Booth (Supporting Actor winner Brad Pitt) and the real-life starlet Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie), whose life is destined to cross paths with Charles Manson and his followers. With its massive, stellar cast (including Margaret Qualley, Timothy Olyphant, Austin Butler, Dakota Fanning, Bruce Dern, Damian Lewis, and Al Pacino) and evocative, needle-drop score, Once Upon a Time elegantly evokes a lost era of Hollywood. Nominated for 10 Oscars including Best Picture, it won for production designer Barbara Ling and set decorator Nancy Haigh, who incorporate real-life locations such as the Musso & Frank Grill and the Playboy Mansion while creating believable living spaces for the protagonists.
